Pulls new commits from the connected GitHub repository into the app.

Call this after someone pushes to the repository, or before you read the app's code, so Base44 is working from the latest version. It applies only what is new since the last pull, and does nothing when the app is already up to date.

A failed pull is reported in the response body rather than as an error, so read `synced` and `error`. Base44 doesn't record the commits it couldn't apply, so the next pull picks them up again rather than skipping past them. A pull that fails late can already have added a chat message or a checkpoint, and retrying repeats those.

post.summary: Turn automatic GitHub sync on or off
post.description:
<Info>This API is in beta. Endpoints, fields, and behavior may still change, so avoid depending on it in production.</Info>

Turns automatic sync between the app and its connected GitHub repository on or off.

Automatic sync brings in commits pushed to the repository from outside Base44. While it's on, the Base44 editor pulls them in as soon as GitHub reports them, as long as someone has the app open in it. While it's off, Base44 ignores those reports, so new commits come in only when someone opens the app in the editor or you call [Pull changes from GitHub](/api-reference/pull-changes-from-github). The setting covers the app's main line and its [branches](/developers/references/app-management/get-started/concepts#branches) alike.

The setting doesn't affect the other direction. Base44 pushes every saved version to the repository whether automatic sync is on or off, and [Push changes to GitHub](/api-reference/push-changes-to-github) works either way.

When the repository receives more than 20 pushes within a minute, counting Base44's own, Base44 pauses automatic sync for an hour. Pushes during the pause are ignored, even if you turn automatic sync on, and turning it on doesn't end the pause early. After the hour, the next push ends the pause. Base44 then turns automatic sync back on only if the pause is what turned automatic sync off.

[Reconnect a GitHub repository](/api-reference/reconnect-a-github-repository) also turns automatic sync back on.

post.description:
<Info>This API is in beta. Endpoints, fields, and behavior may still change, so avoid depending on it in production.</Info>

Sends a message to a Superagent and waits for its reply.

The request stays open while the agent works, which includes any tools it runs, and returns the agent's final reply. A reply that needs many tool calls can take minutes, so set a generous client timeout. The agent's turn uses credits from the agent's workspace.

Send `content`, and optionally `file_urls`, in the body. Use a `conversation_id` from [Create Superagent conversation](/api-reference/create-superagent-conversation) or [List Superagent conversations](/api-reference/list-superagent-conversations).

Each request starts its own reply. Sending another message before the agent answers starts a second reply alongside the first, and retrying a request that timed out runs the turn again and uses credits again. Wait for the reply before you send the next message.

To hear about messages without waiting on this request, subscribe to `message.created` and `message.completed` with [Create Superagent webhook](/api-reference/create-superagent-webhook).

This endpoint is limited to 20 requests per minute.

<Note>This endpoint accepts a personal API key or personal access token belonging to a user with access to the agent. Workspace API keys are not accepted.</Note>

<Warning>The response includes fields beyond the ones documented here. Don't rely on undocumented response fields, as they can change at any time. Send only the fields documented here. Other request fields are not supported and their behavior can change.</Warning>

source.description: Which engine wrote it. The value is `google` for Google's own asset generation and `inhouse` for the Base44 model that covers languages Google does not generate for, and that stands in when Google's call fails.

asset_group_count.title: Asset Group Count
asset_group_count.description: How many of the campaign's asset groups the asset was linked to. The asset goes on every asset group the campaign has, so this is that count.

resource_name.title: Resource Name
resource_name.description: Google Ads resource name of the asset that now holds this creative. Empty when Google's response carried no resource name, which does not mean the attach failed.

AcceptAssetResult.title: AcceptAssetResult
AcceptAssetResult.description: The outcome of attaching a generated asset to a campaign.

status.title: Status
status.description: Outcome of the request. A status of `accepted` means the acceptance was recorded, while `not_recorded` means it was not written because the account is in a blocked or terminal state, which is a failure to act on rather than a no-op.

AcceptTermsResponse.title: AcceptTermsResponse
AcceptTermsResponse.description: Outcome of accepting the Google Ads terms.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app.

app_type.title: App Type
app_type.description: Type of the app, for example `user_app` or `user_agent`, or `null` when it isn't set.

new_owner_id.title: New Owner Id
new_owner_id.description: ID of the Base44 user who owns the app now.

target_workspace_id.title: Target Workspace Id
target_workspace_id.description: ID of the workspace the app is in.

AcceptTransferResponse.title: AcceptTransferResponse
AcceptTransferResponse.description: The app after its ownership changed.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email of the person.

full_name.title: Full Name
full_name.description: Name of the person, or `null` when they didn't give one.

role.title: Role
role.description: App role the person gets when they join.

status.title: Status
status.description: `pending` when the person asked for access and is waiting for your review, `approved` when they're invited or approved but haven't joined yet, or `completed` once they've joined.

requested_at.title: Requested At
requested_at.description: When the request or invitation was made, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

data.title: Data
data.description: Custom `User` fields stored on the invitation, limited by the `User` entity's field-level read rules.

AccessRequestSummary.title: AccessRequestSummary
AccessRequestSummary.description: Doc-only: the handler returns plain dicts with exactly these keys.

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable ID for the suggestion. Pass it as `insight_id` to [Dismiss insight](/api-reference/dismiss-google-ads-insight) to stop it coming back.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: How urgent the suggestion is: `high`, `medium`, or `low`.

title.title: Title
title.description: One-line summary of the suggestion.
title.example: Increase budget for Spring sale - Search

description.title: Description
description.description: The suggestion in full, written for an app owner to read as-is.
description.example: This campaign is consistently spending its full daily budget. Raising it could capture more clicks and conversions.

action.title: Action
action.description: What resolving the suggestion involves: `edit_budget`, `edit_sitelinks`, `improve_assets`, or `open_campaign`. `null` when Base44 could not resolve a campaign to act on.

action_payload.title: Action Payload
action_payload.description: The values the suggestion proposes. `campaign_ids` names the campaigns it applies to, `field` and `value` carry a proposed budget in micros where there is one.

source.title: Source
source.description: `google` when the suggestion is Google Ads' own recommendation rather than Base44's. Absent on Base44's own suggestions.

recommendation_type.title: Recommendation Type
recommendation_type.description: Present with `source`. `CAMPAIGN_BUDGET` for a Google budget recommendation, `AD_STRENGTH_DROP` for an ad-strength one.

AccountInsight.title: AccountInsight
AccountInsight.description: One suggestion in the account's insight feed.

app_ids.title: App Ids
app_ids.description: IDs of the apps to put in the folder, up to 500.

linked_count.title: Linked Count
linked_count.description: Number of apps added to the folder.

skipped_count.title: Skipped Count
skipped_count.description: Number of IDs skipped because the app was already in the folder or was listed twice.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app.

agent_name.title: Agent Name
agent_name.description: Name of the agent the memory belongs to.

content.title: Content
content.description: What the agent remembered, in its own words.
content.example: Prefers delivery updates by email rather than SMS.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: `global` for a memory the agent uses with every user, or `user` for one it uses only with the user in `user_id`.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: ID of the app user a `user` memory belongs to, or `null` for a `global` memory.

conversation_id.title: Conversation Id
conversation_id.description: ID of the conversation the agent saved the memory in, or `null` if it wasn't saved in one.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the memory was saved, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: When the memory was last changed, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

title.title: Title
title.description: Short name for the suggested agent, up to 40 characters.

description.title: Description
description.description: One sentence on what the agent does for the app's users, up to 110 characters.
description.example: Tells customers where their order is and when it should arrive.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: Message you can send to the app's AI chat to have it build the agent, up to 300 characters.
prompt.example: Create an agent that answers customers' questions about their Order status and delivery date.

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.description: Up to 3 suggested agents. The list is empty if none could be generated.

usage_by_agent.title: Usage By Agent
usage_by_agent.description: Integration credits each agent used in the workspace's current billing period, keyed by agent name. An agent that hasn't used any is left out.

AgentUsageResponse.title: AgentUsageResponse
AgentUsageResponse.description: Integration credits the app's agents used in the current billing period.

group.title: Group
group.description: Value of the grouped field, or `null` when the events in this group have no value for it.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: The single metric this entry reports, keyed by the `name` you gave it.

AggregationGroup.title: AggregationGroup
AggregationGroup.description: A single group with its field value and computed metrics.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name to report this metric under. It becomes a key in `metrics` and `totals` in the response.

function.title: Function
function.description: How to aggregate the field. A `count` counts events, `count_unique` counts distinct values, and the rest compute over the field's numeric values.

field.title: Field
field.description: Field to aggregate. Required for every function except `count`. Top-level fields are `user_id`, `session_id`, `event_id`, `event_name`, and `page_url`. Prefix a key with `metadata.` for the device information Base44 captures itself: `metadata.device_type`, `metadata.os`, and `metadata.country`. Any other name reads as an event property, so `amount` and `properties.amount` mean the same thing.

AggregationMetric.title: AggregationMetric
AggregationMetric.description: A single aggregation metric to compute.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Time the event occurred, as reported by the app, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: ID of the app user who triggered the event, or `null` if it was not attributed to one.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Session the event belongs to, or `null` if the app sent none.

page_url.title: Page Url
page_url.description: URL of the page the event happened on, or `null` if the app sent none.

properties.title: Properties
properties.description: The custom properties the app sent with this event, or `{}` if it sent none. Keys and value types are whatever the app tracks.

metadata.description: Device information Base44 captured when it received the event.

device_type.title: Device Type
device_type.description: Device the event came from, derived from the request's user agent, or `null` when the app sent no user agent.

os.title: Os
os.description: Operating system the event came from, or `null` when it could not be derived.

country.title: Country
country.description: Two-letter country code the event came from. The value is `null` when the request reached Base44 without a country header, `XX` when the country is unknown, and `T1` for traffic over Tor.

total.title: Total
total.description: Number of events matching the query, across all pages.

events.title: Events
events.description: The requested page of events, newest first.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Whether more events match beyond this page.

next_offset.title: Next Offset
next_offset.description: Offset to pass as `offset` to get the next page, or `null` when `has_more` is `false`.

AnalyticsEventPage.title: AnalyticsEventPage
AnalyticsEventPage.description: One page of analytics events matching a query.

explanation.title: Explanation
explanation.description: Why the run failed, in plain language. Empty when the model could not be reached.
explanation.example: The email step failed because the recipient address was missing from the trigger payload.

generated_at.title: Generated At
generated_at.description: When the explanation was produced, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. Empty when none was produced.

has_dependent_templates.title: Has Dependent Templates
has_dependent_templates.description: Whether any template listings were made from the app.

catalog_items.title: Catalog Items
catalog_items.description: Template listings made from the app that aren't archived.

has_connected_domains.title: Has Connected Domains
has_connected_domains.description: Whether any custom domains are connected to the app.

connected_domains.title: Connected Domains
connected_domains.description: Custom domains connected to the app, including ones that are turned off. Deleting the app releases them.

app_users_count.title: App Users Count
app_users_count.description: Number of users of the app.

active_google_ads_campaigns.title: Active Google Ads Campaigns
active_google_ads_campaigns.description: Names of the app's Google Ads campaigns that are still serving. [Delete app](/api-reference/delete-app) refuses while this isn't empty.

AppDeleteImpact.title: AppDeleteImpact
AppDeleteImpact.description:
Doc-only: the handler returns a plain dict. ``google_ads_url`` stays
unpublished: it's a builder page path, not an API link.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: What the app's own setting says. `inherit` means the app sets no policy and follows its workspace, `block_all` means no site can frame it, and `allowlist` means only `origins` can.

origins.title: Origins
origins.description: Sites allowed to frame the app when `mode` is `allowlist`, or `null` for the other modes.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the folder.

parent_folder_id.title: Parent Folder Id
parent_folder_id.description: ID of the folder this one sits in, or `null` for a top-level folder.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: `workspace` for a folder every member of the workspace sees, or `personal` for one only you see.

position.title: Position
position.description: Sort key among folders. Lower values come first.

color.title: Color
color.description: Color set on the folder, or `null` when none is set.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: Icon name set on the folder, or `null` when none is set.

app_type.title: App Type
app_type.description: `user_app` for a folder of builder apps, or `user_agent` for a folder of agents. Builder app folders created before agent folders existed leave it out.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: Time the folder was created, in UTC, as an ISO 8601 timestamp without a time zone offset.

favorite_folder_ids.title: Favorite Folder Ids
favorite_folder_ids.description: IDs of the folders in this response that you starred in the Base44 dashboard.

enable_username_password.title: Enable Username Password
enable_username_password.description: Whether people can sign in to the app with an email and password.

enable_google_login.title: Enable Google Login
enable_google_login.description: Whether people can sign in to the app with a Google account.

enable_microsoft_login.title: Enable Microsoft Login
enable_microsoft_login.description: Whether people can sign in to the app with a Microsoft account.

enable_facebook_login.title: Enable Facebook Login
enable_facebook_login.description: Whether people can sign in to the app with a Facebook account.

enable_apple_login.title: Enable Apple Login
enable_apple_login.description: Whether people can sign in to the app with an Apple account.

logo_url.title: Logo Url
logo_url.description: URL of the app's logo, as you sent it.

AppLogo.title: AppLogo
AppLogo.description: Doc-only: the handler returns the whole app document.

auth.title: Auth
auth.description: How clients authenticate. Either `"oauth"`, where clients sign in, or `"none"`, where anyone can call the entity read tools without signing in. Leave it out to keep the current mode.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: The whole `tools` object, which replaces the stored one. `excluded_agents` lists agents to hold back. `entity_overrides` maps an entity name to the `operations` to serve, where an empty list holds the entity back. `functions` lists the custom tools, and one with `disabled` set to `true` is held back. Leave it out to keep the current tools.

AppMcpConfigPatch.title: AppMcpConfigPatch
AppMcpConfigPatch.description: The MCP config keys to change.

config.title: Config
config.description: The editable config, or `null` when the app has no MCP server. It has `auth`, `login_path`, `consent_path`, and the `tools` object that [Update MCP config](/api-reference/update-mcp-config) replaces.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Every tool the config can serve, and whether it does.

pending_removal.title: Pending Removal
pending_removal.description: Tools the live server still serves that the config no longer produces. The next publish removes them.

AppMcpConfigResponse.title: AppMcpConfigResponse
AppMcpConfigResponse.description: The app's editable MCP config and the tools it resolves to.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name AI clients call the tool by.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Where the tool comes from. Either `"entity"`, `"agent"`, or `"function"` for a custom tool.

title.title: Title
title.description: Display title of the tool, or `null` when it has none.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the tool does, as AI clients see it.
description.example: Find Invoice records by ID or filter.

read_only_hint.title: Read Only Hint
read_only_hint.description: Whether the tool is marked as only reading data.

AppMcpLiveToolRow.title: AppMcpLiveToolRow
AppMcpLiveToolRow.description: A tool only the live server still has.

active.title: Active
active.description: Whether AI clients can use the server right now. It's `false` until the app is published, while it's unpublished or blocked, when the workspace has turned MCP off or requires `oauth` from a `none` server, and when a `none` server's app requires visitors to log in.

published.title: Published
published.description: Whether a publish has put an MCP server live for the app.

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: URL AI clients connect to, or `null` when the app has no address yet.

auth.title: Auth
auth.description: How clients authenticate with the live server, or `null` when none is published. Either `"oauth"`, where clients sign in, or `"none"`, where anyone can call the public tools.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Tools the live server serves. A `none` server lists only its public tools.

effective_public_settings.title: Effective Public Settings
effective_public_settings.description: Who can open the app after its next publish, once workspace SSO rules apply. A `none` server only works while this is `public_without_login`.

workspace_policy.title: Workspace Policy
workspace_policy.description: The workspace's rule for app MCP servers. Either `"allow"`, `"oauth_only"`, which stops `none` servers, or `"disabled"`, which stops every server in the workspace.

key.title: Key
key.description: Stable ID of the row. Two rows can share a `name`, but never a `key`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name AI clients call the tool by.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Where the tool comes from. Either `"entity"`, `"agent"`, or `"function"` for a custom tool.

source.title: Source
source.description: Entity, agent, or custom tool in the config that this row belongs to.

operation.title: Operation
operation.description: Entity operation the tool performs, or `null` for agent and custom tools. One of `read`, `create`, `update`, or `delete`.

handler.title: Handler
handler.description: Backend function a custom tool runs, or the server route path it calls (starting with `/`), or `null` for other tools.

title.title: Title
title.description: Display title of the tool, or `null` when it has none.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the tool does, as AI clients see it.
description.example: Find Task records by ID or filter.

read_only_hint.title: Read Only Hint
read_only_hint.description: Whether the tool is marked as only reading data.

exposed.title: Exposed
exposed.description: Whether the config serves the tool.

published.title: Published
published.description: Whether the live server already matches `exposed`. It's `false` while a change waits for a publish.

AppMcpToolRow.title: AppMcpToolRow
AppMcpToolRow.description: A tool the config serves or holds back.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name AI clients call the tool by.

title.title: Title
title.description: Display title of the tool, or `null` when it has none.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the tool does, as AI clients see it.
description.example: Find Task records by ID or filter.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Where the tool comes from. Either `"entity"`, `"agent"`, or `"function"` for a custom tool backed by a backend function.

handler.title: Handler
handler.description: Backend function a custom tool runs, or the server route path it calls (starting with `/`), or `null` for entity and agent tools.

read_only_hint.title: Read Only Hint
read_only_hint.description: Whether the tool is marked as only reading data.

public.title: Public
public.description: Whether the tool can be called without signing in when the server's `auth` is `none`. Only entity read tools can. On an `oauth` server every tool still needs a signed-in client.

AppMcpToolSummary.title: AppMcpToolSummary
AppMcpToolSummary.description: A tool the live MCP server serves.

info.title: Info
info.description: Title and description of the app's API. The title is the app's name followed by `API`.

servers.title: Servers
servers.description: The app's API address, built from its slug.

paths.title: Paths
paths.description: One entry per endpoint of the app's entities, backend functions, and agents.

components.title: Components
components.description: A schema for each entity, and the `api_key` header the app's API authenticates with.

AppOpenApiSpec.title: AppOpenApiSpec
AppOpenApiSpec.description: An OpenAPI 3.0.3 document describing the app's own API.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the app's SSO provider, or an empty string when none is set. The builder uses `google`, `microsoft`, `github`, or `okta` for those providers. Any other name is a custom OpenID Connect or OAuth provider.

client_id.title: Client Id
client_id.description: OAuth client ID from the identity provider, or an empty string when none is stored.

client_secret.title: Client Secret
client_secret.description: Reads `XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX` when a client secret is stored, and an empty string when none is. The secret itself is never returned.

discovery_url.title: Discovery Url
discovery_url.description: OpenID Connect discovery URL, or an empty string when none is stored or the provider doesn't use one.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Scopes requested at sign-in, separated by spaces. Reads `openid email profile` when none is stored or the provider doesn't use one.

auth_endpoint.title: Auth Endpoint
auth_endpoint.description: Authorization endpoint for a provider without a discovery URL, or an empty string when none is stored or the provider doesn't use one.

token_endpoint.title: Token Endpoint
token_endpoint.description: Token endpoint for a provider without a discovery URL, or an empty string when none is stored or the provider doesn't use one.

userinfo_endpoint.title: Userinfo Endpoint
userinfo_endpoint.description: User info endpoint for a provider without a discovery URL, or an empty string when none is stored or the provider doesn't use one.

jwks_uri.title: Jwks Uri
jwks_uri.description: URL of the provider's signing keys, for a custom provider. The value is an empty string when none is stored or the provider doesn't use one.

tenant_id.title: Tenant Id
tenant_id.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID, or an empty string when none is stored or the provider isn't `microsoft`.

okta_domain.title: Okta Domain
okta_domain.description: Okta domain, or an empty string when none is stored or the provider isn't `okta`.

settings.description: The provider and its non-secret settings.

AppSSOSettingsResponse.title: AppSSOSettingsResponse
AppSSOSettingsResponse.description: The app's own SSO provider settings, with the client secret masked.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the SSO provider. Use `google`, `microsoft`, `github`, or `okta` for those providers, or a name of your choice for any other OpenID Connect or OAuth provider. Required unless the app already has a provider.

client_id.title: Client Id
client_id.description: OAuth client ID from the identity provider.

client_secret.title: Client Secret
client_secret.description: OAuth client secret from the identity provider. Leave it out to keep the stored one.

discovery_url.title: Discovery Url
discovery_url.description: OpenID Connect discovery URL. It must be an absolute `http` or `https` URL on a public address.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Scopes to request at sign-in, separated by spaces.

auth_endpoint.title: Auth Endpoint
auth_endpoint.description: Authorization endpoint, for a provider without a discovery URL.

token_endpoint.title: Token Endpoint
token_endpoint.description: Token endpoint, for a provider without a discovery URL.

userinfo_endpoint.title: Userinfo Endpoint
userinfo_endpoint.description: User info endpoint, for a provider without a discovery URL.

jwks_uri.title: Jwks Uri
jwks_uri.description: URL of the provider's signing keys, for a custom provider.

tenant_id.title: Tenant Id
tenant_id.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID, for the `microsoft` provider.

AppSSOUpdateRequest.title: AppSSOUpdateRequest
AppSSOUpdateRequest.description: The app's SSO provider and the settings to change, sent together.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `success`.

auth_config.title: Auth Config
auth_config.description: The app's sign-in settings as saved, with `sso_provider_name` set to the provider and `enable_sso_login` set to `true`.

warning.title: Warning
warning.description: Why the discovery URL couldn't be checked, present only when that happened. The settings are saved, but SSO sign-in fails while the problem lasts.
warning.example: The Discovery URL could not be verified because it did not respond in time. SSO login will fail while that persists.

AppSSOUpdateResponse.title: AppSSOUpdateResponse
AppSSOUpdateResponse.description: The result of saving the app's SSO provider settings.

social_image_url.title: Social Image Url
social_image_url.description: URL of the image shown when someone shares the app's link, or `null` when you removed it.

AppSocialImage.title: AppSocialImage
AppSocialImage.description: Doc-only: the handler returns the whole app document.

state.title: State
state.description: Where the app is in its build lifecycle. Ready means idle with no build in progress, processing means the app is being generated or modified, and error means the last build failed. This tracks building, not publishing.

details.title: Details
details.description: Human readable note about the current state, such as what is being processed or why it failed, or `null` when there is nothing to report.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: ID of the request that last changed the status, or `null` if the status has never changed. Useful when reporting an issue.

last_updated_date.title: Last Updated Date
last_updated_date.description: Time the status was last updated, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

error_source.title: Error Source
error_source.description: Where the failure originated when `state` is `error`, or `null` otherwise. A value of `paywall` means the work was blocked because the app's workspace has no credits left.

paywall_context.description: Present when the operation was blocked by a plan limit, describing what was evaluated, or `null` otherwise.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the app.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: URL slug for the app, auto generated from the name and app ID or set to a custom value, or `null` if the app has no slug yet. The published URL is built from it.

user_description.title: User Description
user_description.description: Description of the app, or `null` if none was set. An app created without a `name` gets a generated description once a build turn changes it.
user_description.example: A CRM to track leads and deals

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: Email of the user who created the app.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: Time the app was created, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: Time the app document was last written, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

status.description: The app's current build status. Poll while a build is in progress to watch it finish. This tracks building, not publishing.

last_deployed_at.title: Last Deployed At
last_deployed_at.description: Time the app was last published, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or `null` if it has never been published.

screenshot_url.title: Screenshot Url
screenshot_url.description: URL of a screenshot of the published app. Captured shortly after each publish, so it can briefly lag or be `null` right after publishing.

preview_screenshot_url.title: Preview Screenshot Url
preview_screenshot_url.description: URL of a preview screenshot taken before publishing, distinct from `screenshot_url`, or `null` if none has been captured.

main_branch_protected.title: Main Branch Protected
main_branch_protected.description: Whether the app's main branch is protected, so changes to main must go through a branch that's merged back. Change it with [Set main branch protection](/api-reference/set-main-branch-protection).

organization_id.title: Organization Id
organization_id.description: ID of the workspace the app belongs to.

owner_id.title: Owner Id
owner_id.description: ID of the user who owns the app. It starts as the creator and changes when ownership is transferred.

app_type.title: App Type
app_type.description: Kind of app, set when it's created. One of `user_app` (a web app), `user_agent` (an AI agent), `mobile_app` (a native mobile app), `user_game` (a game), `slide` (a presentation), or `imported_app` (an app imported from an existing code repository). List apps returns it as stored, so an older agent app can report `agent` instead of `user_agent`, and some older apps don't include it. Get app always returns one of the values above.

public_settings.title: Public Settings
public_settings.description: Who can open the published app. Each value is described under [Update app](/api-reference/update-app), which also changes it.

auth_config.description: Which login methods the app's login page offers. If the workspace enforces SSO for apps, the login page offers only SSO, whatever these are set to. Change them with [Update app](/api-reference/update-app).

is_remixable.title: Is Remixable
is_remixable.description: Whether others can remix the app. While it's `true`, the published app also shows the Base44 badge if `public_settings` is `public_with_login` or `public_without_login`.

hide_entity_created_by.title: Hide Entity Created By
hide_entity_created_by.description: Whether the app's entity records leave out the email of the user who created each one (`created_by`). Newer apps always leave the email out, whatever this is set to.

dev_environment_enabled.title: Dev Environment Enabled
dev_environment_enabled.description: Whether test data is on, which gives the app a test database next to its live one.

logo_url.title: Logo Url
logo_url.description: URL of the app's logo, or `null` if it has none. Set it with [Set app logo](/api-reference/set-app-logo) or [Generate app logo](/api-reference/generate-app-logo).

social_image_url.title: Social Image Url
social_image_url.description: URL of the image shown when the app is shared on social platforms, or `null` if none was set, in which case the logo is shown instead. Set it with [Set social image](/api-reference/set-social-image).

is_unpublished.title: Is Unpublished
is_unpublished.description: Whether the app was taken offline with [Unpublish app](/api-reference/unpublish-app) and hasn't been published again since. While it's `true`, the published URL is offline and `last_deployed_at` still shows the last publish.

AppSummary.title: AppSummary
AppSummary.description: An app in a workspace, limited to the properties the caller requested.

count.title: Count
count.description: Number of the app's users you can read.

AppUserCountResponse.title: AppUserCountResponse
AppUserCountResponse.description: The number of users registered in an app.

applied_incentive_code.title: Applied Incentive Code
applied_incentive_code.description: Google's coupon code for the incentive the account now holds. When the account already held one, this is that incentive's code rather than the offer you sent.

account_id.title: Account Id
account_id.description: ID of the Google Ads account the incentive applies to.

AppliedIncentiveResult.title: AppliedIncentiveResult
AppliedIncentiveResult.description: The incentive the Google Ads account holds after the call.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `archived`.

workflow_id.title: Workflow Id
workflow_id.description: ID of the workflow that was archived.

message.title: Message
message.description: Confirmation message.

ArchivedTemplateListing.title: ArchivedTemplateListing
ArchivedTemplateListing.description: Confirmation that the template listing is archived.

asset_group.title: Asset Group
asset_group.description: Name of the asset group the combination belongs to.

asset_group_id.title: Asset Group Id
asset_group_id.description: ID of that asset group, matching `asset_group_id` on [List asset performance](/api-reference/list-google-ads-asset-performance).

campaign.title: Campaign
campaign.description: Name of the campaign the asset group belongs to.

assets.title: Assets
assets.description: The assets in the combination, each as its text or its Google Ads name. An asset Base44 could not label falls back to its resource name.

AssetGroupCombinationRow.title: AssetGroupCombinationRow
AssetGroupCombinationRow.description: One combination of assets that served together.

resource_name.title: Resource Name
resource_name.description: Google Ads resource name for the asset's link to its asset group or campaign. Empty on rows Base44 synthesized from the campaign's saved creative.

field_type.title: Field Type
field_type.description: The role the asset plays, for example `HEADLINE`, `LONG_HEADLINE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `MARKETING_IMAGE`, `LOGO`, or `YOUTUBE_VIDEO`.

text.title: Text
text.description: The asset's text. Empty for images, logos and videos.

asset_name.title: Asset Name
asset_name.description: Google Ads' own name for the asset. Usually the only label an image, logo or video has.

type.title: Type
type.description: Google Ads asset type, for example `TEXT`, `IMAGE`, or `YOUTUBE_VIDEO`.

image_url.title: Image Url
image_url.description: Hosted URL for an image or logo asset. Empty for text and video assets.

video_id.title: Video Id
video_id.description: YouTube video ID for a `YOUTUBE_VIDEO` asset. Empty on other assets in an asset group, and absent entirely on logo rows and on rows Base44 synthesized from launch creative.

campaign.title: Campaign
campaign.description: Name of the campaign the asset serves in.

asset_group_id.title: Asset Group Id
asset_group_id.description: ID of the asset group the asset belongs to. Empty for logos, which attach to the campaign instead.

asset_group_name.title: Asset Group Name
asset_group_name.description: Name of that asset group. Empty for the same reason.

ad_strength.title: Ad Strength
ad_strength.description: Google Ads' strength rating for the asset group: `POOR`, `AVERAGE`, `GOOD`, `EXCELLENT`, or `PENDING`. Empty for logos.

primary_status.title: Primary Status
primary_status.description: Whether the asset can serve, for example `ELIGIBLE`, `LIMITED`, `DISAPPROVED`, or `PENDING_REVIEW`. `GATHERING_DATA` is Base44's own value, used on a row synthesized from launch creative that Google has not echoed back yet.

primary_status_reasons.title: Primary Status Reasons
primary_status_reasons.description: Why the asset is limited or disapproved. Empty when it serves normally.

policy_topics.title: Policy Topics
policy_topics.description: The Google Ads policy topics limiting the asset, without the generic status reasons `primary_status_reasons` also carries. Always empty for logos, which expose no policy detail, and absent on rows Base44 synthesized from launch creative.

performance_label.title: Performance Label
performance_label.description: Base44's own band for the asset, since Google publishes no per-asset rating for Performance Max: `LEARNING` while the campaign is still in its launch window, then `LOW`, `GOOD` or `EXCELLENT` from the asset's click-through rate against a threshold for its field type. `PENDING` and `DISAPPROVED` pass the serving status through instead. Empty when the asset cannot be rated, which is permanent for logos and for rows Base44 synthesized from launch creative.

impressions.title: Impressions
impressions.description: Impressions over the trailing 30 days. `null` when Google reported no row for the asset in that window, and absent entirely on logos and on rows Base44 synthesized from saved creative.

clicks.title: Clicks
clicks.description: Clicks over the same 30 days, with the same `null` and absent cases.

cost_micros.title: Cost Micros
cost_micros.description: Spend over the same 30 days in micros, with the same `null` and absent cases.

AssetPerformanceRow.title: AssetPerformanceRow
AssetPerformanceRow.description: One creative asset in a Performance Max campaign.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app the asset belongs to.

source_type.title: Source Type
source_type.description: How the file got into the library. `upload` for a file someone uploaded, and `generated` for most files Base44 created for the app, such as AI-generated images and videos or a Figma import.

file_type.title: File Type
file_type.description: File extension without the dot, usually lowercase, such as `png` or `mp4`. The value is `null` when the file was added without one.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the asset was added to the library, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: When the asset was last changed, such as renamed, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

AssetSummary.title: AssetSummary
AssetSummary.description: A file in the app's media library.

auto_renew.title: Auto Renew
auto_renew.description: Whether auto-renewal is now on. The value is `true` after turning renewal on and `false` after turning it off.

AutoRenewalResponse.title: AutoRenewalResponse
AutoRenewalResponse.description: The account's auto-renewal setting after the change.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the function. Nested functions have slashes in their name.

entry.title: Entry
entry.description: Path of the file the function starts from, one of the `path` values in `files`.

automations.title: Automations
automations.description: Automations that run the function. Empty when it has none.

example.description: Emails each user a summary of yesterday's tasks.
example.name: Nightly digest

BackendFunction.title: BackendFunction
BackendFunction.description: A backend function deployed for the app.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the automation.

type.title: Type
type.description: What starts the automation. `scheduled` runs it on a schedule, `entity` when records of an entity change, and `connector` on an event from a connected service. Each automation also carries the settings for its type, such as its schedule or the entity it watches.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the automation is for, or `null` if none was given.
description.example: Emails each user a summary of yesterday's tasks.

function_args.title: Function Args
function_args.description: Arguments the automation passes to the function, or `null` when it passes none.

is_active.title: Is Active
is_active.description: Whether the automation runs (`true`) or is paused (`false`).

BackendFunctionAutomation.title: BackendFunctionAutomation
BackendFunctionAutomation.description: An automation that runs a backend function.

path.title: Path
path.description: Path of the file in the function's deployment.

content.title: Content
content.description: The file's source.

BackendFunctionFile.title: BackendFunctionFile
BackendFunctionFile.description: One file of a backend function's code.

functions.title: Functions
functions.description: The functions, with their code and automations. Empty when the app has none.

operation_id.title: Operation Id
operation_id.description: ID of this entity's part of the restore, as `operation_id` in `launched`.

entity_name.title: Entity Name
entity_name.description: Entity this part of the restore rewrites.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where this entity's restore is, one of `pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, or `failed`. Only `succeeded` and `failed` are final.

counts.description: How many records the restore has changed in this entity so far.

pre_restore_checkpoint_id.title: Pre Restore Checkpoint Id
pre_restore_checkpoint_id.description: ID of the backup Base44 saved of this entity just before rewriting it, or `null` until it's saved. Restore this entity alone from it to undo its part of the restore.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why this entity's restore failed, in plain language, or `null` unless `status` is `failed`.
error.example: This restore point is no longer available.

BatchRestoreStatusItem.title: BatchRestoreStatusItem
BatchRestoreStatusItem.description: Where one entity's part of a restore has got to.

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: One entry per entity in the restore, oldest first. Empty when the app has no restore with this ID.

restore_to.title: Restore To
restore_to.description: The moment the entities are restored to, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format with a `Z` suffix, or `null` when `operations` is empty.

undo_checkpoint_id.title: Undo Checkpoint Id
undo_checkpoint_id.description: ID of the checkpoint that undoes the whole restore, or `null` until Base44 has saved the first backup. Restore the same entities from it to put them all back the way they were before.

BatchRestoreStatusResponse.title: BatchRestoreStatusResponse
BatchRestoreStatusResponse.description: Where each entity in a restore has got to.

results.title: Results
results.description: One entry per tool call that was answered, in the order they were processed. A repeated ID appears once, so this can be shorter than the list you sent. Empty when the request was a duplicate that had already been applied.

app.description: The app once the resumed turn finished.

BatchToolCallResponse.title: BatchToolCallResponse
BatchToolCallResponse.description: The app after a batch of tool calls was answered, with one result per call.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the tool call this result is for.

success.title: Success
success.description: Whether this tool call was answered successfully.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why this tool call could not be answered, or `null` when it succeeded.

billing_cadence.title: Billing Cadence
billing_cadence.description: The cadence now in effect: `1w`, `2w`, or `1m`.

BillingCadenceResponse.title: BillingCadenceResponse
BillingCadenceResponse.description: The account's billing cadence after the change.

has_payment_method.title: Has Payment Method
has_payment_method.description: Whether a usable card is on file. Read it together with `stripe_unavailable`, which changes what a `false` means.

stripe_unavailable.title: Stripe Unavailable
stripe_unavailable.description: Whether Base44 could not reach the payment provider. When it is `true`, `has_payment_method` reports `false` because the check fails closed, not because the card is missing. Retry rather than telling someone to add a card.

currency_code.title: Currency Code
currency_code.description: Currency the workspace is billed in, as an ISO 4217 code, or `null` before a card is on file.

payment_method_brand.title: Payment Method Brand
payment_method_brand.description: Card brand, for display. Empty when no card is on file.

payment_method_last4.title: Payment Method Last4
payment_method_last4.description: Last four digits of the card, for display, or `null` when no card is on file.

BillingStatusResponse.title: BillingStatusResponse
BillingStatusResponse.description: Whether the workspace can be charged for ad spend.

state.title: State
state.description: `processing` while the AI is working on the branch, `ready` once it's idle, and `error` when the last turn on the branch failed.

details.title: Details
details.description: Short note about the state, such as why the last turn failed, or `null` when there's nothing to report.

last_updated_date.title: Last Updated Date
last_updated_date.description: When the state last changed, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app the branch belongs to.

status.title: Status
status.description: `active` while the branch can still be worked on, `merged` once it was merged into main, and `deleted` once it was deleted.

run_state.description: State of the AI's work on the branch, or `null` if no turn has run on it yet.

code_state.title: Code State
code_state.description: `unchanged` when the branch has no code changes of its own to merge into main. `changed` otherwise, including when Base44 can't tell yet.

base_checkpoint_id.title: Base Checkpoint Id
base_checkpoint_id.description: ID of the main [checkpoint](/api-reference/list-checkpoints) the branch started from, or `null` if the app had no checkpoint yet.

created_by_id.title: Created By Id
created_by_id.description: ID of the user who created the branch.

created_by_name.title: Created By Name
created_by_name.description: Display name of the user who created the branch, or the part of their email before the `@` when they have no name. `null` when Base44 can't name them, for example when their account no longer exists.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the branch was created, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

merged_at.title: Merged At
merged_at.description: When the branch was merged into main, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or `null` if it wasn't.

merged_by_id.title: Merged By Id
merged_by_id.description: ID of the user who merged the branch, or `null` if it wasn't merged or Base44 doesn't know who did, as for a branch whose pull request was merged on GitHub.

static_preview_url.title: Static Preview Url
static_preview_url.description: URL of the branch's preview. It shows the branch only while it's active and once it has been built.

sync_status.description: How the branch stands against main after the update.

updated.title: Updated
updated.description: `false` when the branch was already up to date with main, so nothing changed. `true` when the update was applied, or when it's waiting for your input (`sync_status.sync_state` is `needs_input`).

new_main_message_count.title: New Main Message Count
new_main_message_count.description: How many chat messages people sent on main since the branch was created or last updated from main.

main_code_changed.title: Main Code Changed
main_code_changed.description: `true` when main's code changed since the branch was created or last updated from main.

conflict_state.title: Conflict State
conflict_state.description: Whether updating the branch from main is expected to conflict. `clear` when main's code hasn't changed, so an update can't conflict. `overlap` when the update is expected to conflict, or while conflicts from an update are being resolved. `unavailable` when Base44 can't tell, including while an update runs. Once main's code has changed, it's never `clear`, even when the update would apply cleanly.

sync_state.title: Sync State
sync_state.description: `idle` when no update is running. `updating` while main's changes are being applied, `resolving` while the AI resolves conflicts, and `needs_input` when the AI needs an answer to finish resolving them. Answer it in the Base44 editor. Until the state is back to `idle`, the branch can't be merged or deleted.

blocked_reason.title: Blocked Reason
blocked_reason.description: Why [Update branch from main](/api-reference/update-branch-from-main) would be refused right now: `app_processing` while the AI is working on main, and `branch_processing` while it's working on the branch. `null` when neither applies. An update is also refused while `sync_state` is `resolving` or `needs_input`.

BranchSyncStatus.title: BranchSyncStatus
BranchSyncStatus.description: How the branch stands against main.

landing_page.title: Landing Page
landing_page.description: Landing page the campaign would send clicks to. Required for a forecast.

geo_targets.title: Geo Targets
geo_targets.description: Locations to forecast for, as Google geo target constant IDs (`geoTargetConstants/1023191`, or just `1023191`). At least one is required for a forecast.

keyword_themes.title: Keyword Themes
keyword_themes.description: Themes the campaign would match on. An empty list forecasts nothing useful.

language_code.title: Language Code
language_code.description: Two-letter language the ads would run in. Defaults to `en`.

business_name.title: Business Name
business_name.description: Business name, which sharpens Google's forecast.

daily_budget.title: Daily Budget
daily_budget.description: Daily budget you have in mind, in micros (1,000,000 micros = 1 unit of the account's currency). Google's planner chooses the budget it forecasts at, so this is only reported back when Google returns no recommendation of its own.

monthly_limit_dollars.title: Monthly Limit Dollars
monthly_limit_dollars.description: The cap now in effect, in whole units of the account currency rather than micros.

BudgetLimitResponse.title: BudgetLimitResponse
BudgetLimitResponse.description: The account's monthly spend cap after the change.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it failed. Free text for people to read, not a stable code to branch on. Some reasons mean the budget did change on Google and only Base44's record of it failed, so verify before treating the entry as unchanged.
reason.example: Budget below the minimum for this currency

BulkBudgetFailure.title: BulkBudgetFailure
BulkBudgetFailure.description: One campaign whose budget update did not apply.

succeeded.title: Succeeded
succeeded.description: IDs of the campaigns whose budget was updated.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Campaigns that were left unchanged, each with a reason. Empty when every update applied.

example.reason: Budget below the minimum for this currency

BulkBudgetUpdateResponse.title: BulkBudgetUpdateResponse
BulkBudgetUpdateResponse.description: Per-campaign outcome of a bulk budget update.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email of the person to invite.

role.description: Role the invitee gets when they accept. Defaults to `viewer`. `admin` needs the Business plan or higher.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: ID of a custom group to add the invitee to when they accept. Get it from [List workspace groups](/api-reference/list-workspace-groups). Needs a plan that includes groups.

BulkInvitationItem.title: BulkInvitationItem
BulkInvitationItem.description: One invitation in a bulk invite.

total_sent.title: Total Sent
total_sent.description: Number of invitations sent, the length of `successful`.

successful.title: Successful
successful.description: Emails an invitation was sent to.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Invitations that weren't sent, with the reason. Empty when every invitation went out.

example.error: User already has a pending invitation

invitations.title: Invitations
invitations.description: The people to invite, 1 to 50. Each email can appear once.

BulkInviteRequest.title: BulkInviteRequest
BulkInviteRequest.description: Invitations to send in one request.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email of the member, exactly as `email` in [List workspace members](/api-reference/list-workspace-members) returns it. Matching is exact, including case.

credit_limit.title: Credit Limit
credit_limit.description: Most credits the member can use in the workspace each month, at least 1. `null`, or leaving it out, removes their own limit, so the workspace default applies.

results.title: Results
results.description: One entry per item, in request order.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email of the member.

status.title: Status
status.description: `success` when the change was applied, `skipped` when the member changed while the request ran and nothing was applied.

message.title: Message
message.description: Short explanation. Its wording can change, so don't parse it.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email of the member, exactly as `email` in [List workspace members](/api-reference/list-workspace-members) returns it. Matching is exact, including case.

role.description: The member's new role. `admin` needs the Business plan or higher.

emails.title: Emails
emails.description: Emails of the members or pending invitees to remove, 1 to 200, exactly as `email` in [List workspace members](/api-reference/list-workspace-members) returns them. Each email can appear once.

BulkRemoveMembersRequest.title: BulkRemoveMembersRequest
BulkRemoveMembersRequest.description: People to remove in one request.

emails.title: Emails
emails.description: Emails the pending invitations were sent to, 1 to 50. Each email can appear once.

entity_names.title: Entity Names
entity_names.description: Entities to restore, as [List entity schemas](/api-reference/list-entity-schemas) reports them. Name at least one and at most 300. They don't have to include the entity the checkpoint belongs to.

BulkRestoreRequest.title: BulkRestoreRequest
BulkRestoreRequest.description: Which entities to restore to the checkpoint.

batch_id.title: Batch Id
batch_id.description: ID of the restore. Pass it to [Get data restore status](/api-reference/get-data-restore-status) to follow it.

launched.title: Launched
launched.description: The entities whose restore started, each with the ID of its own part of the restore.

skipped_entities.title: Skipped Entities
skipped_entities.description: Entities you asked for that didn't start, because another restore was already running on them. Try them again once it finishes.

BulkRestoreStartResponse.title: BulkRestoreStartResponse
BulkRestoreStartResponse.description: The restore that started, and which entities it covers.

items.title: Items
items.description: The credit limits, 1 to 200. Each email can appear once.

BulkUpdateMemberCreditLimitRequest.title: BulkUpdateMemberCreditLimitRequest
BulkUpdateMemberCreditLimitRequest.description: Credit limits to apply in one request.

items.title: Items
items.description: The role changes, 1 to 200. Each email can appear once.

BulkUpdateMemberRoleRequest.title: BulkUpdateMemberRoleRequest
BulkUpdateMemberRoleRequest.description: Role changes to apply in one request.

business_profile_location_id.title: Business Profile Location Id
business_profile_location_id.description: The linked location as `locations/<id>`. Empty after unlinking.

BusinessProfileLinkResponse.title: BusinessProfileLinkResponse
BusinessProfileLinkResponse.description: The account's linked Google Business Profile location.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the brief. Pass this as `brief_id` to read, update, or delete it.

platform_type.title: Platform Type
platform_type.description: Which campaign type the brief is for, `SMART` or `PERFORMANCE_MAX`.

source.title: Source
source.description: Who wrote the brief. The value is `ai` when Base44 generated it and `user` when you created it.

business_description.title: Business Description
business_description.description: What the business does. Base44 uses this when it generates copy.
business_description.example: Handmade oak furniture, delivered across Germany.

landing_page_url.title: Landing Page Url
landing_page_url.description: URL the ads will send clicks to.

language.title: Language
language.description: Language the ad copy is written in, as a lowercase two-letter code. See the note on this field in each endpoint. Create and update echo what you send, while list and get report the normalized value.

target_audience.title: Target Audience
target_audience.description: Free-text description of who the campaign is for. Empty when unset.

daily_budget_micros.title: Daily Budget Micros
daily_budget_micros.description: Planned daily budget in micros of the account currency, so `15000000` is 15.00. The value is `0` when unset.

geo_targets.title: Geo Targets
geo_targets.description: Google Ads geo target constant IDs to target.

headlines.title: Headlines
headlines.description: Ad headlines. Populated by generate, or by you.

schedule_type.title: Schedule Type
schedule_type.description: When the campaign runs. Use `always` to run continuously, or `custom` to use `schedule_days`.

schedule_days.title: Schedule Days
schedule_days.description: Day and hour windows to run in, used only when `schedule_type` is `custom`.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the brief was created.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: When the brief was last changed.

details.title: Details
details.description: Extra detail about the change. For an `EDITED` entry this carries `field`, `before`, and `after`. It is empty for the other event types.

actor.title: Actor
actor.description: Who made the change: `system` for an automatic change such as a billing pause, otherwise the ID of the user who made it.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the change happened.

CampaignChangeLogEntry.title: CampaignChangeLogEntry
CampaignChangeLogEntry.description: One entry in a campaign's change log.

id.title: Id
id.description: Base44's ID for the campaign. Pass this as `campaign_id` on the other campaign endpoints.

google_campaign_id.title: Google Campaign Id
google_campaign_id.description: The campaign's ID in Google Ads.

status.title: Status
status.description: Serving state. A status of `REMOVED` is a deleted campaign, which stays listed for reporting.

daily_budget_micros.title: Daily Budget Micros
daily_budget_micros.description: Daily budget in micros of the account currency, so `15000000` is 15.00.

start_date.title: Start Date
start_date.description: Date the campaign started, or empty when it has not.

cost_micros.title: Cost Micros
cost_micros.description: Spend in micros of the account currency, or `0` when `metrics_pending` is true.

spend.title: Spend
spend.description: Spend as a decimal amount, taken from `cost_micros`, for display.

ctr.title: Ctr
ctr.description: Click-through rate, or `0` when `metrics_pending` is true.

review_status.title: Review Status
review_status.description: Google's policy review status. Always empty on a deleted campaign.

serving_status.title: Serving Status
serving_status.description: Google's serving status. Always empty on a deleted campaign.

primary_status.title: Primary Status
primary_status.description: Always empty on this endpoint. Read one campaign to get it.

primary_status_reasons.title: Primary Status Reasons
primary_status_reasons.description: Google's reasons why the campaign is limited or not serving. Always empty on a deleted campaign.

metrics_pending.title: Metrics Pending
metrics_pending.description: Present and `true` only when you passed `include_metrics=false`, meaning the metric fields above are zeroed rather than measured.

CampaignListItem.title: CampaignListItem
CampaignListItem.description: One row of the campaign list, carrying metrics but not the landing page, targeting, or phone number. Read one campaign for those.

id.title: Id
id.description: Base44's ID for the campaign. Absent when you changed `images`, which reports `updated_field_types` instead.

CampaignPatchResult.title: CampaignPatchResult
CampaignPatchResult.description: What an update returns, the campaign ID plus only the section that changed.

id.title: Id
id.description: Base44's ID for the campaign. Pass this as `campaign_id` on the other campaign endpoints.

google_campaign_id.title: Google Campaign Id
google_campaign_id.description: The campaign's ID in Google Ads. Empty while a just-created campaign is still being pushed to Google.

campaign_type.title: Campaign Type
campaign_type.description: Campaign type. Base44 creates `SMART` and `PERFORMANCE_MAX`. The other values appear only on campaigns created outside Base44 and synced in.

status.title: Status
status.description: Serving state in Base44's cache. A status of `REMOVED` is a deleted campaign, which Google keeps for reporting.

daily_budget_micros.title: Daily Budget Micros
daily_budget_micros.description: Daily budget in micros of the account currency, where 1,000,000 micros is one unit, so `15000000` is 15.00.

landing_page.title: Landing Page
landing_page.description: URL the ads send clicks to.

geo_targets.title: Geo Targets
geo_targets.description: Google Ads geo target constant IDs the campaign targets.

phone_number.title: Phone Number
phone_number.description: Campaign phone number in E.164, empty when the campaign has none. Both channel types store the normalized form Google holds: a call asset on PERFORMANCE_MAX, `smartCampaignSettings.phone_number` on SMART.

learning_ends_at.title: Learning Ends At
learning_ends_at.description: When Smart Bidding's learning period is expected to end, about 14 days after creation, or `null` on a campaign that has not started learning.

review_status.title: Review Status
review_status.description: Google's policy review status, passed through as Google reports it (`REVIEWED`, `UNDER_REVIEW`, …). Empty until the first sync after creation.

serving_status.title: Serving Status
serving_status.description: Google's serving status, passed through as Google reports it. Can still report review gating after policy review clears, so read it alongside `review_status`.

primary_status.title: Primary Status
primary_status.description: Google's summary of whether the campaign is serving well, passed through as Google reports it (`ELIGIBLE`, `LIMITED`, `NOT_SERVING`, …).

primary_status_reasons.title: Primary Status Reasons
primary_status_reasons.description: Google's reasons behind `primary_status`, for example why a campaign is limited. Empty when there is nothing to explain.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the campaign was created in Base44.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: When Base44 last changed its record of the campaign.

CampaignResource.title: CampaignResource
CampaignResource.description: The campaign fields this API commits to.

status.title: Status
status.description: The action that was applied: `paused`, `resumed`, or `deleted`.

CampaignStatusResponse.title: CampaignStatusResponse
CampaignStatusResponse.description: Acknowledgement returned by the single-campaign state changes.

status.title: Status
status.description: This is `cancelling` when the request was accepted. On a run that had already finished, it's that run's existing status instead, and nothing changed.

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`.

already_terminal.title: Already Terminal
already_terminal.description: `true` when the run had already ended, so nothing changed. Left out when the run was cancelled.

CancelTestRunResult.title: CancelTestRunResult
CancelTestRunResult.description: The result of cancelling a run.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the cancelled ownership transfer.

status.title: Status
status.description: Status of the transfer, which is always `cancelled`.

CancelledOwnershipTransfer.title: CancelledOwnershipTransfer
CancelledOwnershipTransfer.description: An ownership transfer that was just cancelled.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `success`.

message.title: Message
message.description: Short confirmation. Its wording can change, so don't parse it.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: The conversation's messages once the request finished, oldest first.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the app.

status.description: The app's build status once the request returned. Read `state` to tell a finished turn from one that is still processing or that failed.

conversation.description: The app's conversation, including the messages this request produced.

ChatTurnResponse.title: ChatTurnResponse
ChatTurnResponse.description: An app, with its conversation and build status.

message.title: Message
message.description: What went wrong with the build. When a checkpoint is marked `failed` after waiting too long for another build of the same commit, this is `Timed out waiting for another build of this commit to finish`.
message.example: Timed out waiting for another build of this commit to finish

files.title: Files
files.description: The checkpoint's source files, keyed by path. Pages, components, backend functions, entities and agents are keyed by kind and name with no file extension, such as `pages/Home` or `functions/sendWelcomeEmail`. A few files use a fixed name, such as `layout`. Entity, agent and workflow definitions come back as JSON objects, and source files as text.

CheckpointFiles.title: CheckpointFiles
CheckpointFiles.description: The source files saved in a checkpoint.

checkpoint_id.title: Checkpoint Id
checkpoint_id.description: ID of the checkpoint. Pass it to [Download data checkpoint](/api-reference/download-data-checkpoint) or [Restore data to checkpoint](/api-reference/restore-data-to-checkpoint).

data_as_of.title: Data As Of
data_as_of.description: The moment the checkpoint marks, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format with a `Z` suffix. The checkpoint holds the entity's data as it was just before this moment, so it leaves out the change that created it.

trigger_type.title: Trigger Type
trigger_type.description: What created the checkpoint. `crud` means a change to a record, `schema_change` means a change to the entity's schema, and `restore` means the backup Base44 saves just before a restore rewrites the entity.

restore_batch_id.title: Restore Batch Id
restore_batch_id.description: ID of the restore that saved this backup, as `batch_id` from [Restore data to checkpoint](/api-reference/restore-data-to-checkpoint). It is `null` on every checkpoint that isn't a restore backup, and on backups saved before Base44 started recording it.

CheckpointListItem.title: CheckpointListItem
CheckpointListItem.description: One point in an entity's version history that its data can be restored to.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page. The value is `null` if there are no more pages. A full page always carries one, so the page after it can come back empty.

CheckpointListPage.title: CheckpointListPage
CheckpointListPage.description: One page of an app's version-history checkpoints, newest first.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: The entity's columns at the checkpoint, in order. That's the fields its schema declared then, followed by the fields Base44 adds to every record. Use them as the header row when you write `records` to a CSV file.

records.title: Records
records.description: Every record the entity held at the checkpoint, in the same shape as [List entity records](/api-reference/list-entity-records) returns them.

CheckpointSnapshotDownload.title: CheckpointSnapshotDownload
CheckpointSnapshotDownload.description: An entity's records as they stood at a checkpoint.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the checkpoint. Pass it as `checkpoint_id` to [Deploy an app](/api-reference/deploy-an-app) to deploy this saved version.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the checkpoint.

changes.title: Changes
changes.description: Summary of what changed in this checkpoint, or `null` if none was recorded.
changes.example: Added a contact form to the home page

preview_status.title: Preview Status
preview_status.description: Build status of this checkpoint's preview. Either `pending`, `building`, `ready`, or `failed`, or `null` if no preview build was attempted. A `failed` build can be retried with [Retry checkpoint build](/api-reference/retry-checkpoint-build).

build_error.description: Why the checkpoint's last preview build failed, or `null` if no failure was recorded. It's cleared when a build succeeds, so while a retry is `building` it can still describe the previous failure.

example.message: Timed out waiting for another build of this commit to finish

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: Email of the user who created the checkpoint.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: Time the checkpoint was created, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

last_deployed_at.title: Last Deployed At
last_deployed_at.description: Time this checkpoint was last deployed to production, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or `null` if it has never been deployed.

git_commit_hash.title: Git Commit Hash
git_commit_hash.description: Git commit hash of the code captured in this checkpoint, or `null` if it has no commit.

preview_url.title: Preview Url
preview_url.description: URL to preview this checkpoint's build, or `null` if the checkpoint has no build.

is_github_sync.title: Is Github Sync
is_github_sync.description: Whether the checkpoint came from a GitHub sync (`true`) or an in-app change (`false`).

CheckpointSummary.title: CheckpointSummary
CheckpointSummary.description: A saved version of an app.

claim_url.title: Claim Url
claim_url.description: Stripe onboarding link, or `null` when no link is available. Treat this link as a credential.

is_claimable.title: Is Claimable
is_claimable.description: Whether the returned link starts a claim. A link that resumes activation of an already claimed sandbox returns `false`.

no_link_reason.title: No Link Reason
no_link_reason.description: Reason no link is returned. `already_active` means the account already finished activation, so there's nothing left to claim. `sandbox_expired` means an unclaimed sandbox passed its 60-day window. `unavailable` covers every other case, including no sandbox at all. Otherwise `null`, when a link is returned. Defaults to `null`.

https.title: Https
https.description: URL to clone the repository over HTTPS.

ssh.title: Ssh
ssh.description: URL to clone the repository over SSH.

CloneUrls.title: CloneUrls
CloneUrls.description: Repository clone URLs in different formats.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the collaborator. Pass it to [Remove collaborator](/api-reference/remove-collaborator). The owner's entry can have the ID `owner`, which isn't a real ID.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email of the collaborator.

full_name.title: Full Name
full_name.description: Full name of the collaborator, or `null` if none is set.

profile_image_url.title: Profile Image Url
profile_image_url.description: URL of the collaborator's Base44 profile image, or `null` if they don't have one.

profile_slug.title: Profile Slug
profile_slug.description: Slug of the collaborator's public Base44 builder profile, or `null` if they don't have one.

is_owner.title: Is Owner
is_owner.description: Whether the collaborator owns the app.

is_pending.title: Is Pending
is_pending.description: Whether the collaborator was invited but hasn't opened the app in Base44 yet.

is_guest.title: Is Guest
is_guest.description: Whether the collaborator is a guest in the app's workspace rather than a member.

collaborator_source.title: Collaborator Source
collaborator_source.description: `workspace` when the collaborator joined because the app is open to everyone in its workspace, or `null` when they were invited.

CollaboratorResponse.title: CollaboratorResponse
CollaboratorResponse.description: A person who can edit the app in Base44.

source_location.title: Source Location
source_location.description: Position of the element's tag in the app's code, as `file:line:column`, exactly as the element's `data-source-location` attribute in the preview. The pin shows only on an element with this value. `null` for a thread with no pin.

element_tag.title: Element Tag
element_tag.description: HTML tag of the element, such as `button`.

instance_index.title: Instance Index
instance_index.description: Which of the elements sharing `source_location` the pin is on, counting from `0` in page order, for an element repeated in a list. `null` means the first.

point.description: Where on the element the pin sits. `null` puts it at the middle of the top edge.

crop.description: Area of the page the screenshot shows, used to redraw the crop box in the builder.

region.description: Area of the visible preview the screenshot shows when it was taken.

viewport_size.description: Size of the preview when the screenshot was taken.

CommentAnchor.title: CommentAnchor
CommentAnchor.description:
Where a comment thread is pinned in the app's preview. When the builder's AI edits the anchored
file, Base44 moves an open thread's `source_location` to the element's new line.

y.title: Y
y.description: Top edge, in page pixels, scroll included.

CommentAnchorCrop.title: CommentAnchorCrop
CommentAnchorCrop.description: The screenshot's area in page pixels: the visible area plus the page's scroll when it was taken.

x.title: X
x.description: Horizontal position, as a fraction of the element's width.

y.title: Y
y.description: Vertical position, as a fraction of the element's height.

CommentAnchorPoint.title: CommentAnchorPoint
CommentAnchorPoint.description: Fractions of the anchored element's rect, not of the document.

x.title: X
x.description: Left edge, as a fraction of the preview's width.

y.title: Y
y.description: Top edge, as a fraction of the preview's height.

width.title: Width
width.description: Width, as a fraction of the preview's width.

height.title: Height
height.description: Height, as a fraction of the preview's height.

CommentAnchorRegion.title: CommentAnchorRegion
CommentAnchorRegion.description: The screenshot's area as fractions of the visible preview when it was taken, so it depends on the scroll.

width.title: Width
width.description: Width of the preview, in pixels.

height.title: Height
height.description: Height of the preview, in pixels.

CommentAnchorViewportSize.title: CommentAnchorViewportSize
CommentAnchorViewportSize.description: Size of the preview when the screenshot was taken.

content.title: Content
content.description: Text of the comment.
content.example: Make this button match the header color.

sender_id.title: Sender Id
sender_id.description: ID of the Base44 user who wrote it, or `base44` for a reply from the builder agent.

sender_name.title: Sender Name
sender_name.description: Name of the author when they wrote it, or their email when they had no name. `Base44` for the builder agent.

sender_avatar_url.title: Sender Avatar Url
sender_avatar_url.description: URL of the author's profile image, or `null` when they have none.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the comment was posted, in UTC.

edited_at.title: Edited At
edited_at.description: When the comment was last edited, in UTC, or `null` when it never was.

reactions.title: Reactions
reactions.description: Each emoji reacted with, mapped to the IDs of the users who reacted with it.

CommentMessage.title: CommentMessage
CommentMessage.description: One comment: the first comment of a thread or a reply.

page_path.title: Page Path
page_path.description: Path of the app page the thread is on.

anchor.description: Where the thread is pinned in the app's preview.

screenshot_url.title: Screenshot Url
screenshot_url.description: Signed link to the screenshot attached to the thread, valid for one hour. `null` when the thread has no screenshot or it can't be read.

resolved_at.title: Resolved At
resolved_at.description: When the thread was resolved, in UTC, or `null` while it's open.

message_count.title: Message Count
message_count.description: Number of replies, not counting the first comment.

last_activity_at.title: Last Activity At
last_activity_at.description: When the thread was created or last replied to, in UTC.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the thread was created, in UTC.

agent_working_since.title: Agent Working Since
agent_working_since.description: When the builder agent started working on the thread, in UTC, or `null` when it isn't working on it. A value older than an hour is left over from a turn that stopped.

unread.title: Unread
unread.description: Whether the thread has a comment from someone else posted after you last read it. Always `false` in the responses of Create comment and Update comment anchor.

comment.description: The first comment, which started the thread.

example.content: Done, it now uses the header blue.

reactor_names.title: Reactor Names
reactor_names.description: User ID mapped to name, for the people who reacted anywhere in the thread.

CommentThreadItem.title: CommentThreadItem
CommentThreadItem.description: A comment thread with all its comments.

items.title: Items
items.description: Threads on this page, newest first.

comment.content: Make this button match the header color.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: Whether more threads follow this page.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
