next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` on the last page.

CommentThreadList.title: CommentThreadList
CommentThreadList.description: One page of an app's comment threads.

configuration_status.title: Configuration Status
configuration_status.description: Where setup stands after the retry. Only `active` sends mail. A retry starts the next step rather than finishing it, so this is often still a `pending_` value, meaning setup is in progress. The `failed_` values mean it stopped and you can try again.

last_check.title: Last Check
last_check.description: When Base44 last checked this domain's records, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or `null` before the first check.

publishable_key.title: Publishable Key
publishable_key.description: Live Stripe publishable key beginning with `pk_live_`.

secret_key.title: Secret Key
secret_key.description: Live Stripe secret or restricted key beginning with `sk_live_` or `rk_live_`.

webhook_secret.title: Webhook Secret
webhook_secret.description: Live webhook signing secret beginning with `whsec_`. Defaults to `null`, which attempts automatic migration when an existing webhook secret is present.

ConfigureLiveKeysRequest.title: ConfigureLiveKeysRequest
ConfigureLiveKeysRequest.description: Request to configure live mode API keys.

org_name.title: Org Name
org_name.description: GitHub username or organization to create the repository under, as returned in `login` by [List GitHub organizations](/api-reference/list-github-organizations).

repo_name.title: Repo Name
repo_name.description: Name for the new repository. 1 to 100 characters made of letters, digits, hyphens, underscores or periods, starting and ending with a letter or digit, and it must not already exist on the account.

installation_id.title: Installation Id
installation_id.description: ID of the Base44 GitHub App installation on that account, as returned in `installation_id` by [List GitHub organizations](/api-reference/list-github-organizations). Provide either this or `workspace_installation_id`.

workspace_installation_id.title: Workspace Installation Id
workspace_installation_id.description: ID of a GitHub installation connected to the app's workspace, as returned by the workspace installations listing. Provide either this or `installation_id`.

description.title: Description
description.description: Description for the new repository. Defaults to the app's name.
description.example: Sales lead tracker

ConnectRepoRequest.title: ConnectRepoRequest
ConnectRepoRequest.description:
Request to connect a repository.

Exactly one of `installation_id` or `workspace_installation_id` must be provided.

disabled.title: Disabled
disabled.description: Whether the domain is connected but turned off.

name.title: Name
name.description: Key to send the value under in `connection_config`.

description.title: Description
description.description: Help text that explains where to find the value.
description.example: The part of your Snowflake URL before .snowflakecomputing.com.

placeholder.title: Placeholder
placeholder.description: Sample value to show in an empty input.

required.title: Required
required.description: Whether the value has to be sent (`true`) or can be left out (`false`).

default_value.title: Default Value
default_value.description: Value used when the field is left out, or `null` if there is none.

validation_pattern.title: Validation Pattern
validation_pattern.description: Regular expression the whole value has to match, or `null` if any value is accepted.

validation_error.title: Validation Error
validation_error.description: Message returned when the value doesn't match `validation_pattern`, or `null` for the default message.
validation_error.example: Use letters, digits, and hyphens only.

ConnectionConfigField.title: ConnectionConfigField
ConnectionConfigField.description: Schema for a connection configuration field.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Values to collect and send as `connection_config`. Empty when the connector needs none.

example.description: The part of your Snowflake URL before .snowflakecomputing.com.
example.name: subdomain
example.validation_error: Use letters, digits, and hyphens only.

connection_config.title: Connection Config
connection_config.description: Values saved on the app's current connection, keyed by field `name`. Empty when there's no connection.

ConnectionConfigResponse.title: ConnectionConfigResponse
ConnectionConfigResponse.description: The values a connector needs before authorization, and the app's saved ones.

connection_mode.description: Workspace GitHub write model; null when not connected.

user_github_connected.title: User Github Connected
user_github_connected.description: Whether the current user has a linked GitHub account; computed only in per_user mode.

can_push.title: Can Push
can_push.description: Whether the connection permits a push attempt under the workspace mode. Failed user permission lookups allow an attempt; GitHub enforces access.

connected.title: Connected
connected.description: Whether the app still has its repository connection, including one whose `status` is `error` or `revoked`. The value is `false` only when the app never connected and when its repository was disconnected.

repo_full_name.title: Repo Full Name
repo_full_name.description: Full repository name, as `owner/repo`, or `null` when `connected` is `false`.

repo_url.title: Repo Url
repo_url.description: URL of the repository on GitHub, or `null` when `connected` is `false`.

clone_urls.description: URLs and CLI command for cloning the repository, or `null` when `connected` is `false`.

org_name.title: Org Name
org_name.description: GitHub username or organization that owns the repository, or `null` when `connected` is `false`.

status.description: Health of the connection, or `null` when `connected` is `false`. A value of `active` works normally, `error` hit a technical failure, and `revoked` means the GitHub App access was withdrawn. The last two still report `connected: true`, so this is the field that tells you the connection needs repair.

installation_id.title: Installation Id
installation_id.description: ID of the Base44 GitHub App installation backing this connection, or `null` when `connected` is `false` and on a connection stored without one.

webhook_active.title: Webhook Active
webhook_active.description: Whether the repository has the Base44 webhook that triggers automatic pulls. While this is `false` on a connected app, GitHub isn't telling Base44 about pushes, so nothing arrives until you pull.

connected_by_user_id.title: Connected By User Id
connected_by_user_id.description: ID of the Base44 user who connected the repository, or `null` when `connected` is `false`.

previous_repository.description: The repository a user disconnected the app from, which [Reconnect a GitHub repository](/api-reference/reconnect-a-github-repository) can bring back, or `null` when the app is connected, never connected, or lost its repository some other way.

ConnectionStatus.title: ConnectionStatus
ConnectionStatus.description: Current connection status for an app.

connector_mode.title: Connector Mode
connector_mode.description: Which ways the connector can be connected. One of `all`, `shared_only`, `app_user_only`, `byo_shared_only`, or `byo_shared_and_app_user`, with the same meaning as `connector_mode` in [List connectors](/api-reference/list-connectors).

builder_connection_enabled.title: Builder Connection Enabled
builder_connection_enabled.description: Whether the workspace lets builders connect the connector to its apps (`true`) or has turned that off (`false`). When it's `false`, starting a connection is refused.

per_user_connection_enabled.title: Per User Connection Enabled
per_user_connection_enabled.description: Whether the apps' users can connect their own accounts with the workspace's credentials (`true`) or not (`false`). Always `false` when `has_per_user_credentials` is `false`.

has_per_user_credentials.title: Has Per User Credentials
has_per_user_credentials.description: Whether the workspace has set up its own OAuth app credentials for the connector.

items.title: Items
items.description: One entry per connector available to the workspace.

has_any_governance_policies.title: Has Any Governance Policies
has_any_governance_policies.description: Whether the workspace has restricted any connector (`true`) or left them all at the defaults (`false`).

ConnectorGovernanceListResponse.title: ConnectorGovernanceListResponse
ConnectorGovernanceListResponse.description: The workspace's connector policies, as they apply to the app.

ConnectorMode.title: ConnectorMode
ConnectorMode.description: Which ways a connector can be connected.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app the plan belongs to.

strategy.description: The strategy and the per-platform posts.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: Time the plan was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

updated_at.title: Updated At
updated_at.description: Time the plan last changed, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

plan.description: The app's content plan, or `null` if it has none.

ContentPlanResponse.title: ContentPlanResponse
ContentPlanResponse.description: The app's social content plan after the change.

app_summary.title: App Summary
app_summary.description: Short summary of what the app does.
app_summary.example: A CRM for freelancers who want to track leads without a spreadsheet.

marketing_approach.title: Marketing Approach
marketing_approach.description: The approach the content takes, extracted from the accepted strategy. Empty if the strategy text was empty when the plan was generated.
marketing_approach.example: Lead with the spreadsheet pain, then show the app solving it.

platforms.title: Platforms
platforms.description: One entry per platform you approved, in the order you sent them.

last_message_preview.title: Last Message Preview
last_message_preview.description: First 100 characters of the latest message in the user's newest conversation with this agent.
last_message_preview.example: Your order ships tomorrow and should arrive by Friday.

last_message_time.title: Last Message Time
last_message_time.description: When the user's newest conversation with this agent was last updated, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

conversation_count.title: Conversation Count
conversation_count.description: Number of conversations the user has with this agent.

message_count.title: Message Count
message_count.description: Number of messages across the user's conversations with this agent.

credit_count.title: Credit Count
credit_count.description: Credits charged for this agent's replies across the user's conversations with it.

conversations.title: Conversations
conversations.description: Up to 100 of the user's conversations with this agent.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: The requested window of messages, oldest first.

ConversationDetail.description: A window of messages from an app's AI chat.

app_id.description: ID of the app.

agent_name.title: Agent Name
agent_name.description: Name of the agent the conversation is with.

created_by_id.title: Created By Id
created_by_id.description: ID of the app user who started the conversation. An anonymous visitor's conversation carries `anonymous`, `guest`, an empty string, or `null` instead.

created_by_email.title: Created By Email
created_by_email.description: Email of the app user who started the conversation, or `null` for an anonymous visitor or an app user who no longer exists.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Free-form data stored with the conversation. It holds whatever the app set when it created the conversation, plus channel details such as a WhatsApp user's phone number.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Up to the 200 most recent messages, oldest first. Each message has a `role` of `user` or `assistant` and its `content`. An assistant message also lists the `tool_calls` the agent made and what each one returned, which can include records from the app's data.

credit_count.title: Credit Count
credit_count.description: Credits charged for the agent's replies in the conversation.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the conversation was created, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: When the conversation was last updated, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

ConversationDetailResponse.description: One conversation with one of the app's agents, with its messages.

role.title: Role
role.description: Who produced the message. A `user` message is a prompt sent to the AI, an `assistant` message is the AI's reply, and a `system` message is a platform-generated note.

content.title: Content
content.description: Text of the message. Empty on assistant turns whose work is carried entirely by tool calls, and on internal diff messages.

file_urls.title: File Urls
file_urls.description: URLs of the files attached to the message, or `null` if it has none.

hidden.title: Hidden
hidden.description: Whether the message is internal and hidden from the chat in the app editor.

checkpoint_id.title: Checkpoint Id
checkpoint_id.description: ID of the [checkpoint](/developers/references/app-management/get-started/concepts#checkpoints) this message produced, or `null` if it produced none. Pass it as `checkpoint_id` to [Deploy an app](/api-reference/deploy-an-app) to deploy that version.

tool_calls.title: Tool Calls
tool_calls.description: Tool calls the AI made on this message, or `null` on messages that made none. A call with `status` set to `waiting_for_user_input` is holding the turn open until it is answered.

usage.description: Tokens and credits this message consumed, or `null` on messages that consumed none.

created_by_email.description: Email of the app user who started the conversation, or `null` for an anonymous visitor or an app user who no longer exists.

metadata.description: Free-form data stored with the conversation. It holds whatever the app set when it created the conversation, plus channel details such as a WhatsApp user's phone number.

created_date.description: When the conversation was created, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: When the conversation was last updated, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

message_count.title: Message Count
message_count.description: Number of messages in the conversation.

credit_count.title: Credit Count
credit_count.description: Credits charged for the agent's replies in the conversation.

first_message_preview.title: First Message Preview
first_message_preview.description: First 100 characters of the conversation's title, or of its first visible message when it doesn't have a title.

last_message_preview.title: Last Message Preview
last_message_preview.description: First 100 characters of the conversation's latest message.

last_message_time.description: When the conversation was last updated, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the tool call. Pass it as `tool_call_id` to [Submit tool-call input](/api-reference/submit-tool-call-input) when `status` is `waiting_for_user_input`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the tool the AI is calling.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the tool call is. Either `running`, `success`, `error`, `stopped`, or `waiting_for_user_input`. The last one means the turn is paused until the call is answered.

requires_user_input.title: Requires User Input
requires_user_input.description: Whether this tool call has to be approved or rejected before the turn can continue.

arguments_string.title: Arguments String
arguments_string.description: What the AI asked the tool to do, as a JSON object encoded in a string. Parse it to see the arguments before answering a call that is waiting. On a call whose `requires_user_input` is `true` the value is complete rather than shortened, which is the case that matters, because approving without reading it is approving blind. On any other call it can be cut to the first 500 characters. The one exception either way is the browser-typing tools, `local_browser_type` and `local_browser_press_key`, which always replace what was typed with `[redacted]` so a password or one-time code is never returned, waiting or not. Approving one of those means approving a value you cannot see. It is an empty string on a tool call that takes no arguments.

ConversationToolCallSummary.title: ConversationToolCallSummary
ConversationToolCallSummary.description: A tool call on an assistant message.

user_group_key.title: User Group Key
user_group_key.description: Key the user's conversations are grouped under. It's the app user's ID, `anonymous:` followed by the visitor ID for an anonymous visitor, or `__anonymous_visitors__` for anonymous conversations without a visitor ID.

created_by_id.title: Created By Id
created_by_id.description: ID of the app user who started the conversation. An anonymous visitor's conversation carries `anonymous`, `guest`, an empty string, or `null` instead.

created_by_email.title: Created By Email
created_by_email.description: Email of the app user who started the conversation, or `null` for an anonymous visitor or an app user who no longer exists.

created_by_name.title: Created By Name
created_by_name.description: Full name of the app user, or `null` if it isn't set. An anonymous visitor gets a generated display name instead.

role.title: Role
role.description: The app user's role in the app, such as `user` or `admin`. It's `guest` for an anonymous visitor, or `null` if the app user no longer exists.

is_anonymous_user.title: Is Anonymous User
is_anonymous_user.description: `true` for an anonymous visitor, and `false` for a signed-in app user.

anonymous_visitor_id.title: Anonymous Visitor Id
anonymous_visitor_id.description: ID that identifies an anonymous visitor across conversations. Read it only when `is_anonymous_user` is `true`.

agent_names.title: Agent Names
agent_names.description: Names of the agents the user has conversations with.

agent_count.title: Agent Count
agent_count.description: Number of agents the user has conversations with.

conversation_count.title: Conversation Count
conversation_count.description: Number of conversations the user has with the app's agents.

message_count.title: Message Count
message_count.description: Number of messages across the user's conversations.

credit_count.title: Credit Count
credit_count.description: Credits charged for the agents' replies across the user's conversations.

latest_time.title: Latest Time
latest_time.description: When the user's newest conversation was last updated, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: The user's conversations broken down by agent.

conversations.title: Conversations
conversations.description: Up to 100 of the user's conversations across all of the app's agents.

id.title: Id
id.description: Base44's ID for the conversion action.

google_action_id.title: Google Action Id
google_action_id.description: Google Ads' own ID for the goal, as Google Ads reports it. Not the same as `id`.

action_name.title: Action Name
action_name.description: Name of the goal in Google Ads.

category.title: Category
category.description: Google Ads conversion category, for example `PURCHASE`, `ADD_TO_CART`, `SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM`, or `SIGN_UP`.

action_type.title: Action Type
action_type.description: Google Ads conversion type. `WEBPAGE` for the goals Base44 creates. Empty on goals created before Base44 recorded the type.

conversion_id.title: Conversion Id
conversion_id.description: The gtag conversion ID for the goal. Empty until Google publishes the tag.

conversion_label.title: Conversion Label
conversion_label.description: The gtag conversion label for the goal. Empty until Google publishes the tag.

ConversionActionResource.title: ConversionActionResource
ConversionActionResource.description: One conversion goal on the Google Ads account.

status.title: Status
status.description: Outcome of the request, which is `deleted` once the mapping is gone.

ConversionMappingDeleteResponse.title: ConversionMappingDeleteResponse
ConversionMappingDeleteResponse.description: Outcome of deleting a conversion mapping.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the mapping. Pass this as `mapping_id` to update or delete it.

account_id.title: Account Id
account_id.description: ID of the Google Ads account the mapping belongs to.

entity_name.title: Entity Name
entity_name.description: Name of the app entity whose write this goal belongs to, as returned by [List entity schemas](/api-reference/list-entity-schemas). It is empty on a mapping Base44 created from a conversion it verified firing in the app code, because a client-side conversion has no entity behind it.

trigger_action.title: Trigger Action
trigger_action.description: Which write on the entity the goal belongs to. Base44 uses `create`, `update`, and `delete`, and stores any other value as sent.

conversion_type.title: Conversion Type
conversion_type.description: Which kind of conversion this is, using Google's category vocabulary such as `PURCHASE`, `ADD_TO_CART`, `BEGIN_CHECKOUT`, `SIGN_UP`, `LEAD`, or `CONTACT`. Empty when nothing was set for it. The value is stored as sent and not checked against Google's list.

conversion_action_id.title: Conversion Action Id
conversion_action_id.description: Google Ads' own ID for the goal this mapping points at, as returned in `google_action_id` by [List conversion actions](/api-reference/list-google-ads-conversion-actions). Empty when nothing was set for it. A mapping can carry both this and `conversion_type`, and this one is matched first. If it matches no goal on the account, which happens when the goal was recreated in Google Ads under a new ID, the mapping falls back to matching on `conversion_type`.

value_field.title: Value Field
value_field.description: Field on the entity record holding the conversion amount. It is read only when writing the wiring instructions for the AI builder, which falls back to `amount` when this is empty.

currency_field.title: Currency Field
currency_field.description: Field on the entity record holding the currency code. Same use as `value_field`, and the instructions fall back to `USD` when this is empty.

id_field.title: Id Field
id_field.description: Field on the entity record holding the order ID Google dedupes on. Same use as `value_field`, and the instructions fall back to `id` when this is empty.

is_enabled.title: Is Enabled
is_enabled.description: Whether Base44 counts this mapping when it decides a campaign's conversion events are configured (`true`) or ignores it (`false`).

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the mapping was created.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: When the mapping was last changed.

ConversionMappingResource.title: ConversionMappingResource
ConversionMappingResource.description: A conversion goal tied to an entity write in the app.

campaign_id.title: Campaign Id
campaign_id.description: The Google Ads campaign ID. This is not the Base44 campaign ID the campaign endpoints take, which is reported as `id` by [List campaigns](/api-reference/list-google-ads-campaigns).

conversions.title: Conversions
conversions.description: Conversions recorded for the campaign in the window.

conversions_value.title: Conversions Value
conversions_value.description: Total value of those conversions, in the account's currency.

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether anything reached Google. The value is `success` when at least one conversion landed and `no_rows_uploaded` when none did, so it does not tell you the whole batch landed.

total_submitted.title: Total Submitted
total_submitted.description: How many conversions you sent, counted before any of the checks below.

duplicates_removed.title: Duplicates Removed
duplicates_removed.description: How many conversions were dropped as duplicates of another conversion in the same request, matching on order or click ID together with the goal and the timestamp.

cross_request_duplicates.title: Cross Request Duplicates
cross_request_duplicates.description: How many conversions a previous request already reported. Base44 remembers every conversion it has sent, permanently, so a retried upload lands here instead of counting twice.

skipped_no_click_id.title: Skipped No Click Id
skipped_no_click_id.description: How many conversions were dropped before Google saw them because they carried none of `gclid`, `gbraid`, or `wbraid`. Google requires one of the three.

ConversionUploadResult.title: ConversionUploadResult
ConversionUploadResult.description: What happened to a batch of uploaded conversions.

protected.title: Protected
protected.description: Always `true`. The published app now enforces the protection.

CoreIntegrationProtectionEnabled.title: CoreIntegrationProtectionEnabled
CoreIntegrationProtectionEnabled.description: Confirms core integration protection is on.

content.title: Content
content.description: Text of the comment, 1 to 5000 characters.
content.example: Make this button match the header color.

page_path.title: Page Path
page_path.description: Path of the app page the comment is about. Defaults to `/`.

anchor.description: Where to pin the thread in the app's preview. Leave it out for a thread with no pin.

screenshot_file_uri.title: Screenshot File Uri
screenshot_file_uri.description: `file_uri` of a screenshot uploaded to this app with [Upload app file](/api-reference/upload-app-file) and `visibility` set to `private`. Starts with `mp/private/` followed by the app's ID.

mentioned_emails.title: Mentioned Emails
mentioned_emails.description: Emails of up to 50 people the comment mentions. Mentions send no notification.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the folder, 1 to 100 characters. Names don't have to be unique.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: `workspace` for a folder every member of the workspace sees, or `personal` for one only you see.

parent_folder_id.title: Parent Folder Id
parent_folder_id.description: ID of the folder to create this one in, or `null` for a top-level folder. The parent must have the same `scope` and `app_type`, and a personal parent must be yours.

position.title: Position
position.description: Sort key among folders. Lower values come first.

color.title: Color
color.description: Color for the folder, up to 32 characters, such as a hex color.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: Icon name for the folder, up to 64 characters.

app_type.title: App Type
app_type.description: `user_app` for a folder of builder apps, or `user_agent` for a folder of agents. Defaults to `user_app`.

branch_name.title: Branch Name
branch_name.description: Name of the branch. It starts with a letter or digit and contains only letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `/` and `-`. It can't contain `..` or `//`, end with `/` or `.`, start with `b44/`, or be `main`, and no part between slashes can start with `.` or end with `.lock`. Leave it out to have Base44 name the branch from `prompt`.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: Text to name the branch from when you leave out `branch_name`. Base44 generates a short name from it. An empty string names the branch after your first name and today's date.
prompt.example: Add a contact form to the home page

from_message_id.title: From Message Id
from_message_id.description: ID of a message in main's conversation, from [Read conversation messages](/api-reference/read-conversation-messages). The branch starts from the app as it was when that message was sent, instead of from main's latest state. Without `branch_name`, the branch is named after the last user message before that one, and `prompt` is ignored.

CreateBranchRequest.title: CreateBranchRequest
CreateBranchRequest.description: The new branch's name, or text to name it from.

checkpoint_id.title: Checkpoint Id
checkpoint_id.description: ID of the checkpoint. Pass it as `checkpoint_id` to [Restore checkpoint](/api-reference/restore-checkpoint) to come back to this state.

name.title: Name
name.description: The checkpoint's title, either the `name` you sent or one Base44 generated.

git_commit_hash.title: Git Commit Hash
git_commit_hash.description: The commit this checkpoint points at, or `null` when the app has no committed sandbox revision yet. A checkpoint without one still restores the app state Base44 captured.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Metadata to store on the conversation when this call creates it. Ignored when you already have a conversation with the agent.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The domain to add. A scheme, a trailing slash, and a leading `www.` are removed, and it's stored in lower case.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: Domain to send mail from. It has to already be connected to this app.

sender_name.title: Sender Name
sender_name.description: Name recipients see in the From line.

from_email.title: From Email
from_email.description: Address mail is sent from. Its domain has to be the `domain` you're enabling.

CreateEmailDomainRequest.title: CreateEmailDomainRequest
CreateEmailDomainRequest.description: Request to create email domain configuration.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where setup got to. Only `active` sends mail. The `pending_` values mean setup is still in progress, and the `failed_` values mean it stopped and you can start it again with [Retry email domain setup](/api-reference/retry-email-domain-setup).

email_domain_id.title: Email Domain Id
email_domain_id.description: ID of this app's email configuration. It identifies the configuration, not the individual domain.

external.title: External
external.description: Whether you brought the domain yourself (`true`) or bought it through Base44 (`false`).

dns_records.title: Dns Records
dns_records.description: Records to publish for this domain. They come back even when Base44 publishes them for you, so you can pass them to whoever manages the domain's DNS.

provider_id.title: Provider Id
provider_id.description: Identifier for the registrar the domain sits with, when Base44 knows it.

CreateEmailDomainResponse.title: CreateEmailDomainResponse
CreateEmailDomainResponse.description: Response for creating email domain configuration.

entity_name.title: Entity Name
entity_name.description: Name for the new entity. Letters, numbers, and underscores only. Cannot be `User`.

entity_schema.title: Entity Schema
entity_schema.description: The entity's [JSON Schema](/developers/backend/resources/entities/entity-schemas). Needs `"type": "object"` and a `properties` object, plus any `required` fields and [row-level security rules](/developers/backend/resources/entities/security) under `rls`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Short name for the test.

goal.title: Goal
goal.description: What the testing agent should try to do, in plain language.
goal.example: Sign up, create a project called Launch, and check that it appears on the dashboard.

role.title: Role
role.description: Role to run the test as, such as `admin`. Leave it out to let Base44 pick one from the name or goal.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the group, up to 100 characters. Must be unique among the workspace's custom groups, ignoring case.

description.title: Description
description.description: Short description of the group's purpose, up to 500 characters.
description.example: Product designers

role.title: Role
role.description: Role every member gets: `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`, or `no_access` to block members who get their role only from this group. Leave it out, or send `null`, for a group that grants no role.

member_emails.title: Member Emails
member_emails.description: Emails of active workspace members to add, up to 200.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name for the checkpoint, shown in the app's version history. Send a non-empty value: an empty string is not stored, and the checkpoint is named after the app's most recent chat message instead.

unit_amount.title: Unit Amount
unit_amount.description: Amount in the currency's smallest unit. For USD, `2500` represents $25.00.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code. Converted to lowercase before sending to Stripe. Defaults to `usd`.

recurring_interval.title: Recurring Interval
recurring_interval.description: Billing interval. Use `day`, `week`, `month`, or `year`. Omit it or send `null` for a one-time price. Defaults to `null`.

recurring_interval_count.title: Recurring Interval Count
recurring_interval_count.description: Number of billing intervals between charges. Used only when a recurring interval is supplied. Defaults to 1.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Metadata to store, as string key-value pairs. [Stripe's metadata rules](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) limit it to 50 keys, 40 characters per key, and 500 characters per value. Defaults to `null`.

CreatePriceRequest.title: CreatePriceRequest
CreatePriceRequest.description: Request to create a Stripe price.

name.title: Name
name.description: Product name.

description.title: Description
description.description: Product description. Defaults to `null`.
description.example: Access to weekly classes.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Metadata to store, as string key-value pairs. [Stripe's metadata rules](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) limit it to 50 keys, 40 characters per key, and 500 characters per value. Defaults to `null`.

CreateProductRequest.title: CreateProductRequest
CreateProductRequest.description: Request to create a Stripe product.

target_url.title: Target Url
target_url.description: Public HTTPS URL that receives the events.

events.title: Events
events.description: Events to receive. One or more of `message.created` and `message.completed`.

description.title: Description
description.description: Your label for the webhook.
description.example: CRM sync

generate_secret.title: Generate Secret
generate_secret.description: `true` makes Base44 generate an HMAC-SHA256 signing secret and return it once in the response. Deliveries are signed with an `X-Base44-Signature` header only when the webhook has a secret.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name for the workflow. Must be unique among the app's workflows that are not archived.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the workflow is for, in your own words.
description.example: Sends an email whenever a User record is created.

definition.title: Definition
definition.description: The steps to run, as a CNCF Serverless Workflow v1.0 document. Check it with [Validate a workflow definition](/api-reference/validate-a-workflow-definition) first.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.description: What starts the workflow. The trigger goes inside `config`, whose `trigger_type` picks the kind and whose remaining fields configure it. Add a top-level `condition` to skip a dispatch unless a jq expression over the payload is truthy.

change_summary.title: Change Summary
change_summary.description: Note describing this version, kept in the workflow's version history.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the domain. Pass it as `domain_id` to the other domain endpoints.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The domain name, normalized to lower case with any scheme, trailing slash and leading `www.` removed.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app the domain serves.

disabled.title: Disabled
disabled.description: Whether Base44 has stopped serving the domain. A disabled domain stays attached to the app and keeps its DNS, and serves a placeholder page instead of the app.

last_status_check.title: Last Status Check
last_status_check.description: When [Get custom domain status](/api-reference/get-custom-domain-status) last ran for this domain, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or `null` if it never has.

last_status_payload.description: The provider's last report on the domain, or `null` until a status check has run.

redirect_target_domain.title: Redirect Target Domain
redirect_target_domain.description: The domain that visitors to this one are sent to with a 301 redirect. The value is `null` when this domain serves the app itself.

provider_id.title: Provider Id
provider_id.description: Names the registrar when the domain was bought through Base44's Wix flow. The value is `null` otherwise, which covers both a domain you own elsewhere and one bought through the Entri flow, so this isn't a purchased-versus-external signal.

CustomDomainResource.title: CustomDomainResource
CustomDomainResource.description: A custom domain attached to an app.

verificationStatus.title: Verificationstatus
verificationStatus.description: Whether the provider has verified the domain's DNS. Only `verified` means the domain serves the app, and anything else means it doesn't yet. Absent until [Get custom domain status](/api-reference/get-custom-domain-status) has run once.

CustomDomainStatusPayload.title: CustomDomainStatusPayload
CustomDomainStatusPayload.description: What the hosting provider last reported about the domain.

date.title: Date
date.description: The day these totals cover, as `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC.

payments.title: Payments
payments.description: Paid that day, in the smallest unit of `currency`, so `125000` is 1,250.00 in a currency with two decimal places.

refunds.title: Refunds
refunds.description: Refunded that day, in the smallest unit of `currency`, so `125000` is 1,250.00 in a currency with two decimal places.

disputes.title: Disputes
disputes.description: Lost to disputes that day, in the smallest unit of `currency`, so `125000` is 1,250.00 in a currency with two decimal places.

dispute_count.title: Dispute Count
dispute_count.description: Disputes the customer won that day.

unique_customers.title: Unique Customers
unique_customers.description: Distinct customers who paid that day.

id.title: Id
id.description: The Google Ads campaign ID. This is not the Base44 campaign ID the campaign endpoints take, which is reported as `id` by [List campaigns](/api-reference/list-google-ads-campaigns).

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the campaign.

status.title: Status
status.description: Google Ads campaign status, one of `ENABLED`, `PAUSED`, or `REMOVED`.

campaign_type.title: Campaign Type
campaign_type.description: Google Ads channel type, for example `SEARCH`, `PERFORMANCE_MAX`, or `SMART`.

spend.title: Spend
spend.description: Amount spent in the window, in the account's currency.

conversions_value.title: Conversions Value
conversions_value.description: Total value of those conversions, in the account's currency.

ctr.title: Ctr
ctr.description: Click-through rate for the window, as a percentage. `0` when the campaign had no impressions.

trend.title: Trend
trend.description: Daily series for this campaign. Present when `include_campaign_trend` is true, and always present when Base44 served its own copy of the numbers, which builds it regardless of the flag.

conversion_goals.title: Conversion Goals
conversion_goals.description: This campaign's share of each conversion goal. Absent when Base44 served its own copy of the numbers, and `null` when the goal read failed.

DashboardCampaignRow.title: DashboardCampaignRow
DashboardCampaignRow.description: One campaign's totals for the window.

category.title: Category
category.description: Google Ads conversion category, for example `PURCHASE` or `SUBMIT_LEAD_FORM`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the goal as Google Ads reports it.

conversions.title: Conversions
conversions.description: Conversions recorded against this goal in the window. Goals that recorded nothing are still listed, with `0`.

DashboardConversionGoal.title: DashboardConversionGoal
DashboardConversionGoal.description: One conversion goal on the account, with its count for the window.

spend.title: Spend
spend.description: Amount spent in the window, in the account's currency.

spend_trend.title: Spend Trend
spend_trend.description: Percentage change in spend against the previous window of the same length. `null` when the previous window had no spend to compare against.

impressions_trend.title: Impressions Trend
impressions_trend.description: Percentage change in impressions against the previous window.

clicks_trend.title: Clicks Trend
clicks_trend.description: Percentage change in clicks against the previous window.

conversions.title: Conversions
conversions.description: Conversions in the window. `null` when the account has no conversion tracking configured and recorded none, because the number would read as a real zero.

conversions_trend.title: Conversions Trend
conversions_trend.description: Percentage change in conversions against the previous window. `null` whenever `conversions` is `null`.

roas.title: Roas
roas.description: Return on ad spend: conversion value divided by spend. `0` when nothing was spent.

roas_trend.title: Roas Trend
roas_trend.description: Percentage change in return on ad spend against the previous window.

campaign_breakdown.title: Campaign Breakdown
campaign_breakdown.description: One row per campaign that has metrics in the window, archived campaigns included, so the rows sum to the totals above.

top_search_terms.title: Top Search Terms
top_search_terms.description: Up to four search terms that drove the most clicks in the last 30 days, regardless of the window you asked for. Empty when the term read failed or the account has no campaigns yet.

monthly_spend_cap_micros.title: Monthly Spend Cap Micros
monthly_spend_cap_micros.description: The account's monthly spend cap in micros, or `0` when no cap is set. Absent when the account has no synced campaigns yet.

includes_estimated.title: Includes Estimated
includes_estimated.description: `true` when some rows are Base44's own estimate rather than a figure Google reported.

trend.title: Trend
trend.description: Account-wide daily series for the window. Absent when Base44 served its own copy of the numbers instead of Google's live figures.

conversion_goals.title: Conversion Goals
conversion_goals.description: Every conversion goal on the account with its count for the window. Absent when Base44 served its own copy of the numbers, and `null` when the goal read failed.

DashboardResponse.title: DashboardResponse
DashboardResponse.description: Account-wide totals for the window, plus a per-campaign breakdown.

clicks.title: Clicks
clicks.description: Clicks the term drove in the last 30 days.

DashboardTopSearchTerm.title: DashboardTopSearchTerm
DashboardTopSearchTerm.description: One of the search terms that drove the most clicks in the last 30 days.

clicks.title: Clicks
clicks.description: Clicks across the account that day.

conversions.title: Conversions
conversions.description: Conversions across the account that day.

redirect_url.title: Redirect Url
redirect_url.description: One-time Wix dashboard link. Treat it as a credential and open it in a browser.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: The `mode` the folder was deleted with.

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`. A delete that failed returns an error status instead.

DeleteEntitySchemaResponse.title: DeleteEntitySchemaResponse
DeleteEntitySchemaResponse.description: Confirmation that an entity was removed from the app.

title.title: Title
title.description: The issue's `title`, as the report shows it. Case and punctuation don't matter.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the issue isn't a real problem. Stored for your records only.
reason.example: The dashboard refreshes on a timer, so this is expected.

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`. A delete that doesn't happen returns an error instead.

DeleteSecretResponse.title: DeleteSecretResponse
DeleteSecretResponse.description: Confirmation that the secret was deleted.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the deleted app.

is_deleted.title: Is Deleted
is_deleted.description: Whether the app is in the trash. Always `true` here, because the delete succeeded.

deleted_date.title: Deleted Date
deleted_date.description: Time the app moved to the trash, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format. The 30 day restore window starts here. Deleting an app that is already in the trash reports the original deletion time.

deleted_resources.title: Deleted Resources
deleted_resources.description: Kinds of connected resource this delete released for good, which restoring the app doesn't rebuild. DeletedApp.title: DeletedApp
DeletedApp.description: The app that moved to the trash.

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`.

message.title: Message
message.description: Always `Message deleted`.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the template listing.

status.title: Status
status.description: Review status of the listing: `pending`, `approved`, or `rejected`.

type.title: Type
type.description: Who can see the listing: `public` for every Base44 user, or `workspace` for the app's workspace.

deployed_at.title: Deployed At
deployed_at.description: When the deploy was recorded, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format with no offset.

app_url.title: App Url
app_url.description: The app's published URL on its Base44 domain. A custom domain isn't returned here.

file.title: File
file.description: The build output as a gzipped tar archive, with a file name ending in `.tar.gz`.

checkpoint_id.title: Checkpoint Id
checkpoint_id.description: ID of a specific saved version of the app to deploy. If omitted, the app's current version is deployed.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app that was deployed.

checkpoint_id.title: Checkpoint Id
checkpoint_id.description: ID of the saved version associated with this deploy, or `null` if the app has no saved versions. The git commit hash identifies the exact code that was deployed.

git_commit_hash.title: Git Commit Hash
git_commit_hash.description: Git commit hash of the code that was deployed.

deployed_at.title: Deployed At
deployed_at.description: Time the app was deployed, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

DeployResponse.title: DeployResponse
DeployResponse.description: The version of an app that was published, and when.

email.title: Email
email.description: The app user's email

DeprovisionUserPayload.title: DeprovisionUserPayload
DeprovisionUserPayload.description:
Payload for server-to-server app-user deprovisioning (embedded platforms).

The email travels in the body, not the path: a URL reaches access logs,
proxies and traces, and an address is personal data.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `deleted`.

email.title: Email
email.description: The email, lowercased.

DeprovisionUserResponse.title: DeprovisionUserResponse
DeprovisionUserResponse.description: The app user whose access was removed.

name.title: Name
name.description: The entry's own name, without its parent path.

path.title: Path
path.description: Full path relative to the app root.

type.title: Type
type.description: Whether the entry is a file or a directory.

size.title: Size
size.description: Size in bytes. Present on files, absent on directories.

status.title: Status
status.description: Outcome of the request, which is `disconnected` once it is recorded.

budget_end_confirmed.title: Budget End Confirmed
budget_end_confirmed.description: Whether Google confirmed the account's budget was ended as part of the disconnect. A value of `false` means the disconnect is recorded but the budget wind-down is still in progress.

DisconnectAccountResponse.title: DisconnectAccountResponse
DisconnectAccountResponse.description: Outcome of disconnecting the Google Ads account.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `disconnected`.

DisconnectIntegrationResult.title: DisconnectIntegrationResult
DisconnectIntegrationResult.description: Confirmation that the connector is disconnected from the app.

success.title: Success
success.description: Whether the app was disconnected. Always `true`, because a disconnect that fails returns an error instead.

query.title: Query
query.description: The domain you asked about, normalized to lower case.

results.title: Results
results.description: The domain you asked about, first, followed by up to five suggestions.

DomainAvailabilityCheck.title: DomainAvailabilityCheck
DomainAvailabilityCheck.description: Whether a domain can be registered, with similar domains that can.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The domain this entry is about.

available.title: Available
available.description: Whether Base44 can register the domain (`true`) or not (`false`).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the domain can't be registered, or `null` when it can. Either `premium`, a premium-priced domain Base44 doesn't sell, or `unavailable` for every other reason.

detail.description: What to publish before adding the domain again.

DomainClaimChallenge.title: DomainClaimChallenge
DomainClaimChallenge.description: Another workspace released this domain, so you have to prove you control it.

message.title: Message
message.description: Why the domain can't be added yet.
message.example: This domain is registered to another workspace. Add the TXT record below to prove you control it, then try again.

verification.description: The record to publish at the domain's DNS provider before you retry.

name.title: Name
name.description: Host name to publish the record on.

value.title: Value
value.description: Value to publish. It's issued to your workspace, so another workspace can't use it to claim the domain.

DomainClaimVerification.title: DomainClaimVerification
DomainClaimVerification.description: The DNS record that proves you control the domain.

name.title: Name
name.description: Full name of the record, such as `www.example.com`. If your DNS provider asks for a host rather than a full name, enter the part before your root domain, or `@` for the root domain itself.

value.title: Value
value.description: What the record points to. Enter it exactly as returned.

records.title: Records
records.description: The records to create at the domain's DNS provider, on this page.

pagination.description: Where this page sits in the full list of records.

DomainDnsRecords.title: DomainDnsRecords
DomainDnsRecords.description: The DNS records that point a domain at the app.

message.title: Message
message.description: What happened, in plain text.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Either `wix` or `entri`, the provider whose checkout the Base44 editor shows for a new domain.

DomainPurchaseProvider.title: DomainPurchaseProvider
DomainPurchaseProvider.description: Which provider sells this app's workspace a new domain.

url.title: Url
url.description: Checkout link to open in the browser of the person who'll pay. Treat it as opaque. It works once, so create a new one for each checkout.

DomainPurchaseUrl.title: DomainPurchaseUrl
DomainPurchaseUrl.description: A checkout link for buying a domain.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: Domain to open checkout on, such as `example.com`. Leave it out to open checkout on a domain search.

offer_business_email.title: Offer Business Email
offer_business_email.description: Whether checkout also offers a business email address on the domain after the purchase (`true`) or not (`false`).

can_manage.title: Can Manage
can_manage.description: Whether the workspace's account holds the registration, so its renewal can be managed (`true`) or not (`false`). The value is `null` when Base44 couldn't read the registration.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: When the current registration period ends, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. With `auto_renew` on, the domain renews then. The value is `null` when Base44 couldn't read it.

auto_renew.title: Auto Renew
auto_renew.description: Whether the registration renews automatically (`true`) or lapses at `expires_at` (`false`). The value is `null` when Base44 couldn't read it.

registrations.title: Registrations
registrations.description: One entry per domain bought through Base44 for this app, on this page.

pagination.description: Where this page sits in the full list of registrations.

DomainRegistrations.title: DomainRegistrations
DomainRegistrations.description: The registration status of the app's domains bought through Base44.

resource_name.title: Resource Name
resource_name.description: Google Ads resource name of the link between the asset and the asset group.

field_type.title: Field Type
field_type.description: Which slot the asset fills, as Google reports it, or `null` when Google returned no field type.

primary_status.title: Primary Status
primary_status.description: Google's serving status for the asset, such as `ELIGIBLE`, `LIMITED` or `PENDING`. The value is `null` when Google returned no status.

DurableAssetRow.title: DurableAssetRow
DurableAssetRow.description: One asset already attached to a campaign in Google Ads.

content.title: Content
content.description: Text of the comment, 1 to 5000 characters.
content.example: Make this button match the footer color.

mentioned_emails.title: Mentioned Emails
mentioned_emails.description: Emails of up to 50 people the comment mentions. Mentions send no notification.

EditAppCommentPayload.title: EditAppCommentPayload
EditAppCommentPayload.description: The new text of a comment.

path.title: Path
path.description: The normalized path that was edited.

diff.title: Diff
diff.description: Unified diff of the change, whether or not it was applied.

applied.title: Applied
applied.description: `true` when the file was changed, `false` on a `dry_run` preview.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: Advisories about the write that did not stop it. Absent entirely on a `dry_run`, since nothing was written.

EditFileResult.title: EditFileResult
EditFileResult.description: The diff, and whether it landed.

content.title: Content
content.description: New text for the queued message. Up to 100,000 characters.
content.example: Add a contact form with a phone number field to the home page

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: Who can show the published app in a frame. `anyone` means any site can, `block_all` means no site can, and `allowlist` means only `origins` can.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the policy comes from. `app` is the app's own setting, `workspace` is its workspace's policy, and `default` means neither sets one.

origins.title: Origins
origins.description: Sites allowed to frame the app when `mode` is `allowlist`, or `null` for the other modes.

EffectiveEmbeddingPolicyResult.title: EffectiveEmbeddingPolicyResult
EffectiveEmbeddingPolicyResult.description: A published app's framing policy after its workspace policy is applied.

name.title: Name
name.description: Host the record goes on.

ttl.title: Ttl
ttl.description: Time to live to publish the record with, in seconds.

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether Base44 can see the record yet. Either `pending`, `verified` or `failed`. The value is `null` before the first check.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of this app's email configuration. Every domain in the list repeats it, so tell entries apart by `domain` rather than by this.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The domain mail is sent from.

sender_name.title: Sender Name
sender_name.description: Name recipients see in the From line.

configuration_status.title: Configuration Status
configuration_status.description: Where setup stands. Only `active` sends mail. The `pending_` values mean setup is still in progress, and the `failed_` values mean it stopped and you can start it again with [Retry email domain setup](/api-reference/retry-email-domain-setup).

enabled_at.title: Enabled At
enabled_at.description: When the domain finished verifying, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or `null` if it hasn't verified yet.

suspended_reason.title: Suspended Reason
suspended_reason.description: Why sending was suspended, when it was. The value is `null` on a domain in good standing.

external.title: External
external.description: Whether you brought the domain yourself (`true`) or bought it through Base44 (`false`).

dns_records.title: Dns Records
dns_records.description: Records this domain needs, with whether Base44 can see each one yet.

provider_id.title: Provider Id
provider_id.description: Identifier for the registrar the domain sits with, when Base44 knows it.

EmailDomainInfo.title: EmailDomainInfo
EmailDomainInfo.description: Email domain info for get endpoint.

EmbedTarget.title: EmbedTarget
EmbedTarget.description:
The surfaces a platform may frame, named by their ``UrlType``.

A subset rather than ``UrlType`` itself: the rest of that enum is either
internal (``platform``, ``pentest``) or addresses a revision, and a public
payload should not offer what it will only refuse.

email.title: Email
email.description: The app user's email

target.description: Which of the app's surfaces to frame: live_site (the default, the published app), latest_preview (main's static build) or live_preview (the running sandbox).

EmbedTokenPayload.title: EmbedTokenPayload
EmbedTokenPayload.description: The app user to mint for, and which of the app's surfaces to frame.

token.title: Token
token.description: The single-use sign-in token. Already on `embed_url`; you don't need to send it anywhere yourself.

embed_url.title: Embed Url
embed_url.description: The chosen surface's address with the token on it. Load it in an iframe.

EmbedTokenResponse.title: EmbedTokenResponse
EmbedTokenResponse.description: A single-use sign-in token, and the URL that spends it.

client_secret.title: Client Secret
client_secret.description: Token that mounts Stripe's embedded checkout in a browser. It is meant for client-side use and is scoped to this one session, so it is not a secret key, but it does let whoever holds it complete this card setup.

publishable_key.title: Publishable Key
publishable_key.description: Base44's Stripe publishable key, which the embedded checkout needs. It is public by design.

EmbeddedPaymentSetupSession.title: EmbeddedPaymentSetupSession
EmbeddedPaymentSetupSession.description: A Stripe Checkout session for saving a card inside your own page.

raw_prompt.title: Raw Prompt
raw_prompt.description: The image prompt to rewrite, in the caller's own words. Empty or whitespace-only returns an empty result without running a model.

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether anything reached Google. The value is `success` when at least one adjustment landed and `no_rows_uploaded` when none did, so it does not tell you the whole batch landed.

total_uploaded.title: Total Uploaded
total_uploaded.description: How many adjustments Google accepted. Anything short of `total_submitted` is made up of adjustments dropped for carrying no usable hashed identifier and adjustments Google rejected one by one, and the response does not separate the two.

EnhancedConversionUploadResult.title: EnhancedConversionUploadResult
EnhancedConversionUploadResult.description: What happened to a batch of enhanced-conversion adjustments.

count.title: Count
count.description: Number of records you can read in this entity.

EntityCountResponse.title: EntityCountResponse
EntityCountResponse.description: The number of records stored in one of an app's entities.

entity_name.title: Entity Name
entity_name.description: Name of the entity. The name `User` is the built-in user entity, and every other name is one the app defines.

entity_schema.title: Entity Schema
entity_schema.description: The entity's stored [JSON Schema](/developers/backend/resources/entities/entity-schemas), including its `properties`, `required` fields, and any [row-level security rules](/developers/backend/resources/entities/security) under `rls`. For the app's own entities it also carries a `name` key holding the entity name. For `User` it holds only the custom fields added on top of the built-in ones, and has no `name` key.

entity_schema.title: Entity Schema
entity_schema.description: The entity's stored [JSON Schema](/developers/backend/resources/entities/entity-schemas), including its `properties`, `required` fields, and any [row-level security rules](/developers/backend/resources/entities/security) under `rls`. For the app's own entities it also carries a `name` key holding the entity name. For `User` it holds only the custom fields added on top of the built-in ones, and has no `name` key.

EntitySchemaResponse.title: EntitySchemaResponse
EntitySchemaResponse.description: One of an app's entities and its stored JSON Schema.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the event, as the app tracked it.

count.title: Count
count.description: Number of times the event was recorded across the retained history.

EventNameInfo.title: EventNameInfo
EventNameInfo.description: Information about a tracked event name.

event_names.title: Event Names
event_names.description: The app's event names, most frequent first.

EventNamesResponse.title: EventNamesResponse
EventNamesResponse.description: The analytics event names an app has recorded.

event_name.title: Event Name
event_name.description: Name of the event the property keys belong to.

property_keys.title: Property Keys
property_keys.description: Property keys the app has sent with this event. Prefix a key with `properties.` to filter, aggregate, or group by it, which works for keys made up of letters, digits, and underscores.

EventPropertyKeysResponse.title: EventPropertyKeysResponse
EventPropertyKeysResponse.description: The property keys an app has sent with one analytics event.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email the invitation was for.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why it wasn't sent. Its wording can change, so don't parse it.
error.example: User already has a pending invitation

path.title: Path
path.description: Path of the file, relative to the app root.

content.title: Content
content.description: The file's full text.

paths.title: Paths
paths.description: Path of each file, relative to the app root.

FileList.title: FileList
FileList.description: The paths of the app's source files.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app the test belongs to.

name.title: Name
name.description: Short name of the test.

goal.title: Goal
goal.description: What the testing agent tries to do, in plain language.
goal.example: Sign up, create a project called Launch, and check that it appears on the dashboard.

role.title: Role
role.description: Role set on the test, or `null` when none is set. A test without one can still run as a role its name or goal names. The run's `flow_role` shows the role actually used.

source.title: Source
source.description: `manual` for a test you created, `app_context` for one Base44 generated from the app.

revision.title: Revision
revision.description: Starts at 1 and goes up each time the test is edited.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the test was created, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

updated_date.title: Updated Date
updated_date.description: When the test last changed, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

FlowResponse.title: FlowResponse
FlowResponse.description: A test: a goal the testing agent tries to accomplish in a browser.

time.title: Time
time.description: When the line was logged, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

level.title: Level
level.description: Severity of the line, such as `info`, `warn`, or `error`.

message.title: Message
message.description: What the function wrote. An uncaught error carries its name, message and stack trace. Each invocation also gets a line of its own with the request method and response status, like `POST → 200`.

FunctionLogLine.title: FunctionLogLine
FunctionLogLine.description: One line a backend function logged.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: ID of this generation. Pass it as `session_id` to [List Google Ads generated assets](/api-reference/list-google-ads-generated-assets) to poll for the images that are still coming.

text.title: Text
text.description: The copy that was generated. Empty when the text engine produced nothing and when a generation for this app was already running.

images.title: Images
images.description: The pictures that finished in time to be returned inline. The rest are counted in `background_image_count`.

background_image_count.title: Background Image Count
background_image_count.description: How many more pictures are still being generated for this session. The response comes back as soon as the copy is done, so poll [List Google Ads generated assets](/api-reference/list-google-ads-generated-assets) with `session_id` for these. The field is absent when a generation for this app was already running, which is how you tell that case apart.

language.title: Language
language.description: Language the copy was written in, as a lowercase two-letter code. It comes from the app's own site rather than from anything you send. The field is absent when a generation for this app was already running.

business_name.title: Business Name
business_name.description: Name of the business the ads are for.

business_description.title: Business Description
business_description.description: What the business sells, in a sentence or two. The more specific this is, the better the copy.
business_description.example: Handmade solid oak dining tables, built to order in San Francisco.

keywords.title: Keywords
keywords.description: Words the copy should lean on.

landing_page_url.title: Landing Page Url
landing_page_url.description: Page the ads send people to. Used as context for the copy.

campaign_goal.title: Campaign Goal
campaign_goal.description: What the campaign is for: `traffic`, `leads` or `sales`.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: ID of this generation. Pass it as `session_id` to [List Google Ads generated assets](/api-reference/list-google-ads-generated-assets) to collect the pictures that are still coming.

assets.title: Assets
assets.description: The pictures that finished in time to be returned inline. Empty when nothing landed in time, when the engine produced nothing, and when a generation for this app was already running, which `in_flight` tells apart.

background_pending.title: Background Pending
background_pending.description: Present and `true` when more pictures are still being generated under this `session_id`, including when `assets` came back empty because the first one took too long. Absent on a lock-miss response.

background_count.title: Background Count
background_count.description: How many more pictures are still being generated. Absent on a lock-miss response.

in_flight.title: In Flight
in_flight.description: Present and `true` only when an image generation for this app was already running, in which case `session_id` is that run's and `assets` is empty. Poll the returned `session_id` rather than retrying. The field is absent on every other response.

GenerateImageAssetsResult.title: GenerateImageAssetsResult
GenerateImageAssetsResult.description: The pictures one image generation produced.

scheduled_post_id.title: Scheduled Post Id
scheduled_post_id.description: Optional calendar post ID from List scheduled posts. Its source_post_id must match the post_id in the URL. Updates the calendar row rather than the original plan; requires Social Calendar V2. Only proposal and scheduled posts can be edited.

image_prompt.title: Image Prompt
image_prompt.description: Prompt to generate the image from. Used only when the post carries no `image_prompt` of its own, which is the prompt the plan generated for it. Send the post's own `image_prompt` back if you want to be sure of what is used.
image_prompt.example: A freelancer closing a laptop at a tidy desk, warm morning light

refinement_instruction.title: Refinement Instruction
refinement_instruction.description: What to change about the existing image. Sending this regenerates the image even when the post already has one. The first 300 characters are used.
refinement_instruction.example: Make the lighting cooler and remove the coffee cup.

platforms.title: Platforms
platforms.description: Platforms to generate content for, 1 to 3 of `x`, `instagram`, `tiktok`, `linkedin`, `reddit`, `facebook`. The order is preserved in the response. Unsupported values are ignored, and a request where none are supported fails with a 400.

social_url.title: Social Url
social_url.description: HTTPS URL of your social profile, used to match the writing voice of the generated content. Omit it to reuse the voice resolved when you submitted answers.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: ID of this generation. Pass it as `session_id` to [List Google Ads generated assets](/api-reference/list-google-ads-generated-assets), or to [Accept a generated Google Ads asset](/api-reference/accept-a-generated-google-ads-asset) with one of the returned `session_asset_id` values.

assets.title: Assets
assets.description: The copy that was generated, one entry per line. Empty when the engine produced nothing and when a generation for this app was already running, which `in_flight` tells apart.

language.title: Language
language.description: Language the copy was written in, as a lowercase two-letter code. It comes from the app's own site rather than from anything you send. The field is absent on a lock-miss response unless you asked for a specific campaign.

in_flight.title: In Flight
in_flight.description: Present and `true` only when a text generation for this app was already running, in which case `session_id` is that run's and `assets` is empty. Poll the returned `session_id` rather than retrying. The field is absent on every other response.

GenerateTextAssetsResult.title: GenerateTextAssetsResult
GenerateTextAssetsResult.description: The copy one text generation produced.

session_asset_id.title: Session Asset Id
session_asset_id.description: ID of this asset within the session. Pass it as `session_asset_id` to [Accept a generated Google Ads asset](/api-reference/accept-a-generated-google-ads-asset).

asset_field_type.title: Asset Field Type
asset_field_type.description: Which slot on the ad this asset fills. Text assets are `HEADLINE`, `LONG_HEADLINE` or `DESCRIPTION`. Image assets are `MARKETING_IMAGE`, `SQUARE_MARKETING_IMAGE`, `PORTRAIT_MARKETING_IMAGE` or `TALL_PORTRAIT_MARKETING_IMAGE`.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Whether the asset is copy (`text`) or a picture (`image`).

text.title: Text
text.description: The generated copy, or `null` on an image asset.
text.example: Handmade oak furniture, built to last

image_url.title: Image Url
image_url.description: URL of the generated picture, or `null` on a text asset. It is a Base44 preview URL, not a Google one, and it stops resolving once the asset is cleaned up.

source.title: Source
source.description: Which engine wrote it. The value is `google` for Google's own asset generation and `inhouse` for the Base44 model that covers languages Google does not generate for, and that stands in when Google's call fails.

language.title: Language
language.description: Language of a text asset as a lowercase two-letter code, or `null` on an image, because image assets carry no copy.

channel_type.title: Channel Type
channel_type.description: Campaign type the asset was generated for, one of `SEARCH`, `PERFORMANCE_MAX`, `DISPLAY` or `DEMAND_GEN`.

GeneratedAssetSummary.title: GeneratedAssetSummary
GeneratedAssetSummary.description: One generated asset in a live generation session.

session.title: Session
session.description: Assets in the generation session you asked for. Present only when you send `session_id`, and an empty list while the generation is still running or when it produced nothing.

library.title: Library
library.description: The app's generated assets, newest first, capped at the 5,000 most recent. Present only when you omit `session_id`. There is no pagination and nothing marks a truncated list, so an app past 5,000 assets silently stops seeing its oldest ones.

durable.title: Durable
durable.description: Assets already attached to the campaign in Google Ads. Present only when you send `campaign_id`.

GeneratedAssetsList.title: GeneratedAssetsList
GeneratedAssetsList.description: The app's generated Google Ads creative.

flows.title: Flows
flows.description: The saved tests, up to 5. Empty when `no_changes` is `true`.

example.goal: Sign up, create a project called Launch, and check that it appears on the dashboard.
example.name: Create a project

no_changes.title: No Changes
no_changes.description: `true` when the app has no pages or entities yet, so nothing was generated or charged.

GitHubConnectionStatus.title: GitHubConnectionStatus
GitHubConnectionStatus.description:
Health of an app's GitHub repository connection.

- `active` works normally.
- `disconnected` was disconnected by a user.
- `error` hit a technical failure.
- `revoked` means the GitHub App access was withdrawn.

id.title: Id
id.description: GitHub's numeric ID for the account.

login.title: Login
login.description: GitHub username or organization name. Pass it as `org_name` to [Connect a GitHub repository](/api-reference/connect-a-github-repository).

avatar_url.title: Avatar Url
avatar_url.description: URL of the account's GitHub profile picture.

installation_id.title: Installation Id
installation_id.description: ID of the Base44 GitHub App installation on this account. Pass it as `installation_id` to [Connect a GitHub repository](/api-reference/connect-a-github-repository).

type.title: Type
type.description: Either `User` for your personal account or `Organization` for an organization.

repository_selection.title: Repository Selection
repository_selection.description: Whether the Base44 GitHub App can reach all repositories in this account or only chosen ones. Either `all` or `selected`. You can't create a new repository under an account set to `selected`, so switch that account to all repositories in GitHub first, under Settings > Applications > Base44 > Repository access.

missing_pr_automation_permissions.title: Missing Pr Automation Permissions
missing_pr_automation_permissions.description: GitHub App permissions required for PR automation but not granted.

missing_pr_automation_events.title: Missing Pr Automation Events
missing_pr_automation_events.description: GitHub App webhook subscriptions required for PR automation but absent.

GitHubOrganization.title: GitHubOrganization
GitHubOrganization.description: A GitHub account, personal or organization, with the Base44 GitHub App installed.

synced.title: Synced
synced.description: Whether this call applied new commits to the app.

already_up_to_date.title: Already Up To Date
already_up_to_date.description: Whether the repository's head was already the last commit Base44 pulled, so there was nothing to do.

commits_pulled.title: Commits Pulled
commits_pulled.description: How many commits `commits` holds, so commits Base44 pushed itself aren't counted. The value is `0` when nothing was pulled.

latest_commit_hash.title: Latest Commit Hash
latest_commit_hash.description: Repository head after the pull, or `null` when nothing was pulled.

commits.title: Commits
commits.description: The commits this call applied, oldest first. Commits Base44 pushed itself are left out, so a pull of only those comes back with an empty list.

files_summary.description: Change counts for the pulled commits, or `null` when nothing was pulled.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why the pull didn't happen, or `null` when it succeeded. See [Pull error codes](/developers/references/apps-api/sections/github#pull-error-codes) for the possible values.

error_message.title: Error Message
error_message.description: Human-readable explanation of `error`, or `null` when the pull succeeded.
error_message.example: Merge conflict while applying the pulled commits

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: How long the pull took, in milliseconds, or `null` when Base44 recorded no duration for it.

GitHubPullResult.title: GitHubPullResult
GitHubPullResult.description: Outcome of a pull from the connected repository.

short_sha.title: Short Sha
short_sha.description: Short form of the commit SHA.

message.title: Message
message.description: Commit message.

author_name.title: Author Name
author_name.description: The author's GitHub username when GitHub reports one, otherwise the name recorded in the commit.

author_email.title: Author Email
author_email.description: Email recorded as the commit's author, or `null` when GitHub doesn't report one.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: When the commit was authored, in ISO 8601.

url.title: Url
url.description: URL of the commit on GitHub.

GitHubPulledCommit.title: GitHubPulledCommit
GitHubPulledCommit.description: One commit brought in by a pull.

total_files.title: Total Files
total_files.description: Files changed across the pulled commits.

files_with_content.title: Files With Content
files_with_content.description: Changed files whose new content Base44 applied to the app.

files_metadata_only.title: Files Metadata Only
files_metadata_only.description: Changed files Base44 recorded without their content, because GitHub didn't return a usable diff for them.

files_deleted.title: Files Deleted
files_deleted.description: Files removed from the app by the pull.

total_additions.title: Total Additions
total_additions.description: Lines added across the pulled commits.

total_deletions.title: Total Deletions
total_deletions.description: Lines removed across the pulled commits.

GitHubPulledFiles.title: GitHubPulledFiles
GitHubPulledFiles.description: How much the pulled commits changed.

success.title: Success
success.description: Whether the push succeeded.

commit_hash.title: Commit Hash
commit_hash.description: Commit pushed to the repository, or `null` when nothing was pushed.

commits_pushed.title: Commits Pushed
commits_pushed.description: Whether the push moved the repository forward. The value is `false` both when the repository already had this commit and when nothing was pushed at all.

skipped.title: Skipped
skipped.description: Whether the push was skipped. This is `true` for exactly one reason, which is that the connection carries no GitHub App installation. Every other reason nothing was pushed comes back `false`, including no connection at all and a connection in `error` or `revoked`, so read `error` rather than this flag.

error.title: Error
error.description: Why the push didn't happen, or `null` when it succeeded. Plain text, not a code you can branch on.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: How long the push took, in milliseconds, or `null` when Base44 rejected the request before starting one.

GitHubPushResult.title: GitHubPushResult
GitHubPushResult.description: Outcome of a push to the connected repository.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description:
Which side Base44 brought up to date. The value is one of:
- `none`: The two already matched.
- `base44_to_github`: Base44 pushed the app's newer commits.
- `github_to_base44`: Base44 pulled the repository's newer commits.

repo_url.title: Repo Url
repo_url.description: URL of the repository on GitHub.

base44_head.title: Base44 Head
base44_head.description: The app's latest commit when the reconnect started.

github_head.title: Github Head
github_head.description: Head of the repository's default branch when the reconnect started.
