preview_url.description: Where the app is served as it currently stands in the app editor, including changes that haven't been published. Usually a host with no scheme, so add `https://` before you open it in a browser or an iframe. For some imported apps it's already a full URL with its own query parameters, so add the scheme only when it's missing and keep the query.

preview_token.description: Short-lived token the preview URL needs to authenticate against the preview proxy. It works once and expires after 5 minutes. sandbox_info.description: Details of the sandbox serving this preview, including whether it had to be started for this request.

bridge_injected.title: Bridge Injected
bridge_injected.description: Whether the preview host injects the builder bridge. False when the platform proxy is disabled and the preview falls back to the sandbox's own host, so the editor knows the bridge's mount/paint signals will never arrive and must not wait for them.

PreviewUrlResponse.title: PreviewUrlResponse
PreviewUrlResponse.description: A preview URL for an app, and the sandbox serving it.

repo_url.title: Repo Url
repo_url.description: URL of the repository on GitHub.

org_name.title: Org Name
org_name.description: GitHub username or organization that owns the repository.

PreviousRepository.title: PreviousRepository
PreviousRepository.description: The repository an app was connected to before a user disconnected it.

code.title: Code

currency_code.description: Currency of the amounts, as an ISO 4217 code.

amount_micros.title: Amount Micros

used_micros.title: Used Micros
used_micros.description: How much of it has been spent, in micros.

expires_at.title: Expires At

spendable.title: Spendable

already_configured.title: Already Configured

PublicPaginationInfo.description: Pagination metadata for a cursor-paginated page.

limit.title: Limit

QueuedMessage.title: QueuedMessage

user_ids.title: User Ids

content.title: Content

start_line.title: Start Line
start_line.description: First line included, 1-based. Absent when this path failed.

end_line.title: End Line
end_line.description: Last line included, 1-based. Absent when this path failed.

total_lines.title: Total Lines
total_lines.description: How many lines the whole file has, so you can tell whether you received all of it. Absent when this path failed.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: `true` when this entry was cut short, either by your `limit` or by the 1 MB per-file cap. Absent when this path failed.

error.description: Why this path could not be read, and absent when it could. Its presence is what marks a failed entry.

ReadFileEntry.title: ReadFileEntry
ReadFileEntry.description:
One path from a read request: either its contents or why it failed.

Every field except ``path`` is absent-able, because an entry is one of two
shapes. A successful read carries the five content fields and no ``error``;
a failed one carries ``error`` and nothing else.

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable machine-readable reason, from the same taxonomy the error responses use: `NOT_FOUND`, `BINARY_FILE`, `PATH_OUTSIDE_SANDBOX`, `PROTECTED_PATH`, `READ_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` or `BACKEND_ERROR`. Branch on this rather than on the message.

message.title: Message
message.description: Human-readable explanation for this path.

ReadFileError.title: ReadFileError
ReadFileError.description: Why one path in the batch could not be read.

files.title: Files
files.description: One entry per requested path, in request order. Each is either a successful read or an error for that path, so check for `error` before reading `content`.

ReadFileResult.title: ReadFileResult
ReadFileResult.description: The files you asked for, in the order you asked for them.

read_at.title: Read At
read_at.description: The read time recorded for you, in UTC.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: Transaction time in UTC as returned by the analytics store. The string can omit an explicit timezone offset.

action.title: Action
action.description: What this entry represents. Either `payment`, `refund`, or `dispute_lost`.

status.title: Status
status.description: Display status derived from the action. `payment` becomes `succeeded`, `refund` becomes `refunded`, and `dispute_lost` becomes `failed`. Other actions retain their action value. Defaults to an empty string.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Amount in the currency's smallest unit. Read `action` to tell an incoming payment from an outgoing refund or dispute loss. Defaults to `0`.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Currency code recorded with the transaction. Defaults to `usd`.

customer_id.title: Customer Id
customer_id.description: Provider customer ID, or `null` when none was recorded. Defaults to `null`.

transaction_id.title: Transaction Id
transaction_id.description: Provider transaction ID, or `null` when none was recorded. Defaults to `null`.

customer_name.title: Customer Name
customer_name.description: Customer name when provider enrichment succeeds, or `null` when unavailable. Defaults to `null`.

customer_email.title: Customer Email
customer_email.description: Customer email when provider enrichment succeeds, or `null` when unavailable. Defaults to `null`.

is_live.title: Is Live
is_live.description: Whether this entry was recorded in live mode. Defaults to `true`.

RecentTransactionResponse.title: RecentTransactionResponse
RecentTransactionResponse.description: A recent transaction with optional customer details.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.description: Recent payments, refunds, and disputes, newest first. Empty when none match.

exclude_admins.title: Exclude Admins
exclude_admins.description: `true` to leave visits by the app's owners and admins out of recording, `false` to record them too.

sampling_rate.title: Sampling Rate
sampling_rate.description: Share of eligible visits to record, from `0` to `1` in steps of `0.05`. `1` records every visit.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether recordings are on. Reads `false` when they were turned on but the app has since moved to another owner or workspace, or the owner's plan no longer includes recordings.

enabled_at.title: Enabled At
enabled_at.description: When recordings were turned on, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or `null` when they're off. A value read back carries no offset, and the response right after turning recordings on carries `+00:00`. The response to turning recordings off keeps the previous value.

enabled_by.title: Enabled By
enabled_by.description: Email of the user who turned recordings on, or `null` when they're off. The response to turning recordings off keeps the previous value.

exclude_admins.title: Exclude Admins
exclude_admins.description: Whether visits by the app's owners and admins are left out of recording.

sampling_rate.title: Sampling Rate
sampling_rate.description: Share of eligible visits that get recorded, from `0` to `1`. `1` records every visit.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: `true` to turn recordings on, `false` to turn them off.

description.title: Description
description.description: Rough description of what to test, in your own words.
description.example: check that new projects show up on the dashboard

scheduled_post_id.title: Scheduled Post Id
scheduled_post_id.description: Optional calendar post ID from List scheduled posts. Its source_post_id must match the post_id in the URL. Updates the calendar row rather than the original plan; requires Social Calendar V2. Only proposal and scheduled posts can be edited.

request.title: Request
request.description: What to change about the post, in your own words. Can't be empty.
request.example: Make it shorter and drop the emoji.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.description: What to change about the current strategy, in your own words. Can't be empty.
feedback.example: Focus on freelancers rather than agencies, and keep the tone less formal.

name.title: Name
name.description: Short name for the test.

goal.title: Goal
goal.description: The goal, rewritten as steps the testing agent can follow.
goal.example: Sign up, create a project called Launch, and check that it appears on the dashboard.

RefinedTestDescription.title: RefinedTestDescription
RefinedTestDescription.description: A test name and goal written from a rough description.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Amount to refund, in the smallest unit of the payment's own currency, so `1000` is $10.00 for a USD payment. Must be above `0`.

note.title: Note
note.description: Private note stored with the refund, up to 500 characters. Defaults to `null`.

idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key
idempotency_key.description: Key you generate for this refund attempt, up to 100 characters. Keep it the same across retries of one attempt, and use a new one for each new refund. Required unless you send it in the `Idempotency-Key` header instead.

RefundTransactionRequest.title: RefundTransactionRequest
RefundTransactionRequest.description: A refund of all or part of one payment.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the app. The remix is named after it with ` (Copy)` appended, except for an approved template, where it takes the name of the approved version.

app_type.title: App Type
app_type.description: Type of the app. Only `slide`, `user_agent`, `user_app`, `user_game` apps can be remixed.

user_description.title: User Description
user_description.description: Description of the app, or `null` if none was set.
user_description.example: A CRM to track leads and deals

requires_backend_functions.title: Requires Backend Functions
requires_backend_functions.description: Whether the app has deployed backend functions, which the remix copies.

app_secret_names.title: App Secret Names
app_secret_names.description: Names of the secrets set on the app. The remix doesn't copy their values, except the ones in `shared_secrets`, so pass the rest in `secret_values`.

shared_secrets.title: Shared Secrets
shared_secrets.description: Names of the secrets the remix copies automatically, values included. Only an approved workspace template shares secrets, and only with members who can edit in the workspace and aren't the app's owner, collaborators, or workspace admins. Empty otherwise.

is_admin.title: Is Admin
is_admin.description: Whether you are an editor-level collaborator on the app or an admin of its workspace. You can set `with_chat_history` when this is `true`, and also when you own the app.

RemixRequirements.title: RemixRequirements
RemixRequirements.description: What remixing an app involves, before you remix it.

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`.

RemoveCollaboratorResult.title: RemoveCollaboratorResult
RemoveCollaboratorResult.description: The result of removing a collaborator.

unlinked.title: Unlinked
unlinked.description: Always `true`, including when the app wasn't in the folder.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app, in lowercase.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `removed`.

RemoveIntegrationResult.title: RemoveIntegrationResult
RemoveIntegrationResult.description: Confirmation that the connector is removed from the app.

item_ids.title: Item Ids
item_ids.description: IDs of queued messages in the order you want them to run. IDs not in the queue are ignored, and queued messages you leave out keep their order after the ones you list. Each ID can appear once.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: Domain to move to. It has to be connected to this app and different from the current one.

sender_name.title: Sender Name
sender_name.description: Name recipients see in the From line.

from_email.title: From Email
from_email.description: Address mail is sent from once the new domain verifies.

ReplaceEmailDomainRequest.title: ReplaceEmailDomainRequest
ReplaceEmailDomainRequest.description: Request to replace email domain with a new one.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the new domain's setup got to. Only `active` sends mail, and the old domain keeps sending until this reads it. The `pending_` values mean setup is still in progress, and the `failed_` values mean it stopped and you can start it again with [Retry email domain setup](/api-reference/retry-email-domain-setup).

email_domain_id.title: Email Domain Id
email_domain_id.description: ID of this app's email configuration. It identifies the configuration, not the individual domain.

external.title: External
external.description: Whether you brought the new domain yourself (`true`) or bought it through Base44 (`false`).

dns_records.title: Dns Records
dns_records.description: Records to publish for the new domain.

content.title: Content
content.description: Text of the comment, 1 to 5000 characters.
content.example: Done, thanks!

mentioned_emails.title: Mentioned Emails
mentioned_emails.description: Emails of up to 50 people the comment mentions. Mentions send no notification.

ReplyToAppCommentPayload.title: ReplyToAppCommentPayload
ReplyToAppCommentPayload.description: A reply to a comment thread.

connection_id.title: Connection Id
connection_id.description: ID of the connection Base44 stored for this app.

repo_url.title: Repo Url
repo_url.description: URL of the repository on GitHub.

clone_urls.description: URLs and CLI command for cloning the new repository.

default_branch.title: Default Branch
default_branch.description: Default branch of the new repository. Base44 pushes the app's code to this branch.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email the pending invitation was sent to.

ResendInviteRequest.title: ResendInviteRequest
ResendInviteRequest.description: A pending invitation to send again.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `ok` when the reset is applied.

ResetResponse.title: ResetResponse
ResetResponse.description: Confirmation that the app's social content flow was cleared.

status.description: How the run ended. A value of `resolved` published the resolution, `apply_pending` is still applying it, `needs_input` is waiting for an answer in the app's chat, `conflict` left the conflicts in place, and `failed` produced no outcome.

title.title: Title
title.description: The issue's `title`, as the report shows it. Case and punctuation don't matter.

needs_full_name.title: Needs Full Name
needs_full_name.description: Whether onboarding still needs a first and last name.

first_name.title: First Name
first_name.description: Resolved first name, or `null` when a complete name could not be found. Defaults to `null`.

last_name.title: Last Name
last_name.description: Resolved last name, or `null` when a complete name could not be found. Defaults to `null`.

ResolveOutcome.title: ResolveOutcome
ResolveOutcome.description: Final status of a conflict-resolution run.

resolved_at.title: Resolved At
resolved_at.description: When the thread was resolved, in UTC.

reverted.title: Reverted
reverted.description: Records put back to the values they had at the checkpoint.

deleted.title: Deleted
deleted.description: Records created after the checkpoint, moved to the entity's trash.

reinserted.title: Reinserted
reinserted.description: Records deleted after the checkpoint, brought back.

RestoreCounts.title: RestoreCounts
RestoreCounts.description: How many records a restore changed in one entity.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the build stands when the call returns. Either `building` (the build started in the background), `ready` (the checkpoint's commit was already built, so nothing was rebuilt), or `skipped` (the app was imported from an external repository, and those apps have no preview build).

git_commit_hash.title: Git Commit Hash
git_commit_hash.description: Git commit hash of the code being built, the same as the checkpoint's `git_commit_hash`.

RetryCheckpointBuildResponse.title: RetryCheckpointBuildResponse
RetryCheckpointBuildResponse.description: Where a checkpoint's preview build stands when the call returns.

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`. A review that doesn't happen returns an error instead.

message.title: Message
message.description: `Access request approved` or `Access request denied`.

ReviewAccessRequestResponse.title: ReviewAccessRequestResponse
ReviewAccessRequestResponse.description: Doc-only: the handler returns a plain dict with exactly these keys.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email of the person.

status.title: Status
status.description: `completed` when the person was added to the app, `approved` when they join once they sign up, or `denied`.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it wasn't fixed. `no_scan` means the app has no scan result from the current scanner, so run [Run security scan](/api-reference/run-security-scan) first. `no_recommendation` means the latest result holds no recommendation for the entity, because it never had one or it was already resolved. `entity_not_found` means the app no longer has the entity. `write_failed` means saving the rules failed, though some of them may have landed, and the recommendation is kept so you can retry.

RlsFixFailure.title: RlsFixFailure
RlsFixFailure.description: One entity whose recommended rules weren't applied.

entity_names.title: Entity Names
entity_names.description: Entities to fix, as returned in `rls_recommendations` by [Get security scan](/api-reference/get-security-scan). Name at least one and at most 100. A name listed twice is applied once.

record_security_fix_chat.title: Record Security Fix Chat
record_security_fix_chat.description: Whether to add the fix to the app's AI chat and save a checkpoint of the app first (`true`) or apply it with neither (`false`). Defaults to `true`.

security_fix_total_count.title: Security Fix Total Count
security_fix_total_count.description: When you split one fix across several calls, the total number of entities across all of them. It's used only in the chat message, and ignored unless it's larger than the number of names in `entity_names`.

RlsFixRequest.title: RlsFixRequest
RlsFixRequest.description: Which entities to apply the recommended row-level security rules to.

fixed.title: Fixed
fixed.description: Entities whose `rls` now holds the recommended rules. An entity can also appear in `failed` as `no_recommendation` when a newer scan replaced its recommendation while the rules were being applied.

failed.title: Failed
failed.description: Entities that weren't fixed, each with the reason.

RlsFixResponse.title: RlsFixResponse
RlsFixResponse.description: Which entities got their recommended row-level security rules.

stdout.title: Stdout
stdout.description: Everything the command wrote to standard output.

stderr.title: Stderr
stderr.description: Everything the command wrote to standard error. Populated on success too, since many tools log there.

exit_code.title: Exit Code
exit_code.description: The command's exit status. `0` means success. A non-zero status is still a 200 from this endpoint: the command ran and failed, which is not a request error.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: `true` when the output hit the 1 MB cap and was cut short. `stdout` and `stderr` are each capped, and either one hitting it sets this.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: How long the command took, in milliseconds.

workflow_id.title: Workflow Id
workflow_id.description: ID of the workflow that ran.

workflow_name.title: Workflow Name
workflow_name.description: Name of that workflow at the time of the run.

trigger_type.title: Trigger Type
trigger_type.description: What started the run: `scheduled`, `entity`, `connector`, `in_app_agent`, `app_user_auth`, `app_publish`, `app_payment`, `webhook`, or `goal_file`. See [Triggers](/developers/references/apps-api/sections/workflows#triggers) for what each one fires on. A run started through [Run a workflow now](/api-reference/run-a-workflow-now) with no payload to replay reports `manual` instead.

status.title: Status
status.description: How the run is going: `running`, `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. See [Workflow status](/developers/references/apps-api/sections/workflows#workflow-status) for how this compares to the workflow's own status.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When the run started, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

completed_at.title: Completed At
completed_at.description: When the run finished, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. This is `null` while it is still running.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: How long the run took, in milliseconds.

error_message.title: Error Message
error_message.description: Why the run failed. This is `null` when it did not fail.
error_message.example: The email step failed because the recipient address was missing.

is_test_run.title: Is Test Run
is_test_run.description: This is `true` when the run was started by hand rather than by its trigger.

ai_analysis.title: Ai Analysis
ai_analysis.description: Stored failure explanation, once [Analyze a failed workflow run](/api-reference/analyze-a-failed-workflow-run) has generated one. This is `null` until then.
ai_analysis.example: The email step failed because the recipient address was missing from the trigger payload.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The tasks the run executed, in order. Each carries `task_name`, `task_type`, `status`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `duration_ms` and `error_message`, plus the data that went into and came out of the step, whose shape is whatever your workflow passes around.

status_reason.title: Status Reason
status_reason.description: Why the run failed or was cancelled. Empty on runs that finished successfully.

definition_version_id.title: Definition Version Id
definition_version_id.description: Version the run executed, which can be older than the workflow's current one. Read it with [Get workflow version](/api-reference/get-workflow-version).

workflow_id.title: Workflow Id
workflow_id.description: ID of the workflow that ran.

workflow_name.title: Workflow Name
workflow_name.description: Name of that workflow at the time of the run.

trigger_type.title: Trigger Type
trigger_type.description: What started the run: `scheduled`, `entity`, `connector`, `in_app_agent`, `app_user_auth`, `app_publish`, `app_payment`, `webhook`, or `goal_file`. See [Triggers](/developers/references/apps-api/sections/workflows#triggers) for what each one fires on. A run started through [Run a workflow now](/api-reference/run-a-workflow-now) with no payload to replay reports `manual` instead.

status.title: Status
status.description: How the run is going: `running`, `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. See [Workflow status](/developers/references/apps-api/sections/workflows#workflow-status) for how this compares to the workflow's own status.

started_at.title: Started At
started_at.description: When the run started, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

completed_at.title: Completed At
completed_at.description: When the run finished, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. This is `null` while it is still running.

duration_ms.title: Duration Ms
duration_ms.description: How long the run took, in milliseconds. This is `0` while it is still running.

error_message.title: Error Message
error_message.description: Why the run failed. This is `null` when it did not fail.
error_message.example: The email step failed because the recipient address was missing.

is_test_run.title: Is Test Run
is_test_run.description: This is `true` when the run was started by hand through [Run a workflow now](/api-reference/run-a-workflow-now), rather than by its trigger.

status_reason.title: Status Reason
status_reason.description: Why the run failed or was cancelled. Empty on runs that finished successfully.

manual_run_config.description: What a manual run of this workflow needs.

recent_runs.title: Recent Runs
recent_runs.description: Runs whose payload you can replay, newest first, at most 20. Empty when the trigger needs no payload.

replay_from_run_id.title: Replay From Run Id
replay_from_run_id.description: Run whose trigger payload to reuse for this run. Required when [Get workflow run-now options](/api-reference/get-workflow-run-now-options) reports `requires_previous_run`. Leave it out otherwise.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `started`. The run is queued, not finished.

message.title: Message
message.description: Confirmation text you can show someone.

run_id.title: Run Id
run_id.description: ID of the run that started. Pass it to [Get workflow run](/api-reference/get-workflow-run) to follow it.

score.title: Score
score.description: Score for this category, 0 to 100. A passing check counts 100, a warning 50 and a failure 0, averaged over the category's checks.

passed.title: Passed
passed.description: Checks in this category that passed. A plain count, so the three counts add up to the category's checks in `checks`.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: Checks in this category that returned a warning.

failures.title: Failures
failures.description: Checks in this category that failed.

SEOCategoryScore.title: SEOCategoryScore
SEOCategoryScore.description: One category's slice of the overall score.

id.title: Id
id.description: Identifier of the check. Stable across scans, but a check can be missing from a later scan rather than change status, because Base44 collapses cascading failures into their root cause.

category.title: Category
category.description: Which part of the score this check feeds: `meta_tags`, `crawlability`, `structured_data`, `ai_discoverability`, `content_quality`, or `indexing_performance` when Google Search Console integration is enabled for you.

title.title: Title
title.description: Short name of the check, phrased for the finding rather than the subject, so it changes with `status`.

status.title: Status
status.description: Outcome of the check. A `warn` scores 50 against the category and a `fail` scores 0. Not every check can return all three.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the check found, written for the app's owner.
description.example: Turn on the AI site guide so AI engines can understand your app.

details.title: Details
details.description: Supporting detail for the finding, usually one object per page or entity involved. The keys differ per check, so treat the entries as opaque.

fix_action.description: The remedy the Base44 app editor offers, or `null` when the check passed or can't be fixed in-app.

info_only.title: Info Only
info_only.description: Environmental findings, such as DNS or hosting issues that can't be resolved from inside the app, set this to `true`. Everything else is `false`.

SEOCheckResult.title: SEOCheckResult
SEOCheckResult.description: One check from the SEO scan.

type.title: Type
type.description: Identifier of the action that fixes this check. Apply it with [Apply SEO fix](/api-reference/apply-seo-fix). See [Fix actions](/developers/references/apps-api/sections/seo#fix-actions) for what each one does.

label.title: Label
label.description: Label the app editor shows on the button for this action.

params.title: Params
params.description: Arguments to send with the action to [Apply SEO fix](/api-reference/apply-seo-fix). Most actions carry none. The keys differ per action, so send them as they are.

SEOFixAction.title: SEOFixAction
SEOFixAction.description: The remedy Base44 offers for a check.

success.title: Success
success.description: Whether the action was applied. It's `false` when the action had nothing to apply, and `message` says why.

message.title: Message
message.description: Summary of the outcome, written for the app's owner.

redirect.title: Redirect
redirect.description: App editor screen where the app's owner makes this fix, either `"overview"`, `"app-settings"`, `"seo-meta-tags"`, `"domains"`, or `"publish"`. The key is present only for the actions that change nothing.

overall.title: Overall
overall.description: Overall SEO score for the app, 0 to 100.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: Per-category breakdown, keyed by the same category names the checks carry: `meta_tags`, `crawlability`, `structured_data`, `ai_discoverability` and `content_quality`, plus `indexing_performance` when Google Search Console integration is enabled for you. Base44 can add another category, so read the map rather than assuming this list is complete. Every category in the map is scored, including one this scan ran no checks for, which scores 100 with all three counts at zero.

SEOOverallScore.title: SEOOverallScore
SEOOverallScore.description: The scan's score, overall and per category.

title.title: Title
title.description: Title tag for this page. The key is absent while the page overrides no title.

description.title: Description
description.description: Meta description for this page. The key is absent while the page overrides no description.
description.example: Track leads and deals in one place.

og_image.title: Og Image
og_image.description: Image URL for the `og:image` and `twitter:image` tags on this page. It must be an `https://` URL with a host and no backslashes, and it cannot exceed 2048 characters. Send an empty string to stop overriding the image.

noindex.title: Noindex
noindex.description: Whether the page is hidden from search engines. When `true`, Base44 serves the page with a `noindex, nofollow` robots directive and leaves it out of the `sitemap.xml` it generates. This applies only while the app is search-eligible and `seo_disabled` is `false`. Defaults to `false` while the key is absent.

SEOPageSettings.title: SEOPageSettings
SEOPageSettings.description: The meta tags one page overrides, and whether it's hidden from search engines.

result.description: Settings saved for the page, or an empty object if the page has none and the call changes nothing.

checks.title: Checks
checks.description: The checks behind the score, in the order Base44 reports them. Not every check it ran appears here. A failure that only restates an upstream one is dropped in favour of the root cause, so an unpublished or login-gated app returns the one gating failure rather than the dozen findings that follow from it.

example.description: Turn on the AI site guide so AI engines can understand your app.
example.title: AI-readable site guide is off

scanned_at.title: Scanned At
scanned_at.description: When the scan ran, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

SEOScanReport.title: SEOScanReport
SEOScanReport.description: An SEO scan: its score and every check behind it.

result.description: The last scan's score, or `null` if the app has never been scanned.

overall.title: Overall
overall.description: Overall SEO score for the app, 0 to 100.

failures.title: Failures
failures.description: How many checks failed in that scan.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: How many checks returned a warning in that scan.

scanned_at.title: Scanned At
scanned_at.description: When the scan ran, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.

SEOScoreRollup.title: SEOScoreRollup
SEOScoreRollup.description: The last scan's score, without its checks.

seo_disabled.title: Seo Disabled
seo_disabled.description: Whether you run your own SEO. When `true`, Base44 stops injecting titles, descriptions, Open Graph and Twitter tags, canonical URLs, JSON-LD and prerender snapshots, and serves your own `public/robots.txt` when you ship one. Defaults to `false` while the key is absent. This does not add a `noindex` tag, and a login-gated or private app stays unindexed whatever you set here.

platform_meta_injection_enabled.title: Platform Meta Injection Enabled
platform_meta_injection_enabled.description: Whether Base44 injects the title, description, Open Graph and Twitter tag block. Set it to `false` when your deployed `index.html` already carries a complete set. Narrower than `seo_disabled`, which also turns off canonical URLs, JSON-LD and snapshots. Defaults to `true` while the key is absent.

platform_jsonld_injection_enabled.title: Platform Jsonld Injection Enabled
platform_jsonld_injection_enabled.description: Whether Base44 injects its own WebSite, Organization, BreadcrumbList and FAQPage JSON-LD. Set it to `false` when your app ships its own structured data. Defaults to `true` while the key is absent.

robots_txt_enabled.title: Robots Txt Enabled
robots_txt_enabled.description: Whether Base44 generates `/robots.txt`. When `false`, your deployed `public/robots.txt` is served instead, and the path returns 404 when you ship none. Defaults to `true` while the key is absent.

sitemap_xml_enabled.title: Sitemap Xml Enabled
sitemap_xml_enabled.description: Whether Base44 generates `/sitemap.xml`. When `false`, your deployed `public/sitemap.xml` is served instead, and the path returns 404 when you ship none. Defaults to `true` while the key is absent.

llms_txt_enabled.title: Llms Txt Enabled
llms_txt_enabled.description: Whether Base44 serves a generated `/llms.txt` describing the app to AI crawlers. Defaults to `false` while the key is absent.

ai_crawlers_enabled.title: Ai Crawlers Enabled
ai_crawlers_enabled.description: Whether known AI crawlers are allowed in the generated `robots.txt`. Defaults to `true` while the key is absent.

synthesized_breadcrumb_enabled.title: Synthesized Breadcrumb Enabled
synthesized_breadcrumb_enabled.description: Whether Base44 builds a BreadcrumbList for each request path at render time. Set it to `false` to serve the saved `breadcrumb_schema` instead, which is what keeps a hand-written breadcrumb intact. Defaults to `true` while the key is absent.

canonical_url.title: Canonical Url
canonical_url.description: Base URL Base44 builds canonical tags from. The app's own published URL is used while the key is absent.

content_query_params.title: Content Query Params
content_query_params.description: Query-string parameter names whose values serve distinct content, such as `article` for `/guides?article=slug`. Naming one opts its URL variants into prerender warming, which otherwise only covers paths. Send at most 25 names, counted before the list is cleaned up, and match each name's casing exactly. Names are trimmed, and blank or repeated entries are dropped, so the list you read back can be shorter than the one you sent. Defaults to an empty list, meaning no query variants are warmed.

custom_json_ld.title: Custom Json Ld
custom_json_ld.description: Extra JSON-LD entries Base44 injects alongside its own. Each entry needs a `json_ld_template` key holding the markup object to inject, matching the shape [Preview JSON-LD](/api-reference/preview-json-ld) returns. The key is absent while you have added none.

website_schema.title: Website Schema
website_schema.description: Saved WebSite JSON-LD object. The key is absent while none is saved.

organization_schema.title: Organization Schema
organization_schema.description: Saved Organization JSON-LD object. The key is absent while none is saved.

breadcrumb_schema.title: Breadcrumb Schema
breadcrumb_schema.description: Saved BreadcrumbList JSON-LD object. It is served only while `synthesized_breadcrumb_enabled` is `false`. The key is absent while none is saved.

faq_schema.title: Faq Schema
faq_schema.description: Saved FAQPage JSON-LD object. The key is absent while none is saved.

pages.title: Pages
pages.description: Per-page tag overrides, keyed by the page's component name as it appears in the app's code. The key is absent while no page overrides anything.

Home.description: Track leads and deals in one place.
Home.title: Acme CRM

result.description: The saved settings. This is an empty object for an app whose SEO settings have never been changed.

cold_start.title: Cold Start
cold_start.description: Whether a new sandbox was started for this request. A value of `false` means an already running one was reused, which is why a repeat call is much faster.

restored_from_snapshot.title: Restored From Snapshot
restored_from_snapshot.description: Whether the new sandbox was restored from a snapshot rather than built from scratch. Always `false` when `cold_start` is `false`.

timeout_timestamp.title: Timeout Timestamp
timeout_timestamp.description: When the sandbox shuts down if nothing touches it, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` when the sandbox already existed, because reusing it does not change its timeout.

SandboxInfo.title: SandboxInfo
SandboxInfo.description: Metadata about the sandbox serving this preview URL.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the Base44 app.

status.title: Status
status.description: Stored sandbox status. Either `unclaimed`, `claimed`, or `expired`.

claim_url.title: Claim Url
claim_url.description: Onboarding link, or `null` when none is stored, you are a workspace viewer, or the app's workspace restricts payment management. Treat this link as a credential.

stripe_account_id.title: Stripe Account Id
stripe_account_id.description: Stripe account ID for the sandbox.

is_claimable.title: Is Claimable
is_claimable.description: Whether the sandbox is unclaimed, has not expired, has a stored claim link, and the app's workspace allows payment management.

expires_at.title: Expires At
expires_at.description: Sandbox expiration as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format, or `null` when no expiration is stored.

url.title: Url
url.description: Signed link to the thread's screenshot, valid for one year, or `null` when the thread has no screenshot.

search_term.title: Search Term
search_term.description: The term the user searched for.

campaign.title: Campaign
campaign.description: Name of the campaign whose ad the term matched.

impressions.title: Impressions
impressions.description: Impressions the term drove in the window.

clicks.title: Clicks
clicks.description: Clicks the term drove in the window.

cost_micros.title: Cost Micros
cost_micros.description: Amount spent on the term in the window, in micros of the account's currency.

conversions.title: Conversions
conversions.description: Conversions attributed to the term in the window.

SearchTermRow.title: SearchTermRow
SearchTermRow.description: One search term someone used before seeing an ad.

business_name.title: Business Name
business_name.description: Name of the business the campaign is for.

business_description.title: Business Description
business_description.description: What the business sells, in a sentence or two.
business_description.example: Handmade solid oak dining tables, built to order in San Francisco.

landing_page_url.title: Landing Page Url
landing_page_url.description: Page the campaign sends people to. Used as context.

secret_name.title: Secret Name
secret_name.description: Name of the secret, from `transfer_package.secrets` in the preflight result.

action.title: Action
action.description: Either `transfer_value`, to copy the secret's value to the new owner, or `require_new_value`, to clear it so the new owner sets their own.

SecretTransferDecisionRequest.title: SecretTransferDecisionRequest
SecretTransferDecisionRequest.description: Sender decision for one app secret. Values are never sent by the client.

file_path.title: File Path
file_path.description: Path of the file in the app where it was found.

description.title: Description
description.description: What is wrong with the function and what to change.
description.example: createOrder trusts the price sent by the browser. Look the price up server-side instead.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: Stable ID for this finding. Send it to [Ignore security finding](/api-reference/ignore-security-finding) to hide the finding across rescans. It changes when the function's file changes, so an ignored finding comes back once the file is edited.

SecurityBackendFunctionIssue.title: SecurityBackendFunctionIssue
SecurityBackendFunctionIssue.description: A problem found in one of the app's backend functions.

vulnerable_range.title: Vulnerable Range
vulnerable_range.description: Range of versions the advisory covers, or `null` when the advisory does not give one.

fixed_version.title: Fixed Version
fixed_version.description: First version the advisory says is fixed, or `null` when there is no fixed release.

safe_fixed_version.title: Safe Fixed Version
safe_fixed_version.description: The version Base44 checked is safe to install, which can be newer than `fixed_version`. It is `null` when no safe version was found, and absent on a finding recorded before Base44 started checking.

fix_unavailable_reason.title: Fix Unavailable Reason
fix_unavailable_reason.description: Why no safe upgrade exists, when that is the case. It is `null` or absent when there is one.
fix_unavailable_reason.example: No released version satisfies the app's peer dependencies.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: How serious it is, one of `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: Stable ID for this finding. Send it to [Ignore security finding](/api-reference/ignore-security-finding) to hide the finding across rescans. Every vulnerability in the same version of a package shares one fingerprint, so ignoring one ignores them all. It changes when the installed version changes or the package's advisories, their severities, or their fixed versions change, so an ignored package comes back then.

SecurityDependencyVulnerability.title: SecurityDependencyVulnerability
SecurityDependencyVulnerability.description: A known vulnerability in one of the app's npm dependencies.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `ok`, including when nothing changed.

file_path.title: File Path
file_path.description: Path of the file in the app where it was found.

description.title: Description
description.description: What was found and why it is a problem. The secret's own value is not included.
description.example: A Stripe live key is written into the checkout page. Move it to an app secret and read it from a backend function.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: Stable ID for this finding. Send it to [Ignore security finding](/api-reference/ignore-security-finding) to hide the finding across rescans. It changes when the file changes, so an ignored finding comes back once the file is edited.

SecurityHardcodedSecret.title: SecurityHardcodedSecret
SecurityHardcodedSecret.description: A credential written directly into the app's code.

flag.title: Flag
flag.description: Which setting to turn on, either `prevent_iframe_embedding` or `restrict_browser_features`. Turn it on with [Update security headers](/api-reference/update-security-headers), or hide the recommendation with [Dismiss header recommendation](/api-reference/dismiss-header-recommendation).

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: How serious it is, one of `high`, `medium` or `low`.

reason_key.title: Reason Key
reason_key.description: Stable identifier for the reason. The readable text is Base44's own translated copy, so treat this as a code to branch on rather than something to show.

SecurityHeaderRecommendation.title: SecurityHeaderRecommendation
SecurityHeaderRecommendation.description: A recommended change to the published app's HTTP headers.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `ok`, including when there was nothing to dismiss.

SecurityHeaderRecommendationDismissed.title: SecurityHeaderRecommendationDismissed
SecurityHeaderRecommendationDismissed.description: Confirms the header recommendation is dismissed.

prevent_iframe_embedding.title: Prevent Iframe Embedding
prevent_iframe_embedding.description: Whether the app blocks every site from showing it in a frame (`true`) or not (`false`). When `true`, the published app sends `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.

restrict_browser_features.title: Restrict Browser Features
restrict_browser_features.description: Whether the published app sends a restrictive `Permissions-Policy` header (`true`) or not (`false`). It lets only the app's own pages use the camera, microphone, location, payment, and USB features, and turns off the magnetometer and gyroscope.

embedding_origins.title: Embedding Origins
embedding_origins.description: Sites the app itself allows to frame it, or `null` when the app has no list of its own.

org_embedding_origins.title: Org Embedding Origins
org_embedding_origins.description: Sites the app's workspace allows to frame its apps, or `null` when the workspace sets no list or its plan doesn't include one.

org_prevent_iframe_embedding.title: Org Prevent Iframe Embedding
org_prevent_iframe_embedding.description: Whether the app's workspace blocks framing for all of its apps (`true`) or not (`false`).

app_policy.description: The framing policy set on the app itself.

effective_policy.description: The framing policy the published app actually sends, after the workspace policy is applied.

app_allowlist_locked_by_workspace.title: App Allowlist Locked By Workspace
app_allowlist_locked_by_workspace.description: Whether the app's workspace controls which sites can frame its apps (`true`), so the app can't set a list of its own, or not (`false`).

SecurityHeadersSettingsResult.title: SecurityHeadersSettingsResult
SecurityHeadersSettingsResult.description: Security header settings for one app.

entity_name.title: Entity Name
entity_name.description: Entity the recommendation is for, as returned by [List entity schemas](/api-reference/list-entity-schemas).

description.title: Description
description.description: Why the scan recommends these rules, in plain language.
description.example: Orders are readable by anyone. Restrict reads to the customer who placed the order.

create_rule.title: Create Rule
create_rule.description: Recommended rule for creating a record. The rule to apply to this operation. `true` allows it for everyone, `false` blocks it outright, `null` leaves it unset, and an object is a filter matched against the record and the signed-in app user. Send the four rules to [Update entity schema](/api-reference/update-entity-schema) under the entity's `rls` to apply them.

read_rule.title: Read Rule
read_rule.description: Recommended rule for reading records. The rule to apply to this operation. `true` allows it for everyone, `false` blocks it outright, `null` leaves it unset, and an object is a filter matched against the record and the signed-in app user. Send the four rules to [Update entity schema](/api-reference/update-entity-schema) under the entity's `rls` to apply them.

update_rule.title: Update Rule
update_rule.description: Recommended rule for updating a record. The rule to apply to this operation. `true` allows it for everyone, `false` blocks it outright, `null` leaves it unset, and an object is a filter matched against the record and the signed-in app user. Send the four rules to [Update entity schema](/api-reference/update-entity-schema) under the entity's `rls` to apply them.

delete_rule.title: Delete Rule
delete_rule.description: Recommended rule for deleting a record. The rule to apply to this operation. `true` allows it for everyone, `false` blocks it outright, `null` leaves it unset, and an object is a filter matched against the record and the signed-in app user. Send the four rules to [Update entity schema](/api-reference/update-entity-schema) under the entity's `rls` to apply them.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: Stable ID for this finding. Send it to [Ignore security finding](/api-reference/ignore-security-finding) to hide the finding across rescans. It changes when the entity's fields change, so an ignored recommendation comes back then.

SecurityRlsRecommendation.title: SecurityRlsRecommendation
SecurityRlsRecommendation.description: A recommended row-level security rule set for one entity.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `ok`. The recommendation is no longer in the scan result.

SecurityRlsRecommendationDismissed.title: SecurityRlsRecommendationDismissed
SecurityRlsRecommendationDismissed.description: Confirms that the recommendation left the scan result.

analysis_summary.title: Analysis Summary
analysis_summary.example: The app exposes orders to any signed-in user and has one hardcoded credential.

rls_recommendations.title: Rls Recommendations
rls_recommendations.description: Entities whose row-level security should change, one entry per entity.

hardcoded_secrets.title: Hardcoded Secrets
hardcoded_secrets.description: Credentials written into the app's code.

backend_functions.title: Backend Functions
backend_functions.description: Problems found in the app's backend functions.

dependency_vulnerabilities.title: Dependency Vulnerabilities
dependency_vulnerabilities.description: Known vulnerabilities in the app's npm dependencies. Always empty for a caller outside the dependency-scanning rollout.

static_code_findings.title: Static Code Findings
static_code_findings.description: Problems found by reading the app's code, listing only the findings that survived the scan's own second-pass check. It is an empty list when code-reading analysis is switched off for the app, which is not the same as a clean result, so read `static_code_enabled` before concluding there is nothing to find.

header_recommendations.title: Header Recommendations
header_recommendations.description: Recommended changes to the published app's HTTP headers. These are computed from the app's current settings on every read rather than stored with the scan.

core_integration_recommendation.title: Core Integration Recommendation
core_integration_recommendation.description: Whether the app is ready for Base44's core-integration protection. `no_restricted_usage` means nothing in the app needs it, `compatible` means turning it on with [Enable core integration protection](/api-reference/enable-core-integration-protection) is safe, `would_be_blocked` means it would break the app as written, and `publish_required` means the app has to be published before this can be judged. It is `null` when the answer does not apply to this app.

ignored_fingerprints.title: Ignored Fingerprints
ignored_fingerprints.description: Fingerprints of the findings that have been ignored with [Ignore security finding](/api-reference/ignore-security-finding). Those findings are still in their lists, so leave out any whose `fingerprint` appears here to see only the open ones. An entry that matches no finding here stays until the next scan drops it.

scanned_at.title: Scanned At
scanned_at.description: When the scan that produced these findings ran, or `null` on a result recorded before Base44 stored the time.

SecurityScanFindings.title: SecurityScanFindings
SecurityScanFindings.description: What a completed security scan found.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the scan is. `up_to_date` means `result` reflects the app as it is now. `out_of_date` means the app changed since the last scan, so `result` is stale or absent. `none` means the app has never been scanned. `pending` means a scan is queued and `scanning` means one is running, and both can carry an earlier `result` while you wait. `scan_failed` means the last scan died, so run another.

result.description: What the scan found, or `null` when there is nothing to show. It is `null` on `none`, and also on `out_of_date` when the last scan came from a different version of the scanner, in which case only a fresh scan produces findings.

static_code_enabled.title: Static Code Enabled
static_code_enabled.description: Whether code-reading analysis is switched on for this app (`true`) or not (`false`). When it is `false`, `result.static_code_findings` comes back as an empty list, so this field is the only way to tell an analysis that found nothing from one that never ran.

stream.description: Partial results from a scan that is still running, or `null` when there are none. It appears only while `status` is `scanning`, and only for callers inside the progressive-results rollout. `result` above keeps its own meaning — the previous scan's findings — so ignoring this field preserves the earlier behavior of waiting for the whole scan.

SecurityScanStatus.title: SecurityScanStatus
SecurityScanStatus.description: The state of an app's security scan, and its findings when it has any.

result.description: What the areas that have already reported found, in the same shape as `result`. An area that has not reported yet contributes an empty list, which is not the same as a clean result, so read `sections` before concluding there is nothing to find.

sections.title: Sections
sections.description: How each area of the scan is doing, keyed by area: `rls`, `hardcoded_secrets`, `backend_functions`, `dependency_vulnerabilities` and `static_code`. `checking` means the area has not reported yet, `completed` means its findings are in this block's `result`, `failed` means it could not be checked, and `not_run` means it does not apply to this app. Only `completed` means the area's findings are settled.

SecurityScanStreamProgress.title: SecurityScanStreamProgress
SecurityScanStreamProgress.description: How far a still-running security scan has got, area by area.

title.title: Title
title.description: Short name for the problem.
title.example: Order lookup trusts a client-supplied ID

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: How serious it is, one of `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: How sure the scan is, one of `high`, `medium` or `low`. A `low` confidence finding is worth reading before acting on.

category.title: Category
category.description: What kind of problem it is, one of `unauthorized_access`, `unsafe_user_input`, `exposed_sensitive_data`, `unsafe_redirect_or_external_request`, `unsafe_browser_code`, `payment_or_webhook_risk`, `file_handling_risk`, `ai_vulnerability` or `other`.

file_path.title: File Path
file_path.description: Path of the file in the app where it was found.

line_number.title: Line Number
line_number.description: Line the finding points at, or `null` when the scan could not place it on one.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: The snippet of the app's own code the finding is about.

attack_scenario.title: Attack Scenario
attack_scenario.example: Change the id in the URL to another customer's order and read it.

impact.title: Impact
impact.example: Any signed-in user can read every order.

recommendation.title: Recommendation
recommendation.example: Add a read rule on Order restricting it to the customer who placed it.

standards.title: Standards
standards.description: Security standards the finding maps to. Absent on a finding the scan did not classify.

fingerprint.title: Fingerprint
fingerprint.description: Stable ID for this finding. Send it to [Ignore security finding](/api-reference/ignore-security-finding) to hide the finding across rescans. It stays the same when only the wording or line number changes, and changes when the file, `category`, or `evidence` does, so an ignored finding comes back then.

SecurityStaticCodeFinding.title: SecurityStaticCodeFinding
SecurityStaticCodeFinding.description: A problem found by reading the app's code.

framework.title: Framework
framework.description: Which catalog the identifier belongs to.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the entry.

SecurityStaticCodeStandard.title: SecurityStaticCodeStandard
SecurityStaticCodeStandard.description: A security standard a static-analysis finding maps to.

seeded.title: Seeded
seeded.description: Records written for each entity, keyed by entity name. `0` when nothing was written.

generated_total.title: Generated Total
generated_total.description: How many of the records were made up by AI rather than copied from live data.

entities_with_data.title: Entities With Data
entities_with_data.description: Entities that got records, or whose own test records were kept.

entities_without_prod_data.title: Entities Without Prod Data
entities_without_prod_data.description: Entities that got nothing copied from live data and didn't report an error. When this call gave up waiting for another seed of the app, every entity is listed.

entities_with_errors.title: Entities With Errors
entities_with_errors.description: Entities whose seeding reported an error, for example because generating records timed out. An entity whose record writes all failed isn't listed. Its `seeded` count is `0`.

SeededTestData.title: SeededTestData
SeededTestData.description: What a seed wrote into the app's test data.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: Your ID for the message. A retry with the same ID doesn't start a second turn. Defaults to a new UUID.

content.title: Content
content.description: The message to the Marketing Agent. Up to 20,000 characters.
content.example: Focus on LinkedIn instead of Reddit.

target_domain.title: Target Domain
target_domain.description: Domain to send this domain's visitors to, or `null` to stop redirecting. It has to be another verified custom domain on the same app.

success.title: Success
success.description: Whether the secrets were stored.

SetSecretsResponse.title: SetSecretsResponse
SetSecretsResponse.description: Confirmation that the secrets were stored.

selected_label.title: Selected Label
selected_label.description: The answer as the user would say it. It's recorded as their message in the app's chat, and for `budget` it's the stored budget.

value.title: Value
value.description: For `competitor_research`, whether to research competitors (`true`) or not (`false`). Ignored for other questions.

band.title: Band
band.description: For `budget`, the budget band that selects each KPI's target. Either `"none"`, `"low"`, `"mid"`, or `"high"`. Any other value is ignored.

stage.title: Stage
stage.description: The step you're answering, from the state's `setup_stage`. Either `"channels"`, `"kpis"`, or `"budget"`.

reset_epoch.title: Reset Epoch
reset_epoch.description: The state's `reset_epoch`, so the answer is rejected if the plan was reset since you read it. Omit it to skip that check.

answers.title: Answers
answers.description: Answers to the step's questions. Between 1 and 4.

message_id.title: Message Id
message_id.description: ID for the chat message that records the answer. Use a new UUID for every answer, and the same one when you retry it. A retry with the same ID returns the current state and applies nothing. Defaults to a new UUID.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the share. Pass it as `share_id` to update or remove the share.

group_id.title: Group Id
group_id.description: ID of the workspace group the app is shared with.

group_name.title: Group Name
group_name.description: Name of the group, or `null` when the group was deleted. A share whose group was deleted grants no access, and you can still remove it.

group_source.title: Group Source
group_source.description: Where the group comes from: `custom` for a group created in Base44, or `idp` for a group your identity provider syncs over SCIM. `null` when the group was deleted.

member_count.title: Member Count
member_count.description: Number of group members with a Base44 account.

unresolved_count.title: Unresolved Count
unresolved_count.description: Number of group members your identity provider synced who don't have a Base44 account yet. They get access once they have one.

role.title: Role
role.description: App role the share gives the group's members, or `null` when it assigns none and members get the default `user` role.

created_by.title: Created By
created_by.description: Email of the person who shared the app with the group.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the app was shared with the group, in UTC, as ISO 8601 without a timezone suffix.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: What is wrong with the slug.
detail.example: URL slug 'nordwind' is already in use

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.description: Up to five unused slugs close to the one you sent, present only when that slug is taken. Empty when Base44 could not come up with any.

SlugRejected.title: SlugRejected
SlugRejected.description: Why the slug was not accepted.

stage.description: How far the app has got. The stage is `idle` before you start, then `questions`, `strategy`, `generating`, and `completed` once a plan exists.

questions.title: Questions
questions.description: Questions from [Start social content flow](/api-reference/start-social-content-flow), or `null` if the flow hasn't started.

analysis_text.title: Analysis Text
analysis_text.description: One-sentence analysis of the app, or `null` if the flow hasn't started.
analysis_text.example: A CRM for freelancers who want to track leads without a spreadsheet.

answers.title: Answers
answers.description: Answers you submitted, keyed by question `id`, or `null` if none were submitted.

strategy_text.title: Strategy Text
strategy_text.description: The current content strategy, or `null` if none was generated.
strategy_text.example: Lead with the spreadsheet pain, then show the app solving it.

plan.description: The current content plan, or `null` if none was generated. Poll this to pick up images that finish generating after [Generate content plan](/api-reference/generate-content-plan) returns.

builder_handle.title: Builder Handle
builder_handle.description: Social handle taken from the `social_url` you submitted, or `null` if you never sent one.

teaser.description: The standalone teaser posts from [Generate teaser posts](/api-reference/generate-teaser-posts). They're generated outside this flow and are not part of `plan`.

SocialContentStateResponse.title: SocialContentStateResponse
SocialContentStateResponse.description: The current state of an app's social content flow.

social_image_url.title: Social Image Url
social_image_url.description: `https` URL of the image to show in link previews, up to 2048 characters, or `null` to remove the current one. Leaving it out also removes it.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the post. Pass it as `post_id` to [Refine a post](/api-reference/refine-a-post), [Update post content](/api-reference/update-post-content), and [Generate a post image](/api-reference/generate-a-post-image).

platform.description: Platform the post is written for.

post_number.title: Post Number
post_number.description: Position of this post within its platform's set, starting at 1.

total_posts.title: Total Posts
total_posts.description: Number of posts generated for this platform.

suggested_day.title: Suggested Day
suggested_day.description: Suggested day to publish on, counted from the start of the campaign.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Why this post works for this platform and angle.
rationale.example: Opens on the spreadsheet frustration the audience already has.

content.title: Content
content.description: The post text, ready to publish. Change it with [Update post content](/api-reference/update-post-content).
content.example: Still tracking leads in a spreadsheet? I built the thing I wanted instead.

image_url.title: Image Url
image_url.description: URL of the post image, or `null` if no image was generated yet. Create one with [Generate a post image](/api-reference/generate-a-post-image).

image_prompt.title: Image Prompt
image_prompt.description: Prompt used to generate the post image, or `null` if the post has none.

entityNameToSchema.title: Entitynametoschema
entityNameToSchema.description: The app's complete set of entities, keyed by entity name. Each value is that entity's [JSON Schema](/developers/backend/resources/entities/entity-schemas), which needs `"type": "object"` and a `properties` object, plus any `required` fields and [row-level security rules](/developers/backend/resources/entities/security) under `rls`. Any entity the app currently has that this map leaves out is deleted.

warnings.title: Warnings
warnings.description: Row-level security rules Base44 stored but can't enforce. The sync still applied, so an entity named here exists with a rule that isn't protecting anything. Base44 reports a rule this way only for an entity the sync adds fresh (one that didn't exist in the app before). On an entity the app already has, a new or changed rule of this kind fails the call with a 400. An unchanged unenforceable rule on an existing entity is left in place silently and doesn't appear here.
example: Invalid RLS rule in Invoice: "properties.total.rls.delete" — field-level delete rules are not enforced — delete removes the whole record (there is no field-level delete gate); put the restriction in a top-level rls.delete instead.
