search_themes.title: Search Themes
search_themes.description: Search themes the campaign already uses, so the copy matches them.

user_prompt.title: User Prompt
user_prompt.description: Extra direction for the copy, in the caller's own words.

bucket.title: Bucket
bucket.description: Start of the bucket. A date-time for intervals under a day, and a date for intervals of a day or longer.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: The requested metrics for this bucket, keyed by the `name` you gave each one.

TimeBucket.title: TimeBucket
TimeBucket.description: A single time bucket with computed metrics.

event_name.title: Event Name
event_name.description: Name of the event to aggregate. Omit to aggregate every event the app tracks.

q.title: Q
q.description: Filter expression, as a JSON object serialized to a string. Same syntax as [Query analytics events](/api-reference/query-analytics-events).

start_time.title: Start Time
start_time.description: Start of the time range, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to 30 days ago.

end_time.title: End Time
end_time.description: End of the time range, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now.

bucket_size_ms.title: Bucket Size Ms
bucket_size_ms.description: Requested bucket size in milliseconds. Base44 rounds it down to the nearest supported interval, and up to one hour when you ask for anything finer than that. Omit to pick the finest interval that fits `max_buckets`.

max_buckets.title: Max Buckets
max_buckets.description: Maximum number of buckets to return, between 10 and 1000. Drives the interval when `bucket_size_ms` is omitted.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.description: Between 1 and 10 metrics to compute per bucket. Defaults to an event count named `event_count` and a distinct-user count named `unique_users`.

event_name.title: Event Name
event_name.description: The event name that was aggregated, or `null` when the request covered every event.

bucket_interval.title: Bucket Interval
bucket_interval.description: Interval Base44 bucketed by, in milliseconds.

totals.title: Totals
totals.description: Each metric computed over the whole range at once, keyed by metric name. Not the sum of the buckets, because `count_unique` counts distinct values across the range.

buckets.title: Buckets
buckets.description: The buckets, oldest first. Buckets with no matching events are omitted rather than reported as zero.

TimeseriesResponse.title: TimeseriesResponse
TimeseriesResponse.description: Analytics events aggregated into time buckets.

emoji.title: Emoji
emoji.description: Emoji to toggle, up to 16 characters.

status.title: Status
status.description: The status the workflow actually landed in, which is not always the one you asked for.

message.title: Message
message.description: Why a restored workflow did not come back active, written for a person to read. This is `null` when you toggled the status yourself.
message.example: The schedule already ended, so the workflow stayed inactive.

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether to turn automatic sync on or off. Send `true` to turn it on and `false` to turn it off.

ToggleSyncRequest.title: ToggleSyncRequest
ToggleSyncRequest.description: The automatic sync setting to apply.

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`. A change that can't be applied is rejected with an error status instead.

sync_enabled.title: Sync Enabled
sync_enabled.description: Whether automatic sync is now on. The value is `true` when it's on and `false` when it's off, and it always matches what you sent.

name.title: Name
name.description: Customer name from Stripe, or `null` when enrichment is unavailable. Defaults to `null`.

email.title: Email
email.description: Customer email from Stripe, or `null` when enrichment is unavailable. Defaults to `null`.

transaction_count.title: Transaction Count
transaction_count.description: Number of payments in the selected window. Defaults to 0.

total_amount.title: Total Amount
total_amount.description: Total payment amount in the currencies' smallest units. Filter to one currency before interpreting this value. Defaults to 0.

TopCustomer.title: TopCustomer
TopCustomer.description: A top customer with metrics and optional provider details.

customers.title: Customers
customers.description: Customers ranked by the requested metric, highest first. Empty when no matching payments are found.

composer_prompt.title: Composer Prompt
composer_prompt.description: The instruction to send to [Send chat message](/api-reference/send-chat-message). It ends with a reminder to publish, because Google Ads only records conversions from the published app. The value is an empty string when `skipped_reason` is set.
composer_prompt.example:
Wire up Google Ads conversion tracking for this app.

Call get_capability_guide("google_ads") first, then follow it.

conversion_id.title: Conversion Id
conversion_id.description: The gtag conversion ID baked into the prompt, or an empty string when the prompt tells the AI to look each one up instead of carrying a concrete ID. Absent when `skipped_reason` is set.

actions_created_or_existing.title: Actions Created Or Existing
actions_created_or_existing.description: How many conversion goals the account has after this call, counting the ones it already had. Absent when `skipped_reason` is set.

wired_mappings.title: Wired Mappings
wired_mappings.description: How many of the account's conversion mappings the prompt carries wiring guidance for. When you send `wire_events` and the account has no enabled mapping, this reports the number of conversion categories the prompt offers instead, so read any value above `0` as a sign that the prompt carries wiring guidance rather than as a mapping count. Absent when `skipped_reason` is set.

skipped_reason.title: Skipped Reason
skipped_reason.description: Why no prompt was produced. The only value is `no_google_ads_account`, which means the app has no Google Ads account that can carry conversion tracking. The field is absent whenever a prompt was produced.

TrackingFixPromptResponse.title: TrackingFixPromptResponse
TrackingFixPromptResponse.description: A ready-made instruction for the AI to install conversion tracking.

id.title: Id
id.description: Identifier for this gap within the scan. A gap whose ID starts with `missing-call-` is a mapped goal with no firing code, `no-action-` is a mapping with no matching goal in Google Ads, `disabled-` is a disabled mapping, and `orphan-call-` is code firing a conversion no mapping points at.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: How serious the gap is. `error` means a mapped conversion cannot fire, and `warning` means the setup works but something is configured in a way you probably did not intend.

message.title: Message
message.description: What is wrong, written for an engineer. It names the `send_to` and the call shape where those apply.
message.example: Order.create is mapped to PURCHASE but no gtag('event', 'conversion', { send_to: 'AW-123456789/AbCdEfGhIj', ... }) call exists in the app code.

suggested_files.title: Suggested Files
suggested_files.description: Up to three files in the app that look like the place to add or fix the call. Empty when the scan has no suggestion.

composer_prompt.title: Composer Prompt
composer_prompt.description: An instruction you can send to [Send chat message](/api-reference/send-chat-message) to have the AI fix this gap. Only a `missing-call-` gap carries one; it is an empty string on every other kind.
composer_prompt.example: Add a Google Ads conversion call to the order confirmation flow.

mapping_id.title: Mapping Id
mapping_id.description: The conversion mapping this gap is about. Absent on an `orphan-call-` gap, which is about code rather than a mapping.

conversion_type.title: Conversion Type
conversion_type.description: Conversion category the mapping names, such as `PURCHASE`. Absent on an `orphan-call-` gap.

entity_name.title: Entity Name
entity_name.description: App entity the mapping is tied to. Absent on a `disabled-` or `orphan-call-` gap, and empty on a mapping with no entity.

trigger_action.title: Trigger Action
trigger_action.description: Which write on the entity the mapping covers. Absent on a `disabled-` or `orphan-call-` gap.

send_to.title: Send To
send_to.description: The gtag `send_to` value the code should fire. Present only on a `missing-call-` gap, which is the only kind that has resolved one.

display_message.title: Display Message
display_message.description: The same problem in plain language, safe to show someone. Present only on a `missing-call-` gap.
display_message.example: Your Purchase conversion is not being recorded when an order is created.

TrackingGap.title: TrackingGap
TrackingGap.description: One problem the tracking scan found.

gaps.title: Gaps
gaps.description: Everything the scan flagged. Empty when it found nothing and when it did not run, which `skipped_reason` tells apart.

mappings_count.title: Mappings Count
mappings_count.description: How many conversion mappings the account has, enabled or not.

calls_count.title: Calls Count
calls_count.description: How many gtag conversion calls the scan found in the app's code. See the warning on this operation before reading it as zero.

is_clean.title: Is Clean
is_clean.description: Whether the scan flagged no error-severity gap (`true`) or at least one (`false`). It also reads `true` when the scan did not run at all, so check `skipped_reason` first.

enabled_mappings_count.title: Enabled Mappings Count
enabled_mappings_count.description: How many of the mappings are enabled. Absent when `skipped_reason` is set.

skipped_reason.title: Skipped Reason
skipped_reason.description: Why nothing was scanned. The value is `no_google_ads_account` when the app has no active Google Ads account, or `app_not_found`. The field is absent whenever a scan ran.

script.title: Script
script.description: The gtag snippet, wrapped in a `<script>` tag and ready to place in the app's HTML, or `null` when no goal on the account has a published tag yet. [Build Google Ads tracking fix prompt](/api-reference/build-google-ads-tracking-fix-prompt) creates the goals, and Google takes a few minutes to publish each tag, so a `null` straight after setup means you should read this again shortly.
script.example:
<script>
window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}
gtag('js', new Date());
gtag('config', 'AW-123456789', {'send_page_view': false});
</script>

TrackingScriptResponse.title: TrackingScriptResponse
TrackingScriptResponse.description: The gtag snippet that reports the app's conversions to Google Ads.

name.title: Name
name.description: Full name, or `null` when not provided.

address.title: Address
address.description: Street address, or `null` when not provided.

state.title: State
state.description: State or region, or `null` when not provided.

postal_code.title: Postal Code
postal_code.description: Postal code, or `null` when not provided.

country_code.title: Country Code
country_code.description: Two-letter country code, or `null` when not provided.

email.title: Email
email.description: Email address, or `null` when not provided.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: Phone number, or `null` when not provided.

TransactionAddress.title: TransactionAddress
TransactionAddress.description: Billing or shipping details. Each provider fills a different subset of the fields.

transaction_id.title: Transaction Id
transaction_id.description: Provider ID of the payment. For Stripe this is the charge, which can differ from the ID you looked it up by.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the payment stands. Either `succeeded`, `pending`, `failed`, `refunded`, `partially_refunded`, `pending_refund`, or `chargeback`. Other provider values come through in lowercase.

payment_type.title: Payment Type
payment_type.description: Either `one_time` or `recurring`, or an empty string when the provider doesn't say.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the payment was made, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Empty when the provider doesn't say.

currency.title: Currency
currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 code of the payment's currency, in uppercase. Defaults to `USD`.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Amount paid, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency.

fee.title: Fee
fee.description: Processing fee the provider took, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency, or `null` when none was taken, as on a declined payment.

net.title: Net
net.description: What the merchant kept after the fee, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency, or `null` when no money moved.

service_fee.title: Service Fee
service_fee.description: Application fee taken on top of the processing fee, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency, or `null` when there is none.

refunded_amount.title: Refunded Amount
refunded_amount.description: Total refunded so far, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency.

refunds.title: Refunds
refunds.description: Refunds against the payment. Empty when there are none.

method_kind.title: Method Kind
method_kind.description: Payment method type as the provider names it, for example `card`. Empty when the provider doesn't say.

method_moto.title: Method Moto
method_moto.description: `true` when the merchant entered the card for the customer, as in a phone or mail order, and `false` otherwise. Always `false` for Stripe.

card_network.title: Card Network
card_network.description: Card network, or `null` when the payment wasn't by card.

card_masked.title: Card Masked
card_masked.description: Masked card number, or `null` when the payment wasn't by card. Stripe gives only the last four digits.

card_holder.title: Card Holder
card_holder.description: Cardholder name, or `null` when the provider doesn't have it.

provider_id.title: Provider Id
provider_id.description: Processor that handled the payment. Always `stripe` for Stripe. For Wix, the processor Wix routed the payment through.

merchant_account_id.title: Merchant Account Id
merchant_account_id.description: Merchant account at the processor, or `null` when unknown. Always `null` for Stripe.

display_order_id.title: Display Order Id
display_order_id.description: Order number shown to the customer, or `null` when there is none. Always `null` for Stripe.

items.title: Items
items.description: Items bought. Empty when the provider doesn't list them.

billing.description: Billing details the customer gave, or `null` when there are none.

shipping.description: Shipping details, or `null` when the payment has none.

disputes.title: Disputes
disputes.description: Disputes against the payment. Empty when there are none.

history.title: History
history.description: Timeline of the payment, its refunds, and its disputes, newest first.

decline_reason.title: Decline Reason
decline_reason.description: Why the payment was declined, as the provider words it, or `null` when it wasn't declined.

TransactionDetails.title: TransactionDetails
TransactionDetails.description: One payment in full, as its payment provider reports it.

state.title: State
state.description: Where the dispute stands. Either `open`, `won`, `lost`, or `accepted`. An `open` dispute needs a response by `deadline`. Other provider values come through in lowercase.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Amount disputed, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency.

fee.title: Fee
fee.description: Processing fee returned with the dispute, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency. Always 0 for Stripe.

chargeback_fee.title: Chargeback Fee
chargeback_fee.description: Fee charged for the dispute, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency. Always 0 for Stripe.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: Deadline to respond to the dispute, as an ISO 8601 timestamp, or `null` when there is none.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Reason the provider gives for the dispute, or `null` when it gives none.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the dispute was opened, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Empty when the provider doesn't say.

date.title: Date
date.description: When it happened, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Empty when the provider doesn't say.

status.title: Status
status.description: Status of that step, using the same values as the matching payment, refund, or dispute status.

description.title: Description
description.description: Text from the provider, such as a decline reason or dispute reason, or `null` when there is none.
description.example: Your card has insufficient funds.

lines.title: Lines
lines.description: Money lines for this entry, such as the amount, fee, and net.

TransactionHistoryEvent.title: TransactionHistoryEvent
TransactionHistoryEvent.description: One entry in the payment's timeline.

label.title: Label
label.description: What the line is. Either `amount`, `processing_fee`, `net`, `refunded_amount`, `chargeback_amount`, or `chargeback_fee`.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Amount of the line, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency. Money that left the merchant, such as a fee, is negative.

TransactionHistoryLine.title: TransactionHistoryLine
TransactionHistoryLine.description: One money line under a timeline entry.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name of the item. Empty when the provider doesn't say.

quantity.title: Quantity
quantity.description: Number of units bought. Defaults to 1.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Price of one unit, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency, rather than the line total.

amount.title: Amount
amount.description: Amount refunded, in the smallest unit of the payment's currency.

status.title: Status
status.description: Where the refund stands. Either `succeeded`, `pending`, or `failed`. Other provider values come through in lowercase.

arn.title: Arn
arn.description: Acquirer reference number, which the customer's bank can use to trace the refund, or `null` until one is assigned. Always `null` for Stripe.

note.title: Note
note.description: Private note stored with the refund, or `null` when there is none. Always `null` for Stripe.

created_date.title: Created Date
created_date.description: When the refund was created, as an ISO 8601 timestamp. Empty when the provider doesn't say.

new_owner_user_id.title: New Owner User Id
new_owner_user_id.description: ID of the Base44 user who becomes the owner. They have to be an owner, admin, editor, or member of the app's workspace.

keep_sender_as_collaborator.title: Keep Sender As Collaborator
keep_sender_as_collaborator.description: Whether the app's current owner keeps editor access to the app after the transfer (`true`) or loses their direct access to it (`false`). An owner or admin of the workspace the app ends up in keeps access through that workspace either way. Defaults to `false`.

TransferToWorkspaceMemberRequest.title: TransferToWorkspaceMemberRequest
TransferToWorkspaceMemberRequest.description: The workspace member who becomes the app's owner.

requires_previous_run.title: Requires Previous Run
requires_previous_run.description: Whether a manual run must replay a previous run's payload, because the trigger's own payload references real in-app state a synthetic one can't stand in for. This is `false` for triggers that run without a payload, for example a scheduled trigger.

TriggerManualRunConfig.title: TriggerManualRunConfig
TriggerManualRunConfig.description:
Per-trigger behavior of the app editor's manual "Run now" experience.

``requires_previous_run``: the trigger payload references real in-app
state (entity records, agent conversations, connector events) that a
synthetic payload can't satisfy — a manual run must replay the payload
of a previous run. Triggers that run without a payload (e.g. scheduled)
set this to False.

reply.title: Reply
reply.description: The answer, as three to five sentences of plain prose with no markdown and no code blocks. It is written for a person to read, so do not parse it. An empty string means the model returned nothing, which you cannot tell apart from a genuinely empty answer, so treat it as a failed call and retry.
reply.example: Your campaign is spending its full daily budget but converting below the account average, which usually points at the landing page rather than the targeting. Check that the page loads quickly on mobile and that the offer matches the ad copy. Narrowing the geo targets to your best-performing region would also concentrate the budget.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the app.

is_unpublished.title: Is Unpublished
is_unpublished.description: Whether the app is offline. Always `true` here, because the unpublish succeeded.

last_deployed_at.title: Last Deployed At
last_deployed_at.description: Time the app was last published, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format. Unpublishing doesn't change it.

data.title: Data
data.description: Custom `User` fields to set on the invitation, as field names and values.

anchor.description: The thread's new pin. It replaces the old one in full.

screenshot_file_uri.title: Screenshot File Uri
screenshot_file_uri.description: `file_uri` of a screenshot uploaded to this app with [Upload app file](/api-reference/upload-app-file) and `visibility` set to `private`. Starts with `mp/private/` followed by the app's ID.

UpdateAnchorPayload.title: UpdateAnchorPayload
UpdateAnchorPayload.description: A thread's new pin and screenshot.

name.title: Name
name.description: New name, 1 to 100 characters.

position.title: Position
position.description: New sort key among folders. Lower values come first.

color.title: Color
color.description: New color, up to 32 characters, or `null` to clear it.

icon.title: Icon
icon.description: New icon name, up to 64 characters, or `null` to clear it.

default_credit_limit.title: Default Credit Limit
default_credit_limit.description: Most credits each member without their own limit can use in the workspace each month, at least 1. `null`, or leaving it out, removes the default.

UpdateDefaultCreditLimitRequest.title: UpdateDefaultCreditLimitRequest
UpdateDefaultCreditLimitRequest.description: The workspace's default member credit limit.

sender_name.title: Sender Name
sender_name.description: Name recipients see in the From line. Required, so resend the current value to keep it.

from_email.title: From Email
from_email.description: Address mail is sent from. Its domain has to be one the app already has set up for email. Required, so resend the current value to keep it.

UpdateEmailDomainRequest.title: UpdateEmailDomainRequest
UpdateEmailDomainRequest.description: Request to update email domain configuration.

from_email.title: From Email
from_email.description: The address now in use, lower-cased.

domain.title: Domain
domain.description: The domain this configuration belongs to.

configuration_status.title: Configuration Status
configuration_status.description: Where setup stands. Updating these fields doesn't change it. Only `active` sends mail. The `pending_` values mean setup is still in progress, and the `failed_` values mean it stopped and you can start it again with [Retry email domain setup](/api-reference/retry-email-domain-setup).

UpdateEmailDomainResponse.title: UpdateEmailDomainResponse
UpdateEmailDomainResponse.description: Response for updating email domain configuration.

entity_schema.title: Entity Schema
entity_schema.description: The entity's full [JSON Schema](/developers/backend/resources/entities/entity-schemas), replacing the stored one. Needs `"type": "object"` and a `properties` object, plus any `required` fields and [row-level security rules](/developers/backend/resources/entities/security) under `rls`.

name.title: Name
name.description: New name for the test.

goal.title: Goal
goal.description: New goal for the test, in plain language.
goal.example: Sign up, create a project called Launch, and check that it appears on the dashboard.

role.title: Role
role.description: Role to run the test as. Send `null` to clear it, so Base44 picks one from the name or goal again.

name.title: Name
name.description: New name, up to 100 characters. An identity-provider group's name can't change.

description.title: Description
description.description: New description, up to 500 characters. An empty string clears it.
description.example: Brand and marketing designers

role.title: Role
role.description: New role: `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`, or `no_access`. Send `null` to clear it so the group grants no role, or leave it out to keep it.

credit_limit.title: Credit Limit
credit_limit.description: Most credits the member can use in the workspace each month, at least 1. `null`, or leaving it out, removes their own limit, so the workspace default applies.

role.description: The member's new role. `admin` needs the Business plan or higher.

content.title: Content
content.description: The post text to save, replacing whatever the post held before. Sanitized before it is stored, so XML or HTML tags, code fences, and lines starting `system:`, `assistant:`, or `user:` are removed.
content.example: Still tracking leads in a spreadsheet? I built the thing I wanted instead.

active.title: Active
active.description: Whether the price is active. Leave it out to keep the current value. Sending `null` has the same effect. Defaults to `null`.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Metadata to store, as string key-value pairs. [Stripe's metadata rules](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) limit it to 50 keys, 40 characters per key, and 500 characters per value. Defaults to `null`. Leave it out to keep the current value. Sending `null` has the same effect.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: New internal price label. Leave it out to keep the current value. Sending `null` has the same effect. Defaults to `null`.

UpdatePriceRequest.title: UpdatePriceRequest
UpdatePriceRequest.description: Request to update a Stripe price.

name.title: Name
name.description: New product name. Leave it out to keep the current value. Sending `null` has the same effect. Defaults to `null`.

description.title: Description
description.description: New product description. Leave it out to keep the current value. Sending `null` has the same effect. Defaults to `null`.
description.example: Access to weekly classes.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Metadata to store, as string key-value pairs. [Stripe's metadata rules](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) limit it to 50 keys, 40 characters per key, and 500 characters per value. Defaults to `null`. Leave it out to keep the current value. Sending `null` has the same effect.

active.title: Active
active.description: Whether the product is active. Leave it out to keep the current value. Sending `null` has the same effect. Defaults to `null`.

UpdateProductRequest.title: UpdateProductRequest
UpdateProductRequest.description: Request to update a Stripe product.

role.title: Role
role.description: App role the group's members get, one of the roles defined on the app's User entity. Send `null`, or leave `role` out, to stop assigning a role, so members get the default `user` role.

role.title: Role
role.description: App role the share now gives the group's members, or `null` when it assigns none.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: New slug, 3 to 50 characters of letters, numbers, and hyphens that starts and ends with a letter or number. It has to be unused by any other app and not a reserved name, and it's lowercased before it's saved. Send `null` to reset it to the slug Base44 generates from the app's name and ID.

test_mode.title: Test Mode
test_mode.description: Whether to switch the checkout to test mode (`true`) or live (`false`).

target_url.title: Target Url
target_url.description: New public HTTPS URL that receives the events.

events.title: Events
events.description: New set of events to receive. One or more of `message.created` and `message.completed`.

description.title: Description
description.description: New label for the webhook, or `null` to remove it.
description.example: CRM sync

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: `true` turns the webhook back on and resets `consecutive_failures`. `false` turns it off.

signing.title: Signing
signing.description: `rotate` generates a new signing secret and returns it once in `secret`. `disable` removes the secret, so deliveries are no longer signed.

name.title: Name
name.description: New name. Leave it out to keep the current one. Must be unique among the app's workflows that are not archived, so renaming to one another live workflow already uses is rejected.

description.title: Description
description.description: New description. Leave it out to keep the current one.
description.example: Sends an email whenever a User record is created.

definition.title: Definition
definition.description: New definition. Leave it out to keep the current one. One that differs from the current definition is saved as a new immutable version, and the workflow runs it from then on. An invalid definition is rejected with the validation errors, and nothing is saved.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.description: New trigger. Leave it out to keep the current one. See [Triggers](/developers/references/apps-api/sections/workflows#triggers) for its shape.

change_summary.title: Change Summary
change_summary.description: Note describing this change, kept in the version history. This is only recorded when `definition` actually changes, since that's what creates the version it's attached to.
change_summary.example: Send to the ops alias instead

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`. An update that doesn't happen returns an error instead.

data.title: Data
data.description: The invitation's custom `User` fields after the update, limited by the `User` entity's field-level read rules.

UpdatedInvitation.title: UpdatedInvitation
UpdatedInvitation.description: Doc-only: the handler returns a plain dict with exactly these keys.

file_uri.title: File Uri
file_uri.description: Storage URI of the file. `mp/public/` or `mp/private/` shows its visibility.

url.title: Url
url.description: Link to the file. For a public file it's permanent and anyone with it can open the file. For a private file it's a signed link that stops working after `expires_in` seconds.

UploadedAppFile.title: UploadedAppFile
UploadedAppFile.description: Doc-only: the handler returns a plain dict with exactly these keys.

source_path.title: Source Path
source_path.description: Path visitors request, starting with `/` and carrying no query string or fragment. Base44 strips a trailing slash and decodes percent-escapes before storing it, so `/old/` and `/%6Fld` are the same rule.

target_path.title: Target Path
target_path.description: Where to send the visitor. Either an internal path starting with `/`, normalized the same way as `source_path`, or an absolute `https://` URL on another site, kept as you sent it. Send it without a query string or fragment. The visitor's own query string is carried over to the destination, so `/old?utm=x` lands on `/new?utm=x`.

match_type.description: Use `single` to redirect that exact path, or `prefix` to redirect it and everything under it, keeping the remainder of the path. Defaults to `single`, so omitting it on an update turns an existing `prefix` rule into a `single` one and its child paths stop redirecting.

id.title: Id
id.description: ID of the redirect. Pass it as `redirect_id` to [Update URL redirect](/api-reference/update-url-redirect) and [Delete URL redirect](/api-reference/delete-url-redirect).

source_path.title: Source Path
source_path.description: The path visitors request, normalized with no trailing slash and percent-escapes decoded.

target_path.title: Target Path
target_path.description: Where the visitor is sent. Either an internal path, normalized the same way as `source_path`, or an absolute `https://` URL on another site, kept exactly as you sent it.

match_type.description: How the rule matches. A `single` rule redirects that exact path, and a `prefix` rule redirects it and everything under it, keeping the remainder of the path.

retention_days.title: Retention Days
retention_days.description: How many days of history Base44 keeps, or `null` unless `state` is `enabled`.

history_available_since.title: History Available Since
history_available_since.description: The earliest moment you can restore to, as a UTC timestamp in ISO 8601 format with a `Z` suffix, when history was paused while the workspace was on a plan without it. status.description: Where the invoice stands. `FAILED` is an invoice whose charge did not go through, and `PENDING` is one Base44 is still collecting.

billing_type.title: Billing Type
billing_type.description: Which billing run produced the invoice. `weekly` is the recurring charge, `reconciliation` trues up a period, `threshold` is spend-triggered, `google_monthly` mirrors an invoice Google issued, and `adjustment` is a manual correction.

period_start.title: Period Start
period_start.description: First day of the spend the invoice covers, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

period_end.title: Period End
period_end.description: Last day of the spend the invoice covers, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

amount_micros.title: Amount Micros
amount_micros.description: Amount owed in micros of `currency_code`, so `43500000` is 43.50.

currency_code.title: Currency Code
currency_code.description: Currency of `amount_micros` as a three-letter ISO 4217 code.

failed_at.title: Failed At
failed_at.description: When the charge last failed, or `null` on an invoice that has not been attempted or is still pending.

WorkspaceDebtInvoice.title: WorkspaceDebtInvoice
WorkspaceDebtInvoice.description: The unpaid Google Ads invoice behind a workspace's billing hold.

brand.title: Brand
brand.description: Card brand, as the payment provider reports it. Empty when the provider did not return one.

last4.title: Last4
last4.description: Last four digits of the card. Empty when the provider did not return them.

WorkspaceDebtPaymentMethod.title: WorkspaceDebtPaymentMethod
WorkspaceDebtPaymentMethod.description: The card the workspace has on file.

state.title: State
state.description: What can be done about the balance. `no_workspace_debt` means nothing is held. `payable` means there is an invoice and a usable card. `requires_payment_method` and `requires_payment_refresh` both mean a card is needed. `pending_payment` means a charge is already in flight. `paid_recovery_incomplete` means the invoice is paid but the account is still held. `unavailable` means the balance cannot be settled right now, including when `stripe_unavailable` is `true`. `no_debt` and `not_recoverable` mean the account has no settleable balance.

account_id.title: Account Id
account_id.description: ID of the Google Ads account the balance belongs to, or `null` when `state` is `no_workspace_debt`.

app_id.title: App Id
app_id.description: ID of the app that owns the held account, which is not necessarily the app in the path. The value is `null` when `state` is `no_workspace_debt`.

account_status.title: Account Status
account_status.description: Status of the held Google Ads account, or `null` when `state` is `no_workspace_debt`.

block_reason.title: Block Reason
block_reason.description: Why the account is held, or `null` when it is not held or the reason is unrecorded.

charge_trigger_mode.title: Charge Trigger Mode
charge_trigger_mode.description: How the account is billed. `cadence` is the recurring charge and `threshold` is spend-triggered. The value is `null` when `state` is `no_workspace_debt`.

recoverable.title: Recoverable
recoverable.description: Whether the account is in a state Base44 can settle at all (`true`) or not (`false`).

can_pay_now.title: Can Pay Now
can_pay_now.description: Whether there is a chargeable invoice and a usable card, so settling would go through now (`true`) or not (`false`).

requires_payment_method.title: Requires Payment Method
requires_payment_method.description: Whether a card has to be added or replaced before the balance can be settled (`true`) or not (`false`).

stripe_unavailable.title: Stripe Unavailable
stripe_unavailable.description: Whether Base44 could not reach the payment provider (`true`) or reached it fine (`false`). When it is `true` the card check failed closed, so `payment_method` reads `null` and `can_pay_now` reads `false` because the check failed, not because the card is missing. Retry rather than telling someone to add a card.

payment_method.description: The card on file, or `null` when the workspace has none and when the payment provider could not be reached.

invoice.description: The unpaid invoice behind the hold, or `null` when there is none to settle and when the latest one is already paid.

WorkspaceDebtSummary.title: WorkspaceDebtSummary
WorkspaceDebtSummary.description: Whether the workspace owes anything for Google Ads spend.

unresolved_count.title: Unresolved Count
unresolved_count.description: Members your identity provider sent who don't have a Base44 account in the workspace yet. Always `0` for a `custom` group.

email.title: Email

full_name.title: Full Name
full_name.description: Full name, or `null` when there isn't one, as for an invitee without a Base44 account.

user_id.title: User Id
user_id.description: ID of the person's Base44 account, or `null` for an invitee without one.

role.title: Role
role.description: Role in the workspace: `owner`, `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`, or `guest`.

status.title: Status

access_state.title: Access State

invitation_expires_at.title: Invitation Expires At
invitation_expires_at.description: When a pending invitation expires, in ISO 8601 UTC without an offset. `null` for members who joined.

credits_used.title: Credits Used
credits_used.description: Credits the member used in the workspace this month. `null` on other members' rows when you aren't an owner or admin.

credit_limit.title: Credit Limit

apps_owned.title: Apps Owned

agents_owned.title: Agents Owned
agents_owned.description: Agents the member owns in the workspace.

agents_shared.title: Agents Shared

last_seen.title: Last Seen

recommended_daily_budget_micros.title: Recommended Daily Budget Micros
recommended_daily_budget_micros.description: The daily budget the suggestion showed, in micros. This confirms what you saw rather than choosing an amount: if Google's current figure differs, the call is rejected with a 409 and nothing changes.

_ApplyBudgetRecommendationRequest.title: ApplyBudgetRecommendation
_ApplyBudgetRecommendationRequest.description:
Request shape for the user-approved budget-recommendation apply.

`recommendation_resource_name` is Google's `customers/.../recommendations/...`
id (used for idempotency + server-side re-resolution). The route re-fetches
the recommendation from Google and applies Google's own recommended amount
for the recommendation's target campaign, so the request body amount is
advisory only (what the user saw) and a tampered value can't change what is
applied. It is still bounds-checked by update_campaign_budget.

success.title: Success
success.description: Always `true`. A removal that doesn't happen returns an error instead.
